- The `warlock-inspect` topic — the report the section is built from.
- The `warlock-check` topic — the verify command the section points at.
- The `warlock-conventions` topic — the conventions listed in the section.


## warlock-board  `@warlock.js/core/warlock-board/SKILL.md`

---
name: warlock-board
description: 'Coordinate two coding agents (an implementer and a reviewer) through `warlock board`: work items with a review state machine (todo, in-progress, ready-for-review, changes-requested, approved, blocked), append-only numbered messages per recipient in the git-ignored `.warlock/board/`, `VERDICT: APPROVED` / `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED` lines that move the item, and a blocking `watch` with a timeout; `--json` on every action. Triggers: `warlock board`, `board init`, `board add`, `board status`, `board send`, `board watch`, `--verdict`, `WARLOCK_AGENT`, `.warlock/board`, `to-reviewer/`, `initBoard`, `addBoardItem`, `moveBoardItem`, `sendBoardMessage`, `watchBoard`, `readBoardStatus`, `WL7401`, `WL7402`, `WL7403`, `WL7404`; "hand this to the reviewer agent", "wait for the review", "two agents working together", "request changes", "approve the item". Skip: verifying the code itself — the `warlock-check` topic; app facts — the `warlock-inspect` topic.'
---

# Warlock — `warlock board`

A shared folder of plain files two agents use to hand work back and forth: **items** move through review states, **messages** are appended to the other agent's inbox, and `watch` blocks until something new arrives. Set `WARLOCK_AGENT` to your agent name so `--from` / `--by` default to it.

```bash
export WARLOCK_AGENT=implementer
npx warlock board init
npx warlock board add "Add the orders module" --assignee implementer --reviewer reviewer --json
npx warlock board status --json
```

## The loop

Implementer:

```bash
npx warlock board status 1 in-progress
# write the code; loop on `npx warlock check --changed --json` until it is clean
npx warlock board status 1 ready-for-review --note "check passes"
npx warlock board send reviewer "Orders module ready" --item 1 --body @handoff.md
npx warlock board watch implementer --timeout 1800 --json   # blocks for the verdict
```

Reviewer (`WARLOCK_AGENT=reviewer`):

```bash
npx warlock board watch reviewer --timeout 1800 --json
# review the diff, run `npx warlock check --changed --json`
npx warlock board send implementer "Review of orders" --item 1 --verdict changes-requested --body @review.md
# or, when it is right:
npx warlock board send implementer "Approved" --item 1 --verdict approved
```

On `changes-requested` the implementer moves the item back with `status 1 in-progress`, fixes, moves it to `ready-for-review` and sends a new message. The loop ends on `approved`.

## States

| From                | Allowed next                                   |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `todo`              | `in-progress`, `blocked`                       |
| `in-progress`       | `ready-for-review`, `blocked`, `todo`          |
| `ready-for-review`  | `approved`, `changes-requested`, `in-progress` |
| `changes-requested` | `in-progress`, `blocked`                       |
| `approved`          | `in-progress` (reopen)                         |
| `blocked`           | `todo`, `in-progress`                          |

Anything else fails with `WL7403`, and the message lists the allowed states. `npx warlock board status <id> --json` returns `{ item, next }`.

## Reading what `watch` returns

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "timedOut": false,
  "agent": "implementer",
  "cursor": 3,
  "messages": [
    {
      "number": 3,
      "file": ".warlock/board/to-implementer/0003-review-of-orders.md",
      "from": "reviewer",
      "to": "implementer",
      "item": 1,
      "subject": "Review of orders",
      "at": "2026-10-17T09:12:44.512Z",
      "body": "Wrap the list response in OrderResource.",
      "verdict": "changes-requested"
    }
  ]
}
```

- Every unread message comes back at once, oldest first, and the cursor moves past them. `--since 0` replays the inbox.
- Timeout: exit code **3** and `{ "ok": false, "code": "WL7404", "timedOut": true }`. Just run `watch` again.
- A message file ends with exactly `VERDICT: APPROVED` or `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED` when it carries a verdict.

## From code

```ts
import {
  initBoard,
  addBoardItem,
  moveBoardItem,
  sendBoardMessage,
  watchBoard,
} from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

initBoard();
const item = addBoardItem({
  title: "Add the orders module",
  assignee: "implementer",
  reviewer: "reviewer",
});
moveBoardItem(item.id, "in-progress", { by: "implementer" });
moveBoardItem(item.id, "ready-for-review", { by: "implementer" });
sendBoardMessage({
  to: "reviewer",
  from: "implementer",
  subject: "Ready",
  item: item.id,
  body: "See the diff.",
});

const { messages } = await watchBoard({ agent: "implementer", timeoutMs: 30 * 60_000 });
```

## Gotchas

- Run `init` first; every other action fails with `WL7401` until the board exists. `init` git-ignores `.warlock/board/`.
- Messages are append-only and numbered per inbox; never edit or delete one by hand — send a new message.
- A verdict naming an item moves it; if the item is not in `ready-for-review`, the send fails with `WL7403` and no message is written.
- Agent names: lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
- `@mongez/agent-kit` lives outside this repository; it integrates by calling these commands.

## See also

- The `warlock-check` topic — the verify command both agents loop on.
- The `warlock-inspect` topic — the app's facts as JSON before you change it.


## warlock-check  `@warlock.js/core/warlock-check/SKILL.md`

---
name: warlock-check
description: 'Verify a change with one command: `warlock check [--changed] [--json]` runs an incremental typecheck, the app''s ESLint/oxlint, the tests affected by the change and framework convention checks, and reports one JSON object per problem `{ code, category, severity, source, file, line, column, message, hint, skill, docs, rule }` with exit 1 for problems in your code and 2 for problems with this machine (missing Redis/DB, busy port, Node version, missing tool). Also `warlock typecheck [--changed]`, `warlock explain <CODE>` and the stable `WL` error codes (`errorCodeOf`, `WarlockError`). Triggers: `warlock check`, `warlock typecheck`, `warlock explain`, `--changed`, `--base`, `runCheck`, `runTypecheck`, `CHECK_EXIT_CODES`, `ToolingProblem`, `WL7101`, `WL8003`, `errorCodeOf`, `explainErrorCode`, `WarlockError`, "verify my change", "run the checks", "is this failure my code or the machine", "what does WL3001 mean", "typecheck only changed files". Skip: app diagnostics at boot — the `warlock-doctor` topic; reading the app''s routes/models — the `warlock-inspect` topic; writing tests — the `test-http` / `test-service` topics.'
---

# Warlock — `warlock check`, `typecheck`, `explain`

Run `warlock check` after every change and loop on it until it exits 0.

```bash
npx warlock check --changed --json    # inner loop: only what changed vs HEAD (+ untracked)
npx warlock check --base main         # what changed since the branch left main
npx warlock check                     # everything, before you finish
npx warlock check --skip tests        # steps: environment, typecheck, lint, tests, conventions
```

## Exit codes

| Exit | Meaning                                                 | What to do                                                                                                      |
| ---- | ------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`  | no errors (warnings allowed)                            | done                                                                                                            |
| `1`  | problems **in your code**                               | fix each problem at `file:line:column`                                                                          |
| `2`  | a problem with **this machine** — the run is incomplete | fix the environment (start Redis/DB, free the port, switch Node, install the tool); do **not** edit code for it |

`2` wins when both kinds exist. Each problem's `category` (`code` / `environment`) says the same per problem.

## One problem

```json
{
  "code": "WL8003",
  "category": "environment",
  "severity": "error",
  "source": "environment",
  "file": "src/app/posts/publish.spec.ts",
  "line": null,
  "column": null,
  "message": "Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379",
  "hint": "Start the service named in the message (database, Redis, ...) or point the config at a running one.",
  "skill": "warlock-check",
  "docs": "https://warlock.js.org/v/latest/core/cli/error-codes/#wl8003",
  "rule": "publish caches the post"
}
```

```bash
npx warlock check --changed --json > check.json; code=$?
jq -r '.problems[] | "\(.file // "-"):\(.line // 0) \(.code) \(.message)\n  → \(.hint)"' check.json
[ "$code" = 2 ] && echo "environment problem — fix the machine, not the code"
```

| Code                | Problem                                                                                                       |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WL7101`            | type error (`rule` = `TS2322`, …)                                                                             |
| `WL7102`            | tsconfig missing/invalid                                                                                      |
| `WL7201` / `WL7202` | lint error / warning (`rule` = the rule id)                                                                   |
| `WL7301` / `WL7302` | a test failed / a test file failed to load                                                                    |
| `WL9001`            | imports an auto-loaded file (`routes.ts`, `main.ts`, `worker.ts`, `events/*`)                                 |
| `WL9002`            | relative import ends in `.js`                                                                                 |
| `WL9003`            | relative import into another `src/app/<module>` — use `app/<module>/...`                                      |
| `WL9004`            | `experimentalDecorators: true` in tsconfig                                                                    |
| `WL9005`            | `request.all()` passed to a query, a service or `inApp()` — use `request.validated()`                         |
| `WL9006`            | POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route with no auth middleware and no `public: true`                                     |
| `WL9007`            | redirect / `navigateTo()` / `<Link to>` target from request input without `safeRedirect()`                    |
| `WL9008`            | raw email, credential or request body in a log call                                                           |
| `WL9009`            | regex with `*` / `+` / `{n,}` run on request input                                                            |
| `WL9010`–`WL9012`   | warnings: `await log.*()`, a second controller in a file, a `kind` discriminator                              |
| `WL8001`–`WL8007`   | this machine: Node version, missing tool, unreachable service, busy port, esbuild binary, git, tool crash/OOM |

## `warlock typecheck`

```bash
npx warlock typecheck                 # whole program, incremental (.warlock/cache/typecheck.tsbuildinfo)
npx warlock typecheck --changed       # changed files + the files importing them
npx warlock typecheck --json --project tsconfig.app.json
```

`--changed` checks the changed files and their direct importers only; a full run (cheap after the first, it is incremental) catches anything further away.

## `warlock explain`

```bash
npx warlock explain WL3001          # title, fix, skill, docs link
npx warlock explain WL3001 --json   # the registry entry
npx warlock explain                 # every code
```

## Error codes in code

Framework errors carry a stable `code`; read any thrown value with `errorCodeOf()` (it also maps `ECONNREFUSED` → `WL8003`, `EADDRINUSE` / `PortInUseError` → `WL8004`, and follows `cause`):

```ts
import { errorCodeOf, explainErrorCode, router, WarlockError } from "@warlock.js/core";

try {
  router.getRoute("posts.show", {});
} catch (error) {
  const code = errorCodeOf(error); // "WL3003" (unknown route name) or "WL3004" (missing param)
  console.error(code, code && explainErrorCode(code)?.fix);
}

// Throw a coded framework error from a connector or plugin:
throw new WarlockError("WL2003", "search connector failed to boot: SEARCH_URL is not set");
```

## From code

```ts
import { CHECK_EXIT_CODES, runCheck, runTypecheck } from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

const report = await runCheck({ changed: true });

if (report.exitCode === CHECK_EXIT_CODES.environment) {
  // tell the user which service/tool is missing; don't touch the code
}

const types = runTypecheck({ files: ["src/app/posts/services/publish.service.ts"] });
```

## Gotchas

- `check` boots nothing — no config, no connection, no port — so it runs the same with or without services; only tests that need them fail, and those report `WL8003`/`WL8004`.
- Lint defaults to Oxlint (an app-root config + the app-installed package). No Oxlint config skips lint. A missing package reports `WL8002`. ESLint requires `--lint eslint` (or `runCheck({ lint: "eslint" })`); its flat config alone never enables it. This deprecated selection prints one warning on stderr and is removed in 5.34.0.
- Tests use the app's own vitest (`vitest run`, or `vitest related <files> --run` with `--changed`). Test files without vitest installed → `WL8002`.
- The typecheck runs in a child `warlock typecheck` process; running out of memory is reported as `WL8007` instead of ending the run.
- The convention checks are the framework's own and run the same with ESLint, Oxlint or no linter. A deliberate exception gets `// warlock-check-ignore WL9006 -- why` on the problem's line or the line above (no code = every code on that line).

## See also

- `report-framework-issue.md` — confirm a framework bug or missing capability, collect `warlock issue` output, and get the user's approval before filing.
- The `warlock-doctor` topic — boot-time diagnostics; `doctor --json` uses the same codes and fields.
- The `warlock-inspect` topic — the app's routes, models and config as JSON.
- The `warlock-conventions` topic — the rules behind `WL9001`–`WL9012`, with the fix for each.

Migrate lint and format tooling with
`npx warlock upgrade --from 5.32 --to 5.33.0 --dry-run`, then remove `--dry-run`
and work through the manual-review list. Use `--lint=oxc` for new apps.


## warlock-conventions  `@warlock.js/core/warlock-conventions/SKILL.md`

---
name: warlock-conventions
description: 'Framework-wide invariants for projects built on @warlock.js/core — module layout, canonical imports, layered flow, file naming, and the non-negotiable rules every other warlock skill assumes. Triggers: `src/app/<module>`, `routes.ts`, `main.ts`, `Request<TSchema>`, `RequestHandler`, `GuardedRequestHandler`, `app/<module>/...`; "where do files go in this project", "canonical Warlock imports", "module layout rules", "controller-service-repository layering"; typical import `import { router, type RequestHandler } from "@warlock.js/core"`. Skip: scaffold a new module — the `create-module` topic; route shape — the `register-route` topic; controller shape — the `create-controller` topic; competing patterns: `express` ad-hoc layouts, `@nestjs/common` decorator-driven structure.'
---

# Warlock — framework-wide conventions

This skill is the foundation. Every other warlock skill (`register-route`, `create-controller`, `send-response`, …) assumes you know these rules. Don't repeat them in task skills — link here instead.

## Always-true facts

1. **Every feature lives in `src/app/<module>/`.** No exceptions. A module is a folder with the standard subfolders (`controllers/`, `services/`, `models/`, `repositories/`, `resources/`, `schema/`, `routes.ts`, `main.ts`). Generate with `warlock generate.module <name>`.
2. **Several files are auto-loaded — never `import` them.** The dev-server file watcher and the production builder categorize these as "special" and load them on boot.
   - `src/app/<module>/routes.ts` — route declarations
   - `src/app/<module>/main.ts` — per-module one-time setup
   - `src/app/<module>/worker.ts` — worker-only setup (queue job definitions,
     `scheduler.addJob(...)`, `scheduler.start()`); loaded only for the
     `worker` role, and always loaded by `warlock dev`
   - `src/app/main.ts` — **project-level** one-time application setup (global hooks and other app initialization; connector instances belong in `warlock.config.ts > connectors`)
   - `src/app/<module>/events/*.ts(x)` — **any** `.ts(x)` file inside the `events/` folder (the `*.event.ts` suffix is convention, not a framework requirement)
   - `src/app/<module>/utils/locales.ts` — module translations via `groupedTranslations(...)`
   - `src/config/*.ts(x)` — subsystem config files
3. **Canonical imports — each package owns its surface.** `@warlock.js/core` does **NOT** re-export `v`/`Infer` or Cascade types. Import from the home package:
   - `v`, `Infer` → `@warlock.js/seal`
   - `Model`, `RegisterModel`, `Migration`, `onceConnected` → `@warlock.js/cascade`
   - `router`, `RequestHandler`, `Request`, `Response`, `useCase`, `RepositoryManager`, `Resource`, `defineResource`, `Restful`, `defineConfig`, `config`, `env`, `Application`, `BaseConnector`, `connectorsManager`, `storage`, `Mail`, `sendMail`, `hashPassword`, `verifyPassword`, `encrypt`, `decrypt`, `hmacHash`, `measure`, `retry`, `t`, `command`, `CLICommand` → `@warlock.js/core`
   - `cache` → `@warlock.js/cache`
   - `log` → `@warlock.js/logger`
   - `authMiddleware`, `authService` → `@warlock.js/auth`
   - `ai`, `OpenAISDK`, etc. → `@warlock.js/ai*`
4. **Layered flow is one-way.** `routes.ts → controllers → services → repositories → models`. Resources cut across as the wire mapper. Never invert — repositories don't call services, services don't call controllers.
5. **Controllers are thin.** Pull input from `request`, call a service or use-case, return via `response.<helper>()`. No business logic. No transactions. No external API calls.
6. **Resources are output-only.** Map model fields to wire fields and nothing else. Reconciliation, hydration, and computed side-effects belong in services or model accessors — never in resources.
7. **No per-action `*.request.ts` files.** Schema files export **both** the value and the inferred type from one place; controllers consume both directly and type themselves as `RequestHandler<Request<TSchema>>` (or `GuardedRequestHandler<TSchema>` for auth'd routes). Source pattern:

   ```ts title="src/app/<module>/schema/create-<thing>.schema.ts"
   import { v, type Infer } from "@warlock.js/seal";

   export const createThingSchema = v.object({/* … */});
   export type CreateThingSchema = Infer<typeof createThingSchema>;
   ```

   ```ts title="src/app/<module>/controllers/create-<thing>.controller.ts"
   import { type GuardedRequestHandler } from "app/auth/requests/guarded.request";
   import { type CreateThingSchema, createThingSchema } from "../schema/create-thing.schema";
   import { createThingService } from "../services/create-thing.service";

   export const createThingController: GuardedRequestHandler<CreateThingSchema> = async ({
     request,
     response,
   }) => {
     const thing = await createThingService(request.validated());
     return response.success({ thing });
   };

   createThingController.validation = { schema: createThingSchema };
   ```

8. **Model getters beat `.get<T>("field")`.** Add a typed getter on the model rather than scattering `.get<string>("name")` casts across call sites.

## Module layout (the standard subfolders)

```
src/app/<module>/
  controllers/              thin request handlers
  services/                 stateless business logic
  models/<entity>/          Cascade model + migrations
  repositories/             RepositoryManager subclasses
  resources/                Resource subclasses (output mapping)
  schema/                   seal schemas (`<action>.schema.ts`) — value + type from one file
  events/                   any `*.ts(x)` file here is auto-loaded
  types/                    `.type.ts` files for module-internal types
  utils/                    module-private helpers (`utils/locales.ts` is auto-loaded)
  seeds/                    seed data for `warlock seed`
  routes.ts                 ← auto-loaded
  main.ts                   ← auto-loaded once, one-time setup
  worker.ts                 ← auto-loaded for the worker role only
```

Some older modules still have a `validation/` folder instead of `schema/` — historical drift. The framework treats them as plain folders either way; the generator emits to `schema/`.

## File naming (project-wide)

| Suffix           | Role                                                                                         | Example                                  |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `.controller.ts` | HTTP handler                                                                                 | `create-product.controller.ts`           |
| `.service.ts`    | Stateless business logic                                                                     | `create-product.service.ts`              |
| `.usecase.ts`    | `useCase()` pipeline                                                                         | `login.usecase.ts`                       |
| `.model.ts`      | Cascade model class                                                                          | `product.model.ts`                       |
| `.repository.ts` | `RepositoryManager` subclass                                                                 | `products.repository.ts`                 |
| `.resource.ts`   | `Resource` subclass                                                                          | `product.resource.ts`                    |
| `.schema.ts`     | seal validation schema + its inferred `<Name>Schema` type from the same file                 | `create-product.schema.ts`               |
| `.type.ts`       | data shape (TypeScript `type`)                                                               | `cart-state.type.ts`                     |
| `.contract.ts`   | interface (TypeScript `interface`)                                                           | `model.contract.ts`                      |
| `.event.ts`      | event listener registrations (any `.ts(x)` inside `events/` works; the suffix is convention) | `audit.event.ts`                         |
| `.migration.ts`  | Cascade migration                                                                            | `2026_05_22_120000_product.migration.ts` |
| `.seed.ts`       | seed data                                                                                    | `products.seed.ts`                       |

Filenames are kebab-case. Class names are PascalCase. Function names are camelCase. Table/collection names are snake_case (plural).

## Path aliases

The scaffolded `tsconfig.json` defines:

```jsonc
{
  "paths": {
    "app/*": ["./src/app/*"],
  },
}
```

Use `app/<module>/...` when crossing module boundaries:

```ts
// ✅ from src/app/orders/services/place-order.service.ts
import { Product } from "app/products/models/product";

// ❌ deep relative path
import { Product } from "../../../products/models/product";
```

Within the same module, use relative paths (`./`, `../`).

## Type augmentations

`src/typings.d.ts` is the project's module-augmentation file. It ships with the scaffold, is listed explicitly in `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, and is where application-wide `declare module "@warlock.js/core"` blocks live — `RequestLocals` and `RequestUser` are already there as empty interfaces. Keep its trailing `export {}` (without it the block declares an ambient module and erases the framework's real typings) and keep the augmented declarations as `interface`, the one sanctioned exception to this project's prefer-`type` rule, since declaration merging is interface-only. See the `use-request-locals` topic.

## Decorators

Cascade uses `@RegisterModel()` for the model registry and `@BelongsTo` / `@HasMany` / `@MorphTo` for relations. The scaffolded `tsconfig.json` has `"experimentalDecorators": false` — these are native Stage-3 decorators, not legacy. Never set that flag to `true`; see the `lower-stage3-decorators` topic.

## What `warlock check` enforces

`npx warlock check` (the `warlock-check` topic) reports these with a stable code. They run the same whatever linter the app uses.

| Code     | Rule                                                                                              |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `WL9001` | never import an auto-loaded file (fact 2)                                                         |
| `WL9002` | no `.js` extension on a relative import                                                           |
| `WL9003` | cross-module imports use `app/<module>/...` (see Path aliases)                                    |
| `WL9004` | no `"experimentalDecorators": true`                                                               |
| `WL9005` | queries, services and `inApp()` get `request.validated()`, never `request.all()`                  |
| `WL9006` | every POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE route is guarded or says `public: true`                               |
| `WL9007` | redirect and link targets from request input go through `safeRedirect()` / `safeRedirectTarget()` |
| `WL9008` | no raw email, credential or request body in a log call                                            |
| `WL9009` | regexes run on request input have bounded quantifiers                                             |
| `WL9010` | warning: no `await` on `log.info()` and its siblings                                              |
| `WL9011` | warning: one controller per file                                                                  |
| `WL9012` | warning: a tagged union's discriminator is `type`, not `kind`                                     |

### `WL9005` — validated input only

`request.all()` hands every client-sent field to whatever receives it (mass assignment). Declare a schema and pass what it accepted:

```ts
import { type RequestHandler } from "@warlock.js/core";
import { v } from "@warlock.js/seal";

const createPostSchema = v.object({ title: v.string(), body: v.string() });

async function createPostService(input: { title: string; body: string }) {
  return { id: 1, ...input };
}

export const createPostController: RequestHandler = async ({ request, response }) => {
  const post = await createPostService(request.validated());
  return response.successCreate({ post });
};

createPostController.validation = { schema: createPostSchema };
```

### `WL9006` — guarded or public

```ts
import { authMiddleware } from "@warlock.js/auth";
import { router, type RequestHandler } from "@warlock.js/core";

const createPostController: RequestHandler = async ({ response }) => response.successCreate({});
const contactController: RequestHandler = async ({ response }) => response.success({ sent: true });

router.post("/posts", createPostController, { middleware: [authMiddleware("user")] });

// Intentionally open: say so.
router.post("/contact", contactController, { public: true });
```

A route inside `guarded(() => …)` or `router.group({ middleware: [authMiddleware()] }, …)` is guarded. A middleware counts as a guard when its name contains `auth` or `guard`, or when it is a constant initialised with `markAuthGuard()` in the same file. `warlock dev` warns about the same routes at runtime.

### `WL9007` — safe redirects

```ts
import { safeRedirect, type RequestHandler } from "@warlock.js/core";

export const afterLoginController: RequestHandler = async ({ request, response }) => {
  return response.redirect(
    safeRedirect(request.input("next"), { allowedOrigins: ["https://app.example.com"] }),
  );
};
```

In pages, `safeRedirectTarget(target) ?? "/"` from `@warlock.js/web` does the same for `navigateTo()` and `<Link to>`. A target checked by an enclosing `if (isSafeRedirect(target))` passes.

### `WL9008` — redacted logs

```ts
import type { Request } from "@warlock.js/core";
import { log, maskEmail } from "@warlock.js/logger";

export function logLogin(request: Request, user: { id: number; email: string }, token: string) {
  log.info("auth", "login", `Signed in ${maskEmail(user.email)}`, {
    userId: user.id,
    token, // `token` is a key the logger censors by default
    request: request.toLogSnapshot(),
  });
}
```

Keys the logger censors by default (`token`, `password`, `apiKey`, `authorization`, …) may carry secrets as structured data. Emails are not censored by default, so they always need `maskEmail()`. Free text from the client goes through `escapeLogValue()`.

### `WL9009` — bounded regexes on input

```ts
const SLUG = /^[a-z0-9-]{1,64}$/;

export function isSlug(value: string): boolean {
  return SLUG.test(value);
}
```

Bound each repetition (`{1,64}`, not `+`) or cap the input's length before matching.

### `WL9010`–`WL9012`

Drop the `await` from `log.info(…)` (`await log.flush()` waits for delivery); move each extra controller into its own `<name>.controller.ts`; rename a union's `kind` tag to `type` and update the `switch`.

### A deliberate exception

```ts
// warlock-check-ignore WL9006 -- authenticated by the provider's signature header
router.post("/webhooks/billing", billingWebhookController, { middleware: [verifySignature()] });
```

The comment covers the codes it names on its own line and the next; with no code it covers every code there.

---
name: warlock-doctor
description: 'Run `warlock doctor` — a read-only diagnostics command that checks routes / config / connectors / optional-peers / health endpoints / release hygiene and prints a pass/warn/fail report, exiting non-zero on any failure. Add your own probe with the `DoctorCheck` contract and `runChecks` / `formatReportLines`. Triggers: `warlock doctor`, `warlock doctor --json`, `toDoctorJson`, `WL1001`, `doctorCommand`, `DoctorCheck`, `CheckResult`, `CheckStatus`, `DoctorReport`, `runChecks`, `formatReportLines`, `printReport`, `defaultDoctorChecks`; "diagnose my app", "preflight / preflight check", "is the app healthy", "why are there 0 routes", "pre-release sanity check", "CI smoke check"; run as `npx warlock doctor`. Skip: the live `/health` + `/ready` HTTP probes — the `health-checks` topic; authoring a general CLI command — the `write-cli-command` topic; releasing the package — `releasing-warlock-monorepo`; competing tools `npm doctor`, `nest info`, hand-rolled preflight scripts.'

# Warlock — `warlock doctor`

`warlock doctor` is a read-only preflight. It boots the app far enough to introspect it — loads every config file and bootstrap code so routes and connectors register — but **starts no connectors**, so it never opens a database, cache, or socket connection. It then runs a set of checks and prints a grouped pass / warn / fail report.

```bash
npx warlock doctor
```

```
✓ routes: 42 registered
✓ config: required sections present (app, http)
✓ connectors: 3 registered, active: database, cache
⚠ optional-peers: not installed → unavailable: sharp (image processing); redis (Redis cache driver)
✓ health: liveness /health + readiness /ready registered
✓ release-hygiene: package.json and CHANGELOG agree on 4.6.0

Summary: 5 ok, 1 warn, 0 fail
```

## Error codes and `--json`

Every `warn`/`fail` finding carries a stable error code (`WL1001`, `WL2001`, …), printed after the detail and explained by `warlock explain <code>`. `--json` prints the report with the same `code` / `hint` / `skill` / `docs` fields `warlock check --json` uses (boot output goes to stderr):

```bash
npx warlock doctor --json | jq '.results[] | select(.status != "ok") | "\(.code) \(.detail)"'
npx warlock explain WL1001
```

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "results": [
    {
      "name": "config",
      "status": "fail",
      "detail": "missing required config section(s): http",
      "code": "WL1001",
      "hint": "Add the missing file under src/config/ (for example src/config/app.ts) exporting the section.",
      "skill": "configure-app",
      "docs": "https://warlock.js.org/v/latest/core/cli/error-codes/#wl1001"
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "ok": 0, "warn": 0, "fail": 1 },
  "exitCode": 1
}
```

A custom check sets `code` on its non-ok results the same way (`{ name, status: "fail", code: "WL2003", detail }`); `ok` results carry none.

## What it checks

The default set is `defaultDoctorChecks` (in registration order — runtime-surface checks first, release hygiene last):

| Check             | `ok`                                                                | `warn`                                          | `fail`                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `routes`          | ≥ 1 route registered                                                | 0 routes (a route module likely failed to load) | —                                                                                                          |
| `config`          | required sections (`app`, `http`) present                           | —                                               | a required section is missing                                                                              |
| `connectors`      | manager enumerable; reports registered + active set                 | —                                               | (only if the probe itself throws)                                                                          |
| `optional-peers`  | every known optional peer installed                                 | a peer is missing → its feature is unavailable  | —                                                                                                          |
| `jwt-secret`      | `auth.userType` configured and a JWT signing secret set             | —                                               | `auth.userType` is configured but no signing secret (`auth.accessToken.secret` / `auth.jwt.secret`) is set |
| `health`          | `/health` + `/ready` will be exposed                                | `http.health.enabled = false` (probes off)      | —                                                                                                          |
| `release-hygiene` | `package.json` version matches the top `## x.y.z` CHANGELOG heading | no `CHANGELOG.md`, or no parseable heading      | version ≠ top heading                                                                                      |

`jwt-secret` is the pre-flight form of the silent first-login 500: when `auth.userType` is set but no signing secret is, every login and token operation fails with a generic 500 at runtime — `doctor` turns that into a `fail` before you ship. It resolves the secret from both the current key (`auth.accessToken.secret`) and the legacy `auth.jwt.secret`, so a project on the older-but-supported shape doesn't trip it. When `auth.userType` isn't configured at all (no auth), the check emits **no line** — it's skipped, not a pass — so it never nags a project that isn't doing auth.

Optional peers are resolved from the **consuming app's** `node_modules` (via `createRequire(process.cwd())`), so the report reflects what _your_ project has installed, not core's own deps.

## Exit code

```
warn only  → exit 0   (warnings never fail the command)
any fail    → exit 1   (so CI / a release script can gate on it)
```

`doctor` itself can never crash: a check that throws is caught by the runner and recorded as a `fail` (detail `check threw: <message>`), not re-thrown.

## The contract

```ts
type CheckStatus = "ok" | "warn" | "fail";

type CheckResult = {
  name: string; // stable check name, e.g. "routes"
  status: CheckStatus;
  detail: string; // one-line, user-facing explanation
  code?: WarlockErrorCode; // stable code of a warn/fail verdict, e.g. "WL1001"
};

type DoctorCheck = {
  name: string;
  run: () => CheckResult | Promise<CheckResult>; // MUST be read-only
};

type DoctorReport = {
  results: CheckResult[]; // in registration order
  summary: Record<CheckStatus, number>; // counts per status
  hasFailures: boolean; // true iff any fail
  exitCode: 0 | 1; // 1 when hasFailures, else 0
};
```

A `DoctorCheck.run` must be **read-only** — it may introspect the router, connectors, config, and `package.json`, but must never mutate state or open a connection. It may be sync or async, and may throw (the runner degrades a throw to a `fail`).

## Running checks yourself

The runner and formatter are exported, so you can assemble your own check set — e.g. an app-specific preflight script or a custom CLI command:

```ts
import {
  runChecks,
  formatReportLines,
  printReport,
  defaultDoctorChecks,
  type DoctorCheck,
} from "@warlock.js/core";

const migrationsCheck: DoctorCheck = {
  name: "migrations",
  async run() {
    const pending = await countPendingMigrations(); // your read-only probe

    return pending === 0
      ? { name: "migrations", status: "ok", detail: "no pending migrations" }
      : { name: "migrations", status: "warn", detail: `${pending} pending` };
  },
};

const report = await runChecks([...defaultDoctorChecks, migrationsCheck]);

printReport(report); // colored, to stdout
const lines = formatReportLines(report); // plain strings — snapshot-friendly

if (report.hasFailures) process.exit(report.exitCode);
```

`formatReportLines` returns plain (uncolored) `<symbol> <name>: <detail>` lines plus a `Summary: …` line — handy for tests. `printReport` is the colored stdout wrapper; the structured `DoctorReport` stays the source of truth for the exit code.

## Patterns

### CI / pre-release gate

```bash
npx warlock doctor || exit 1   # non-zero exit fails the job
```

A red `release-hygiene` line catches the classic "bumped `package.json` but forgot the CHANGELOG heading" mistake before a publish.

### Diagnosing a silent 404 surface

A `⚠ routes: 0 routes registered` line is the tell that a route module threw on import or registration and the failure was surfaced (not swallowed). Re-run `warlock dev` and read the boot error.

## Gotchas

- **`doctor` starts no connectors.** It intentionally does not open DB / cache / socket connections — the `connectors` check reports the _registered_ set and which are already active, without forcing any up. Don't expect it to detect a down database.
- **Optional-peers resolves from the project, not core.** A peer installed only inside core's own `node_modules` still reports as missing — the probe uses `process.cwd()`.
- **Warnings don't fail the command.** Only a `fail` flips the exit code. Missing optional peers and disabled health endpoints are deliberate-choice `warn`s.
- **Custom checks must stay read-only.** `run()` runs against a booted-but-not-connected app; mutating state or opening a connection breaks the contract and can hang the command.

## Lint and format checks

`warlock doctor` checks application wiring and HTTP health probes. Use
`npx warlock check` for source lint diagnostics and `npm run format:check` for
formatting. In 5.33, Oxlint/Oxfmt are the defaults; ESLint requires
`warlock check --lint eslint` or `devServer.healthCheckers.eslint: true` for
background checks. ESLint/Prettier are deprecated and removed in 5.34.0.
Migrate with `npx warlock upgrade --from 5.32 --to 5.33.0` (preview with `--dry-run`).

# Warlock — `warlock inspect`

Read the app's facts from its **booted registries**, not from source text. Run it before changing an app you do not know, and when you need a fact the code only implies (the effective rate limit of a route, whether a guard runs, which resource a model uses).

```bash
npx warlock inspect                                  # counts + a route list
npx warlock inspect --json > app.json                # the full report
npx warlock inspect --json --section routes,models   # only some sections
```

It boots like `warlock doctor`: connectors boot (routes register) but none starts — no database, cache or socket connection, no port. With `--json`, stdout is only the JSON.

Sections: `routes`, `models`, `resources`, `config`, `events`, `pages`, `jobs`, `schedules`, `packages`. An unknown section fails before the app boots.

## Answer questions with jq

```bash
# Mutating API routes without an auth guard
npx warlock inspect --json --section routes \
  | jq -r '.routes[] | select(.method != "GET" and .auth.required == false and .isPage == false) | "\(.method) \(.path)  \(.sourceFile)"'

# Routes that log request bodies
npx warlock inspect --json --section routes | jq -r '.routes[] | select(.logging.body) | .path'

# A model's columns and relations
npx warlock inspect --json --section models | jq '.models[] | select(.name == "User") | {columns: [.columns[].name], relations}'

# Config keys (types only — values are never printed)
npx warlock inspect --json --section config | jq -r '.config[] | "\(.key): \(.type)"'
```

## The route entry

```json
{
  "method": "PATCH",
  "path": "/posts/:id",
  "name": "posts.update",
  "sourceFile": "src/app/posts/routes.ts",
  "handler": "updatePostController",
  "middleware": ["authMiddleware"],
  "auth": { "required": true, "sources": ["header"], "userTypes": ["user"] },
  "csrf": true,
  "rateLimit": { "source": "global", "max": 60, "timeWindow": 60000 },
  "logging": { "body": true, "query": true, "privateRules": false },
  "request": {
    "parameters": [
      { "name": "id", "in": "path", "required": true, "schema": { "type": "string" } }
    ],
    "body": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": { "title": { "type": "string" } },
      "required": ["title"]
    },
    "customValidation": false
  },
  "responses": {
    "200": {
      "description": "Successful response",
      "schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": { "post": { "$ref": "#/components/schemas/PostResource" } },
        "required": ["post"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

`$ref`s resolve against `components.schemas` in the same report. Request and response schemas come from the same code as `warlock generate.openapi`.

## From code

```ts
import { inspectApp, type InspectReport } from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

// The app is already booted in this process (a dev-server hook, a test with setupTest()):
const report: InspectReport = await inspectApp({ sections: ["routes", "models"] });
const publicWrites = report.routes?.filter(
  (route) => route.method !== "GET" && !route.auth.required,
);
```

`inspectApp()` boots nothing. To boot first, the way the command does:

```ts
import { bootForInspect, inspectApp, inspectOptionsFromBoot } from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

const boot = await bootForInspect();
const report = await inspectApp({ ...inspectOptionsFromBoot(boot) });
```

Validate a report with the published schema — `INSPECT_REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA` (draft 2020-12), also shipped as `node_modules/@warlock.js/core/schemas/inspect-report.schema.json`:

```ts
import Ajv2020 from "ajv/dist/2020";
import { INSPECT_REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA, inspectApp } from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

const report = await inspectApp();
const valid = new Ajv2020({ strict: false }).validate(INSPECT_REPORT_JSON_SCHEMA, report);
```

## Stability (schemaVersion 1)

- Fields are only added; none is removed, renamed or retyped. Ignore keys you do not know.
- A section you did not request is absent, not empty.
- Warning and description text is not a contract; match on `code` fields.
- A breaking change ships as `schemaVersion: 2`, listed under BREAKING in the changelog.

## Agents: ask through MCP instead of shelling out

`npx warlock mcp` serves the same report as tools — `inspect_app` for the counts, then `inspect_routes` (`filter`, `method`, `unguardedWrites`), `inspect_models`, `inspect_config`, … one per section, plus `db_schema` built from the `models` section. `npx warlock dev --mcp` serves them from the dev server, so they reflect the last hot reload. See the `warlock-mcp` topic.

`warlock dev` also writes a summary of this report (modules, routes, unguarded writes, models, installed skills) into the generated section of `AGENTS.md` — see the `warlock-agents-md` topic.

## Gotchas

- `warnings` lists what could not be read — `WL2001` a module failed to import (its routes are missing from the report), `WL4001` a schema with no JSON Schema form. Run `npx warlock explain <code>`.
- `events` lists listeners app modules registered on `@mongez/events` while loading; listeners added later at runtime, and `Model.events()` listeners, are not included.
- `jobs` and `schedules` appear only when a loaded module (usually `worker.ts`) defined them through the app's `@warlock.js/queue` / `@warlock.js/scheduler`.
- App modules are imported, so their import-time side effects run, as in `warlock dev`.

- The `warlock-check` topic — verify a change: typecheck, lint, tests, conventions, error codes.
- The `warlock-mcp` topic — the same facts as MCP tools for a coding agent.
- The `warlock-agents-md` topic — the app summary `warlock dev` keeps in AGENTS.md.
- The `warlock-routes` topic — the human route table.
- The `generate-openapi` topic — the same route schemas as an OpenAPI document.

---
name: warlock-mcp
description: 'Serve the app to a coding agent over the Model Context Protocol: `warlock mcp` (stdio, or `--http` on loopback with a bearer token required off loopback) and `warlock dev --mcp` / `devServer.mcp` (live registries) expose `inspect_app` + `inspect_<section>` (routes, models, resources, config, events, pages, jobs, schedules, packages), `db_schema`, `docs_search` / `docs_read` (installed @warlock.js skills, READMEs and llms files only, offline), `explain`, `check_run`, `test_run`, `requests_recent` (devtools: timeline, queries with nPlusOne, logs) and `generate_make` / `generate_add` (a unified diff from a throw-away copy; writes only with `--allow-writes`). Read-only by default. Needs `@warlock.js/ai-tools` (optional peer). Triggers: `warlock mcp`, `--allow-writes`, `--http`, `WARLOCK_MCP_TOKEN`, `warlock dev --mcp`, `devServer.mcp`, `startWarlockMcpServer`, `createMcpContext`, `createWarlockMcpTools`, `runTests`, `sandboxBackend`, `WL7003`, `WL7004`, `WL7005`, `.mcp.json`; "connect Claude Code / Cursor to my Warlock app", "let the agent ask the app", "MCP server for this project", "preview what a generator writes". Skip: the JSON report itself — the `warlock-inspect` topic; serving YOUR OWN agent tools over MCP — the `expose-as-mcp-server` topic of @warlock.js/ai-tools; one request''s timeline from the terminal — the `warlock-trace` topic.'

# Warlock — `warlock mcp`

One MCP server per app that answers what the app actually has and does — from its registries, its installed docs and its devtools — so an agent asks instead of grepping.

```bash
npm install -D @warlock.js/ai-tools @warlock.js/ai   # once: the MCP transport (optional peers)

npx warlock mcp                       # stdio — what an MCP client spawns
npx warlock mcp --http                # Streamable HTTP on 127.0.0.1, a free port (printed on stderr)
npx warlock mcp --http --port 7333 --token "$WARLOCK_MCP_TOKEN"
npx warlock mcp --allow-writes        # generate tools may write files
npx warlock dev --mcp                 # inside the dev server: live registries after every reload
```

Register it with a client (Claude Code reads `.mcp.json` at the project root):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "warlock": { "command": "npx", "args": ["warlock", "mcp"] }
  }
}
```

## Tools

| Tool                                                                                                                                                | What it returns                                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inspect_app`                                                                                                                                       | App name/version/Node, a count per section, inspect warnings. Start here.                                                                                                             |
| `inspect_routes`                                                                                                                                    | Routes with middleware, guard, CSRF, rate limit, logging, JSON Schemas. `filter`, `method`, `unguardedWrites`.                                                                        |
| `inspect_models`, `inspect_resources`, `inspect_config`, `inspect_events`, `inspect_pages`, `inspect_jobs`, `inspect_schedules`, `inspect_packages` | One `warlock inspect` section each, with `filter`.                                                                                                                                    |
| `db_schema`                                                                                                                                         | Tables from the models: columns with type, required, primary key, `belongsTo` foreign keys, relations, timestamps. No database connection.                                            |
| `docs_search` / `docs_read`                                                                                                                         | Ranked sections of `node_modules/@warlock.js/*/skills/**`, `README.md`, `llms*.txt` — the installed versions, offline.                                                                |
| `explain`                                                                                                                                           | A `WL` code: meaning, your code vs this machine, fix, skill, docs link.                                                                                                               |
| `check_run`                                                                                                                                         | The `warlock check` report (`changed`, `base`, `skip`). Exit code 2 = the machine, not the code.                                                                                      |
| `test_run`                                                                                                                                          | vitest for `files` (tests run directly, sources via `vitest related`), `changed`, or the suite.                                                                                       |
| `requests_recent`                                                                                                                                   | Recent requests from devtools: status, phases (each middleware, validation, handler), queries with `nPlusOne`, warnings, logs, timings. Needs `warlock dev` + `@warlock.js/devtools`. |
| `generate_make`                                                                                                                                     | `generate.<module\|controller\|service\|use-case\|model\|repository\|resource\|migration>` → a unified diff per file.                                                                 |
| `generate_add`                                                                                                                                      | `warlock add <features>` → the diff (package.json included; nothing installed).                                                                                                       |

Names use `_`, not `.`: model APIs only accept `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$` as a tool name.

## Read-only by default

Without `--allow-writes`, `generate_make` / `generate_add` have no `write` argument: the generator runs in a temporary copy of the project (root files and `src/`, `.env*` never copied, `node_modules` linked) and the tool returns what it would create or change:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "command": ["warlock", "generate.service", "posts/publish-post"],
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "src/app/posts/services/publish-post.service.ts",
      "status": "created",
      "diff": "--- /dev/null\n+++ b/src/app/posts/services/publish-post.service.ts\n@@ -0,0 +1,5 @@\n+…"
    }
  ]
}
```

A `write: true` sent to a read-only server is refused with `WL7005`. With `--allow-writes`, `write: true` runs the generator in the project and returns the same diff.

## HTTP rules

- Binds `127.0.0.1` by default. Any other `--host` needs `--token` (or `WARLOCK_MCP_TOKEN`), otherwise `WL7004` before anything boots.
- Clients send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when a token is set; foreign browser `Origin`s are refused (the `@warlock.js/ai-tools` HTTP transport).
- `warlock dev --mcp` serves HTTP on loopback only and records the endpoint in `.warlock/dev-server.json` (`mcp.url`). Options in `warlock.config.ts`:

```ts title="warlock.config.ts"
import { defineConfig } from "@warlock.js/core";

export default defineConfig({
  devServer: {
    mcp: { port: 7333, token: process.env.WARLOCK_MCP_TOKEN, allowWrites: false },
  },
});
```

## From code

```ts
import {
  createMcpContext,
  inspectApp,
  runTests,
  startWarlockMcpServer,
} from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

// The app is already booted in this process.
const context = createMcpContext({ inspect: (sections) => inspectApp({ sections }) });
const server = await startWarlockMcpServer({ context, transport: { type: "http", port: 0 } });

console.error(`MCP at ${server.url} — ${server.tools.length} tools`);

const tests = await runTests({ files: ["src/app/posts/services/publish-post.service.ts"] });
console.error(
  tests.ok ? "tests pass" : tests.problems.map((problem) => problem.message).join("\n"),
);

await server.close();
```

## Gotchas

- `warlock mcp` boots like `warlock inspect` (connectors booted, none started — no database connection, no app port) on the first tool call, and keeps that snapshot. After changing routes or models, restart it — or use `warlock dev --mcp`, which reads the live registries.
- Over stdio, stdout is the JSON-RPC stream: `console.log` / `info` / `debug` are sent to stderr for the whole run.
- `requests_recent` fails with `WL8008` when no dev server is recorded or reachable, and `WL8009` when devtools is not installed (`npx warlock add devtools`).
- Missing `@warlock.js/ai-tools` / `@warlock.js/ai` → `WL7003` with the install line.

- The `warlock-inspect` topic — the report the `inspect_*` tools return.
- The `warlock-check` topic — what `check_run` and `test_run` report.
- The `warlock-trace` topic — send a request and read its timeline.
- The `expose-as-mcp-server` topic of @warlock.js/ai-tools — the transport underneath.


## warlock-routes  `@warlock.js/core/warlock-routes/SKILL.md`

---
name: warlock-routes
description: 'Run `warlock routes` — a read-only command that lists the registered HTTP routes as a verb-colored table (method / path / name / action / middleware-count / source), a sibling of `warlock doctor`. Filter with `--method` / `--path` / `--name`, or emit normalized rows as JSON with `--json`. Also covers `warlock routes:diff`, which compares live page routes against the last `warlock build`''s route snapshot and exits non-zero on drift. Triggers: `warlock routes`, `routesCommand`, `warlock routes:diff`, `routesDiffCommand`, "list my routes", "show all routes", "route table", "what endpoints does my app expose", "dump routes as JSON", "which routes have middleware", "route map for CI", "did my page routes drift from the last build"; run as `npx warlock routes` / `npx warlock routes:diff`. Skip: read-only health/preflight checks — the `warlock-doctor` topic; defining/naming/grouping routes — the `register-route` topic; authoring a general CLI command — the `write-cli-command` topic; competing tools `nest`/`express` route listers, `php artisan route:list`.'
---

# Warlock — `warlock routes`

`warlock routes` lists every registered HTTP route as a table. It's the read-only sibling of the `warlock-doctor` topic: it boots the app far enough to register route modules — but **starts no connectors**, so it never opens a database, cache, or socket connection.

```bash
npx warlock routes
```

```
METHOD  PATH              NAME           ACTION    MW  SOURCE
GET     /users            users.list     index     2   app/users/routes.ts
POST    /users            users.create   store     2   app/users/routes.ts
GET     /users/:id        users.get      show      2   app/users/routes.ts
DELETE  /users/:id        users.delete   destroy   3   app/users/routes.ts

4 routes (2 GET · 1 POST · 1 DELETE)
```

The `METHOD` column is verb-colored (GET green, POST blue, PUT/PATCH yellow, DELETE red, `all`/OPTIONS/HEAD dim). Rows sort by path, then by HTTP-method order within a path.

## Columns

| Column   | Meaning                                                     |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `METHOD` | HTTP verb; a wildcard `all` route lists as `ALL`.           |
| `PATH`   | Full request path (group prefix already folded in).         |
| `NAME`   | Route name, or `—` when unnamed.                            |
| `ACTION` | Handler function name (`anonymous` for an unnamed handler). |
| `MW`     | Count of middleware attached to the route.                  |
| `SOURCE` | Source file the route registered from, or `—`.              |

## Filters

Optional, case-insensitive, AND-combined:

```bash
npx warlock routes --method GET     # -m  exact HTTP method
npx warlock routes --path /users    # -p  path substring
npx warlock routes --name users     # -n  route-name substring
npx warlock routes -m POST -p /users
```

## JSON output

`--json` (`-j`) emits the normalized rows instead of the table — for `jq`, a CI diff, or a generated API map. Filters apply before serialization.

```bash
npx warlock routes --json
```

```json
[
  {
    "method": "GET",
    "path": "/users",
    "name": "users.list",
    "action": "index",
    "middleware": 2,
    "source": "app/users/routes.ts"
  }
]
```

## Patterns

### Audit which routes are guarded

```bash
npx warlock routes --json | jq '[.[] | select(.middleware == 0)]'
```

Surfaces public routes (no middleware) — a quick check that auth-protected paths actually carry a guard.

### Confirm a route registered

```bash
npx warlock routes --name users.create
```

An empty result means the route isn't registered — re-run `warlock dev` and read the boot error (the route-module loader is fail-loud, so a throwing route file aborts boot rather than being silently dropped).

## `warlock routes:diff` — catch page-route drift before it ships

Compares the **live dev-server page routes** (`router.list().filter(r => r.isPage)`) against a **snapshot written by the last successful `warlock build`** (`page-routes.manifest.json` in `resolveBuildConfig().outdir`, e.g. `dist/page-routes.manifest.json`). Boots the same diagnostic way as `warlock routes` — route modules registered, no connectors started — then diffs.

```bash
npx warlock routes:diff
```

```
Page routes match (4 routes).
Note: page names are compared as DERIVED by the build, so a clean diff does not prove
that no route name collided at registration (the router appends `.<method>` to a name
already claimed by another method). Run `warlock routes` to see the registered names.
```

**A clean baseline is now expected immediately after a successful `warlock build`.** Through 5.1, running `routes:diff` on an untouched checkout right after a green build reported drift, because the manifest recorded the catch-all as `"*"` while the router serves it as `"/*"`. The manifest is now written through the router's own path normalizer, so the two sides agree and a clean tree reports clean. If you see drift on a tree you have not edited since building, that is a bug worth reporting — it is no longer the expected greeting.

⚠ **What a clean diff does NOT prove.** The manifest records what each page's name was **derived** as, not what it was **registered** as. `warlock build` never boots connectors, so it cannot see the API routes a page name might collide with; when a name is already claimed by another method the router appends a `.<method>` suffix at registration, and the comparison accepts that suffix rather than reporting it as drift. So `Page routes match` means _the page surface did not move since the build_ — it does not mean _no page route name collided_. Use `warlock routes` to see the names as actually registered.

or, on drift:

```
changed - GET /blog/:slug  blog.post (src/web/blog/[slug].page.tsx)
        + GET /blog/:id    blog.post (src/web/blog/[slug].page.tsx)
removed - GET /legacy      legacy.home
added   + GET /promo       promo.home   (src/web/promo.page.tsx)
Page route drift: 1 changed, 1 removed, 1 added. Run `warlock build` after reviewing these changes.
```

and exits non-zero.

- **Identity is `method` + `path` + `name`.** A route is only reported `changed` — instead of one `removed` line and one unrelated `added` line — when it shares its **`source` file** with the route it's being paired against. A moved checkout (same source, different absolute path on disk) never shows as drift; a route whose declared path/name literally changed in the same file does.
- **Requires a prior successful build.** No `page-routes.manifest.json` yet, or a malformed one → the command refuses to run and tells you to `warlock build` first, rather than diffing against nothing.
- **Fails loudly on a broken dev boot**, same as `warlock routes` / `warlock doctor` — a route module that throws on import, or a connector registration error, aborts before any comparison happens.
- **Only page routes are compared.** API routes registered without `isPage` never appear on either side of the diff; this command exists for the file-system page-routing surface `@warlock.js/web` adds, not the general route table.
- **Core reads the snapshot; it does not write it.** `warlock build` writes `page-routes.manifest.json` through a connector's `build`/`emit` contribution (`@warlock.js/web`'s build integration, keyed off pages it discovers) — a project with no `@warlock.js/web` page routes never produces one, and `routes:diff` has nothing to compare against.

## Gotchas

- **No connectors are started.** The list reflects what's _registered_, not what would connect. It never opens a DB/cache/socket.
- **An empty table is a tell.** `No routes registered` is the same signal `warlock doctor`'s `routes` check warns on — a route module likely failed to load.
- **`MW` counts, it doesn't name.** It's a "is this route guarded?" signal; for the actual chain, read the route definition.
- **`ACTION` is the handler function name.** A controller method shows its method name; an inline anonymous handler shows `anonymous`.

## See also

- The `warlock-doctor` topic — the read-only diagnostics sibling; its `routes` check warns when this table would be empty.
- The `register-route` topic — defining, naming, and grouping the routes this command lists.
- The `run-app` topic — `warlock build`, the command that produces the snapshot `routes:diff` compares against.
- The `write-cli-command` topic — the command + `preload` shape `routesCommand` is built from.


## warlock-trace  `@warlock.js/core/warlock-trace/SKILL.md`

---
name: warlock-trace
description: 'Verify runtime behaviour without a browser: `warlock trace <method> <url> [--body json|@file] [--header k:v] [--json]` sends one request to the running `warlock dev` server and prints what devtools recorded for it — middleware chain with timings, validation result and errors, handler time, queries with N+1 flags, logs, cache operations, captured mails, the response and timings — as a versioned report (`schemaVersion: 1`); `traceRequest()` returns the same object. Triggers: `warlock trace`, `traceRequest`, `TraceReport`, `buildTraceReport`, `x-request-id`, `.warlock/dev-server.json`, `WL8008`, `WL8009`, `WL5004`, `--id-header`; "did validation pass for this request", "which queries does this endpoint run", "is there an N+1 on this route", "what middleware runs on this route", "check the endpoint after my change", "request timeline as JSON". Skip: the devtools dashboard in a browser — the `devtools-overview` skill of @warlock.js/devtools; static route facts (guard, rate limit, schemas) — the `warlock-inspect` topic; typecheck/lint/tests — the `warlock-check` topic.'
---

# Warlock — `warlock trace`

Send a real request to the running dev server and read back its devtools timeline. Use it after a change to confirm what the code actually does at runtime: the middleware that ran, whether validation refused the body, which queries ran and whether any is an N+1.

Needs `warlock dev` running in the project and `@warlock.js/devtools` installed (`npx warlock add devtools`). The dev server records its address in `.warlock/dev-server.json`; `trace` reads it from there.

```bash
npx warlock trace GET /posts
npx warlock trace POST /posts --body '{"title":"Hello"}' --json
npx warlock trace PATCH /posts/1 --body @payload.json -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --json
npx warlock trace GET /posts --url http://localhost:2030 --json   # explicit server
```

`--header` / `-H` repeats. A JSON `--body` is sent as `application/json` unless you pass a `content-type` header; `@file` reads the body from a file.

## Answer questions with jq

```bash
# Validation verdict and errors
npx warlock trace POST /posts --body '{"title":""}' --json | jq '.timeline.validation'
# → { "ran": true, "durationMs": 0.6, "passed": false, "errors": [{ "input": "title", "error": "The title is required" }] }

# N+1 queries with the line that issued them
npx warlock trace GET /posts --json | jq '.queries[] | select(.nPlusOne) | {sql, caller}'

# Middleware chain, in run order
npx warlock trace GET /admin/users -H "authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --json \
  | jq -r '.timeline.middleware[] | "\(.index) \(.name) \(.durationMs)ms"'

# Status and body
npx warlock trace GET /posts/1 --json | jq '{status: .response.status, body: .response.body}'
```

## The report (schemaVersion 1)

Top-level keys: `requestId`, `server`, `request` (method, url, headers with credentials `[redacted]`, body), `response` (status, headers, body — parsed JSON or text, cut at 64 KiB with `truncated`), `route`, `error`, `timeline` (`phases`, `routeMatch`, `middleware[]`, `validation`, `handler`), `queries[]` (each with `nPlusOne`), `warnings[]`, `logs[]`, `cache[]`, `mails[]`, `timings` (`totalMs` server, `clientMs` round trip, `phasesMs` per phase).

`timeline.validation.passed`: `true` when the handler ran after validation, `false` when the request was answered with an error before the handler, `null` when the route validates nothing.

## From code

```ts
import { traceRequest } from "@warlock.js/core/tooling";

const report = await traceRequest({ method: "POST", url: "/posts", body: { title: "Hello" } });

const slowQueries = report.queries.filter((query) => Number(query.durationMs) > 50);
const nPlusOne = report.queries.some((query) => query.nPlusOne);
```

## How the request is matched

`trace` sends a fresh UUID as `x-request-id`. Core adopts it as `request.id` and echoes it back; devtools keys its record by that id. If the app renamed the header (`http.requestId.header`), pass `--id-header <name>`. If it disabled it (`http.requestId.enabled: false`), no record can be matched.

## Errors

| Code     | Meaning                                                             | Exit |
| -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---- |
| `WL8008` | No dev server recorded, or it does not answer — start `warlock dev` | 2    |
| `WL8009` | Dev server up, devtools not mounted — `warlock add devtools`        | 2    |
| `WL5004` | Devtools has no record of the request (request id disabled)         | 1    |

Devtools is checked before anything is sent. With `--json` a failure prints `{ "ok": false, "code", "message" }`. Exit 2 means "this machine", not your code — start the server instead of editing code. `npx warlock explain <code>` prints the fix.

## Gotchas

- Run it on the same machine as the dev server: devtools answers loopback requests only, in development only.
- Paths under the devtools prefix (`/__warlock`) are never recorded.
- Devtools keeps the last 200 requests in memory; a restart of `warlock dev` clears them.
- The request really runs: a `POST` writes to the development database.

## See also

- The `warlock-inspect` topic — the static facts of a route (guard, rate limit, schemas).
- The `warlock-check` topic — typecheck, lint, tests and conventions in one run.
- The `devtools-overview` skill of `@warlock.js/devtools` — the dashboard behind the timeline.


## wire-socket  `@warlock.js/core/wire-socket/SKILL.md`

---
name: wire-socket
description: 'Configure Socket.IO via `src/config/socket.ts`, reach the live server through `getSocketServer()` (or `app.socket` post-bootstrap), register `connection` handlers once the late-phase socket connector has booted, emit from controllers/services, use rooms and namespaces. Triggers: `app.socket`, `getSocketServer`, `SocketOptions`, `socket.io` `Server`, `socket.join`, `socket.to`, `io.of`, `io.use`; "add realtime chat", "emit socket events from a service", "use rooms and namespaces", "per-socket JWT auth". Skip: connector lifecycle — the `add-connector` topic; app context accessors — the `use-app-context` topic; competing libs `ws`, `socket.io` direct without Warlock connector, `uWebSockets.js`.'
