# `@warlock.js/ai-bedrock`

Provider adapter that turns AWS Bedrock's **Converse API** into a vendor-neutral `ModelContract`, plus an Amazon **Titan** embedder. One wire mapping covers every Bedrock family.

## Construction

```ts
import { BedrockSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

// Ambient AWS credential chain (env vars / SSO / IAM role):
const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({ region: "us-east-1" });

// Explicit static credentials:
const bedrock2 = new BedrockSDK({
  region: "us-east-1",
  credentials: { accessKeyId: "AKIA...", secretAccessKey: "..." },
  provider: "bedrock-eu",
});

// Amazon Bedrock API key (bearer auth, no AWS credentials):
const bedrock3 = new BedrockSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.BEDROCK_API_KEY!,
  region: "us-east-1",
});
```

Bedrock authenticates via the **AWS credential chain** or an **Amazon Bedrock API key**. `apiKey` sends `Authorization: Bearer <key>` instead of a SigV4 signature (the adapter sets the AWS SDK's `token` + `authSchemePreference: ["httpBearerAuth"]`); combining it with `credentials` or `token`, or passing an empty key, throws `InvalidRequestError`. Without `apiKey`, the AWS SDK still reads a key from `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK` on its own. `region` is required; `credentials` is optional (omit to use the standard provider chain). The whole config object is forwarded to `BedrockRuntimeClient`, so any AWS client option (`endpoint`, `requestHandler`, retry config) is accepted. `provider` defaults to `"bedrock"`.

## Producing a model

`name` is the Bedrock **model id or inference-profile id**:

```ts
bedrock.model({ name: "anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0" });
bedrock.model({ name: "us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0", temperature: 0.2 });
bedrock.model({ name: "meta.llama3-1-8b-instruct-v1:0", maxTokens: 1024 });
```

Uses the model-agnostic **Converse / ConverseStream** API — one wire mapping covers every Bedrock family (Claude, Nova, Llama, Mistral, Cohere) instead of per-family `InvokeModel` body shapes.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `structuredOutput` | `true` (via Converse `outputConfig.textFormat`)                                                                                                        |
| `vision`           | Inferred from model id substring. `true` for Claude 3/3.5/3.7/4, Nova Lite/Pro/Premier, Llama 3.2-11B/90B, Llama 4.                                    |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3.7 + Claude 4 (Sonnet/Opus/Haiku) — they expose a configurable thinking budget on Converse.                 |
| `promptCaching`    | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3.5+/3.7/4/5 and Nova 2 Lite / Micro / Lite / Pro / Premier — the families that honor Converse `cachePoint`. |
| `pdf`              | Inferred from model id. `true` for Claude 3+ and Nova Lite/Pro/Premier (Converse `document` blocks).                                                   |
| `audio`            | `false` by default — Converse does not accept audio blocks for the families this adapter targets. Pass `audio: true` for a confirmed audio model.      |

Explicit config always wins — every flag is overridable per model, e.g. `bedrock.model({ name, reasoning: false, promptCaching: true, pdf: false, audio: true })`.

## Reasoning / extended thinking

For a `reasoning`-capable model (Claude 3.7 / 4), `ModelCallOptions.reasoning` maps to Converse's escape hatch `additionalModelRequestFields.thinking = { type: "enabled", budget_tokens }`:

```ts
// Explicit thinking budget (token cap):
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { maxTokens: 2048 } });

// Effort tier → conventional budget (low 1024 / medium 4096 / high 16384):
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } });
```

`maxTokens` wins over `effort` when both are set. For non-reasoning models — or when neither `effort` nor `maxTokens` is given — the option is a no-op, so unsupported params never reach the wire. Bedrock's Converse `TokenUsage` reports no reasoning-token channel, so `usage.reasoningTokens` is left unset (reasoning text arrives as `reasoningContent` content blocks, not a token count).

A thinking budget below `1024` throws before the request. When thinking is enabled and no output cap is configured, Converse receives `maxTokens = thinking budget + 4096`; an explicit `maxTokens` must be greater than the budget. On tool calls, Converse `reasoningContent` is retained and replayed automatically on the next turn through provider metadata. The stored shape is JSON-safe: signed reasoning text stays text, while redacted reasoning bytes are base64 encoded, so persisted history preserves the opaque block exactly.

## Prompt caching

For a `promptCaching`-capable model, `ModelCallOptions.cacheControl.breakpoints` (any positive value) places a Converse `cachePoint` on every stable segment of the prefix, in the order Bedrock processes them (`tools` → `system` → `messages`, three of the four checkpoints it allows):

| Segment  | Where the `cachePoint` goes             | Models                                               |
| -------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| tools    | after the last `toolConfig.tools` entry | Claude only — Nova accepts no cache point in `tools` |
| system   | after the system blocks                 | every caching-capable model                          |
| messages | appended to the LAST message            | every caching-capable model                          |

The lifetime is the per-call `cacheControl.ttl`, else the model's `promptCacheTtl`. `ttl: "1h"` is sent only to models that accept it — Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet / Opus 4.5+ and every Claude 5 family; any other model gets the 5-minute default, because AWS warns that the field "can result in a ValidationException" on 5-minute-only models.

```ts
import { BedrockSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({ region: "us-east-1" });
const model = bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6", promptCacheTtl: "1h" });

// tools + system + last message are cached for an hour:
await model.complete(
  [
    { role: "system", content: "Long, stable instructions…" },
    { role: "user", content: "First question" },
  ],
  { cacheControl: { breakpoints: 1 } },
);

// Per call, the TTL can be overridden:
await model.complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }], {
  cacheControl: { breakpoints: 1, ttl: "5m" },
});
```

Source for the placement rules and TTL support: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/prompt-caching.html (checked 2026-10-17). No-ops gracefully when the model is not caching-capable or no breakpoint was requested. Read-side accounting works without any breakpoint — see the usage section below.

## System prompt

Converse has no `"system"` role in `messages`. The adapter hoists every neutral `role: "system"` message into the separate `system: SystemContentBlock[]` request field. Transparent to the agent.

## Tool calls

- Outgoing: neutral tools → `toolConfig.tools[].toolSpec` with a JSON `inputSchema`. No tools → `toolConfig` omitted entirely (Bedrock rejects an empty `tools` array).
- Assistant tool calls in history → `assistant` message with optional leading `{ text }` + one `{ toolUse }` block per call.
- Tool results (`role: "tool"`) → a `user` turn with one `{ toolResult: { toolUseId, content: [{ text }] } }` block.
- Response `toolUse` blocks → neutral `toolCalls`; `stopReason: "tool_use"` → `finishReason: "tool_calls"`.

## Structured output

Object-root `responseSchema` + `structuredOutput`-capable → `outputConfig.textFormat = { type: "json_schema", structure: { jsonSchema: { name, schema } } }` — note Bedrock wants the schema as a **stringified JSON document**.

## Multipart messages (vision)

- `{ type: "text" }` → `{ text }`
- `{ type: "image", source: { base64, mediaType } }` → `{ image: { format, source: { bytes } } }` (base64 decoded; media type → `jpeg`/`png`/`gif`/`webp`)
- `{ type: "image", source: { url } }` → **throws `InvalidRequestError`**. Bedrock's `ImageSource` only accepts raw bytes or an S3 location. Resolve images to base64 first.

## Streaming

`model.stream()` drains `ConverseStreamCommand`'s `response.stream`:

- `contentBlockDelta.delta.text` → `{ type: "delta", content }`
- `toolUse`: `contentBlockStart` opens an accumulator, `contentBlockDelta.delta.toolUse.input` fragments append, `contentBlockStop` emits one consolidated `{ type: "tool-call", ... }`
- terminal `{ type: "done", finishReason, usage }` — usage from `metadata.usage` (a `TokenUsage`), including `cachedTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` when reported (see the usage table below)
- opt-in (`options.streamChunks`, set by `agent.stream()`): `{ type: "reasoning", delta }` per `reasoningContent.text` delta, `{ type: "tool-args", callId, name, delta }` per client `toolUse.input` delta; no `usage` chunk (usage arrives once at the end)

**System tools:** `ai.providerTool({ provider: "bedrock", definition: { systemTool: { name: "nova_grounding" } } })` is appended to `toolConfig.tools` verbatim. `toolUse` blocks with `type: "server_tool_use"` are never dispatched as tool calls.

```ts
const grounding = ai.providerTool({
  provider: "bedrock",
  definition: { systemTool: { name: "nova_grounding" } },
});
ai.agent({ model: bedrock.model({ name: "us.amazon.nova-premier-v1:0" }), tools: [grounding] });
```

## Finish-reason mapping

`end_turn` / `stop_sequence` → `stop` · `max_tokens` → `length` · `tool_use` → `tool_calls` · `content_filtered` / `guardrail_intervened` / unknown / null → `error`.

## Embeddings — Amazon Titan only

```ts
const embedder = bedrock.embedder({ name: "amazon.titan-embed-text-v2:0" });
const { vector } = await embedder.embed("Hello world");
const { vectors } = await embedder.embedMany(["a", "b"]); // N sequential calls
```

Targets the **Titan Text Embeddings** family via `InvokeModel`. **Titan has no batch endpoint** — `embedMany` issues one request per input sequentially and aggregates token usage. Cohere-on-Bedrock batch embeddings use an incompatible body shape and are out of scope — use the OpenAI adapter when batch throughput matters.

Pass `dimensions` to forward Titan v2's truncation hint (256 / 512 / 1024).

## Errors

Raw AWS SDK exceptions are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy. Dispatch keys on the Smithy exception `name`:

- `AccessDeniedException` / 401 / 403 → `ProviderAuthError`
- `ThrottlingException` / 429 → `ProviderRateLimitError`
- `ServiceQuotaExceededException` → `QuotaExceededError`
- `ValidationException` with "too long / context window" → `ContextLengthExceededError`, else `InvalidRequestError`
- `ModelTimeoutException` / `ETIMEDOUT` → `ProviderTimeoutError`
- `ServiceUnavailableException` / 503 → `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`) — the service is temporarily unable to serve the request
- other 5xx / `ModelError` → `ProviderError`

Every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"` — AWS publishes no rule for failed requests). `fallbackModel` fails over on `PROVIDER_OVERLOADED` by default.

## Token counting

```ts
await bedrock.count("some text"); // approximate heuristic, offline
```

Per-model tokenizers differ across Bedrock families.

## Pricing — built-in Claude prices and registry

All rates are **USD per 1,000,000 tokens** (`ModelPricing`: `input`, `output`, optional `cachedInput`, `cacheWrite`, `cacheWrite1h`). Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` (`bedrock.model({ name, pricing })`) > SDK registry (exact id) > built-in profile price > `undefined` (no cost computed).

```ts
import { ai, totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import {
  BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING,
  BedrockSDK,
  bedrockPricingFor,
  withClaudeCacheWriteRates,
} from "@warlock.js/ai-bedrock";

const bedrock = new BedrockSDK({
  region: "eu-west-1",
  pricing: {
    // In-Region and non-US geographic ids are not built in — price them yourself.
    "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6": { input: 3.3, output: 16.5, cachedInput: 0.33 },
    "amazon.nova-pro-v1:0": { input: 0.8, output: 3.2 }, // your own rates for unlisted models
  },
});

bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }).pricing; // built-in global rate
bedrock.model({ name: "eu.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }).pricing; // registry + Claude write rates filled (cacheWrite 4.125, cacheWrite1h 6.6)
bedrockPricingFor("us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0"); // US geographic rate
withClaudeCacheWriteRates("anthropic.claude-opus-4-8", { input: 5, output: 25 }); // + cacheWrite 6.25, cacheWrite1h 10
Object.keys(BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING); // the priced Claude model ids

const { usage } = await ai
  .agent({ model: bedrock.model({ name: "global.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6" }) })
  .execute("hi");
console.log(usage.cost, totalCost(usage.cost)); // per-channel USD breakdown of THIS run, and its sum
```

- **Source.** https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/pricing/ — the page's own price feed for "US East (N. Virginia)", fetched 2026-10-17; model ids from the prompt-caching guide. `BEDROCK_GLOBAL_PRICING` holds the `global.` cross-Region profile rates, `BEDROCK_US_PRICING` the `us.` geographic rates (10% above global for these models). Both are keyed by the bare model id; `bedrockPricingFor(id)` strips the profile prefix.
- **Covered:** Claude Sonnet 5.5 / 5 / 4.6 / 4.5, Opus 5.5 / 5 / 4.8 / 4.7 / 4.6 / 4.5, Fable 5.1 / 5, Haiku 4.5 — with cache read, 5-minute write (1.25x input) and 1-hour write (2x input).
- **Deliberately unpriced:** in-Region ids with no profile prefix and other geographies (`eu.`, `apac.`, …) — their rates vary by Region; Claude Haiku 5.5 (not verified); and every non-Claude model (Nova, Llama, Titan, …). Pass `pricing` for them.
- **Claude write rates are filled.** Any Claude entry (your own included) without `cacheWrite` / `cacheWrite1h` gets 1.25x / 2x the input rate (`withClaudeCacheWriteRates`). Non-Claude entries are left as given; an unpriced cache write then bills at the input rate.

### Tokens & usage — cost truth

Both `complete()` and `stream()` normalize Converse's `TokenUsage` into the neutral `Usage` shape. With caching, `inputTokens` "represents only the non-cached input tokens" — total input is `inputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheWriteInputTokens` (AWS prompt-caching guide) — so the adapter marks the usage `inputIncludesCache: false` and cost bills each channel once:

| Converse `TokenUsage` field | Neutral `Usage` field      | Notes                                                                |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `inputTokens`               | `usage.input`              | **Excludes** cache reads and writes. Bills at `pricing.input`.       |
| —                           | `usage.inputIncludesCache` | Always `false` on Bedrock.                                           |
| `outputTokens`              | `usage.output`             |                                                                      |
| `totalTokens`               | `usage.total`              | Falls back to `input + output` when absent.                          |
| `cacheReadInputTokens`      | `usage.cachedTokens`       | Only when `> 0`. Cache-hit reads — bills at `pricing.cachedInput`.   |
| `cacheWriteInputTokens`     | `usage.cacheWriteTokens`   | Only when `> 0`. Cache writes — bills at `pricing.cacheWrite`.       |
| `cacheDetails[ttl: "1h"]`   | `usage.cacheWrite1hTokens` | The 1-hour share of the writes — bills at `pricing.cacheWrite1h`.    |
| —                           | `usage.reasoningTokens`    | **Never set** — Converse exposes no reasoning-token count.           |
| —                           | `usage.cost`               | Attached on `complete()` and the streaming `done` chunk when priced. |

Read-side accounting is populated whenever Bedrock reports it, independent of whether you sent a `cacheControl` breakpoint.

## Provider body options and input-token counts

Native body fields merge after neutral options. When both values are plain
objects, their immediate keys merge and caller-provided keys win; untouched
neutral fields remain. Arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field. This merge
is one level deep: a nested object explicitly supplied by the caller replaces
that nested value.

`providerOptions.bedrock.body` adds native Converse request fields after the
neutral options, for completion and streaming:

```ts
const options = {
  reasoning: { effort: "high" as const }, // preserved alongside top_k
  providerOptions: { bedrock: { body: { additionalModelRequestFields: { top_k: 4 } } } },
};
await model.complete(messages, options);
```

The key stays `bedrock` for custom provider labels. Other provider keys are
ignored. `BedrockCallOptions` is exported. `modelId`, `messages`, `system` and
`toolConfig` are protected; attempting to replace them throws
`InvalidRequestError`. Provider fields are otherwise forwarded without validation.

`model.countTokens(messages, options?)` calls Bedrock `CountTokens` using the same
Converse messages, system blocks, tool configuration and
`additionalModelRequestFields` used for generation. Cancellation is forwarded.
Availability depends on the model and region; provider failures use the adapter's
normal typed errors. `sdk.count(text)` remains a separate offline estimate.

For budget preflight, `countInputTokens(model, messages, { tools })` from
`@warlock.js/ai` returns `{ tokens, source }`. It estimates only when native
counting is absent or explicitly throws `InvalidRequestError` with
`reason: "count-unsupported"`; this adapter preserves that signal. System and
tools are supported natively. Ordinary validation, auth, network and rate-limit
errors propagate. See the cost/budget guide for reserve mode.

```ts
if (model.countTokens) {
  const inputTokens = await model.countTokens(messages, options);
}
```

## When NOT to use this skill

- Direct `@aws-sdk/client-bedrock-runtime` calls without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.
- OpenAI / Anthropic-direct / Gemini / Ollama models — those have their own adapter packages.
- Batch embeddings throughput — Titan is single-input upstream; use the OpenAI / Google / Ollama adapter (those batch natively).

## See also

- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill
- The `embed-text` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill

## Adjacent conversation turns

Converse messages combine adjacent turns of the same role, retaining every
content block in order. This keeps parallel tool results in one user turn and
allows an automatic compaction summary beside an assistant tool-call turn
without creating consecutive assistant turns. Agent compaction frames a summary
as user context when it replaces the first non-system turn.

Adjacent-turn normalization preserves empty histories and separate system prompts
without inserting synthetic conversation turns.

## Hosted-search accounting limit

Bedrock Converse's [TokenUsage schema](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/APIReference/API_runtime_TokenUsage.html)
and the installed SDK expose token/cache counts, with no hosted-tool request
counter (verified 2026-10-18). `usage.serverToolUse` therefore remains absent;
no count or search fee is inferred from `server_tool_use` system-tool blocks.
Hosted system tools continue to stay outside function dispatch. Direct
Anthropic counters are not assumed to exist on Converse. Supply fees only when
your own verified metering establishes the billing unit.

# `@warlock.js/ai-deepseek`

Provider adapter for DeepSeek. DeepSeek's API is **OpenAI-compatible**, so this package is a **thin wrapper** over `@warlock.js/ai-openai`'s `OpenAISDK` (the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill): it constructs an internal `OpenAISDK` pinned to `https://api.deepseek.com` with `provider: "deepseek"` and delegates `model()` / `embedder()` / `image()` / `count()` to it — while injecting DeepSeek's own capability inference and pricing so the right flags are set even though the model names aren't OpenAI names. Pair with `@warlock.js/ai` for the agent / tool / system-prompt surface.

## Construction

```ts
import { DeepSeekSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-deepseek";

const deepseek = new DeepSeekSDK({ apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY! });
```

`apiKey` is the only required field — `baseURL` defaults to `https://api.deepseek.com` (DeepSeek's OpenAI-compatible endpoint) and `provider` defaults to `"deepseek"`. Override `baseURL` only for a proxy/gateway, or `provider` to relabel the upstream:

```ts
new DeepSeekSDK({ apiKey, baseURL: "https://my-gateway/deepseek", provider: "deepseek-proxy" });
```

`DeepSeekSDK` is a class (like `OpenAISDK`) holding one long-lived wrapped client — construct once per account and reuse.

## Producing a model

```ts
deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-chat" }); // V3 lineage, non-thinking
deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-reasoner" }); // R1 lineage, reasoning-capable
deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-chat", temperature: 0.2 });
```

Returns a `ModelContract` you pass straight into `ai.agent({ model })`.

## Models

| Model               | Notes                                                                              |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deepseek-chat`     | Non-thinking surface (V3 lineage). Fast, cheap, broad coverage. Reasoning **off**. |
| `deepseek-reasoner` | Thinking surface (R1 lineage). Emits a reasoning channel. Reasoning **on**.        |
| `deepseek-v4-flash` | Newer flash tier. Reasoning **off** by default.                                    |
| `deepseek-v4-pro`   | Newer quality tier. Reasoning **on** by default.                                   |

DeepSeek announced the legacy `deepseek-chat` / `deepseek-reasoner` names retire 2026/07/24 in favor of the `deepseek-v4-*` family; both name sets are understood by the capability inference. `deepseek.model({ name })` accepts any id the upstream serves.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from the DeepSeek model name. `true` for `deepseek-reasoner` and the `*-pro` tier; `false` for `deepseek-chat` / `*-flash`. Drives whether the reasoning-effort knob is forwarded. |
| `vision`           | `false` for every DeepSeek model — no DeepSeek chat model documents image input (mid-2026).                                                                                                 |
| `structuredOutput` | `true` (inherited from the wrapped OpenAI model), unless `responseFormat` is set to a loose mode.                                                                                           |
| `promptCaching`    | `true` (inherited). DeepSeek reports cache hits via `usage.cachedTokens`, the same shape as OpenAI.                                                                                         |

**Override any flag explicitly** via `.model({ name, reasoning?, vision?, structuredOutput? })` — an explicit value always wins over the injected inference.

```ts
deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-chat", reasoning: true }); // force thinking flag
deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-reasoner", reasoning: false }); // suppress it
```

## Uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint

Everything on the wire — Chat Completions request/response shape, streaming loop, tool-call accumulation, structured-output `response_format`, multipart message mapping, and error wrapping — is inherited **unchanged** from `OpenAIModel`. See the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill for the wire-level detail; it all applies here against `https://api.deepseek.com`.

Structured output, reasoning effort, and streaming therefore behave exactly as documented for the OpenAI adapter:

```ts
const model = deepseek.model({ name: "deepseek-reasoner" }); // reasoning auto-true
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } }); // → reasoning_effort: "high"
```

## Embeddings & images

`deepseek.embedder({...})` and `deepseek.image({...})` delegate to the wrapped `OpenAISDK`. **DeepSeek does not officially document an OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint or an image-generation endpoint (mid-2026)** — these delegates exist for adapter parity and work against a compatible gateway you point `baseURL` at, but may fail against the stock DeepSeek endpoint. Use a dedicated embeddings provider (e.g. `@warlock.js/ai-openai` / `@warlock.js/ai-google`) for RAG.

## Pricing

The adapter ships **built-in DeepSeek pricing defaults** (`DEEPSEEK_DEFAULT_PRICING`, USD per 1M tokens; `cachedInput` is the cache-hit rate), so `usage.cost` is computed out of the box — on agent reports and on each `model.complete()` / streaming `done` usage.

DeepSeek bills by time of day: peak hours (01:00–04:00 and 06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday) cost twice the off-peak rate. A flat `ModelPricing` cannot follow the clock, so the defaults are the **peak** rates — an upper bound that keeps USD budgets safe; off-peak calls really cost half. Opt into `DEEPSEEK_OFF_PEAK_PRICING` when you know you run off-peak.

```ts
import { totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import {
  DEEPSEEK_DEFAULT_PRICING,
  DEEPSEEK_OFF_PEAK_PRICING,
  DeepSeekSDK,
} from "@warlock.js/ai-deepseek";

const deepseek = new DeepSeekSDK({ apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ?? "" });
DEEPSEEK_DEFAULT_PRICING["deepseek-flash"]; // { input: 0.3, output: 1.2, cachedInput: 0.006 } — peak

const offPeak = new DeepSeekSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ?? "",
  pricing: DEEPSEEK_OFF_PEAK_PRICING, // { input: 0.15, output: 0.6, cachedInput: 0.003 } for flash
});

const { usage } = await offPeak
  .model({ name: "deepseek-v4-pro" })
  .complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }]);
console.log(usage.cachedTokens, totalCost(usage.cost));
```

Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` > SDK `pricing` registry > built-in DeepSeek default > `undefined`.

- **Source.** https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing, fetched 2026-10-17. Covered: `deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-flash` (its legacy name, same rate) and `deepseek-v4-pro`.
- **Unpriced:** `deepseek-chat` / `deepseek-reasoner` are gone from the price list (announced for discontinuation on 2026-07-24) — pass `pricing` if a gateway still serves them.
- **Usage semantics.** DeepSeek's `prompt_tokens` equals cache hits + misses and `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` mirrors `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`, so the usage is `inputIncludesCache: true` and hits bill at `cachedInput`. DeepSeek caches automatically on disk and takes no request hint, so `promptCacheKey` is never sent.

## Errors

Raw errors surface through the wrapped OpenAI adapter's wrapper into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy — see the `handle-ai-errors` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill. DeepSeek documents 503 as "Server Overloaded" (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/error_codes); it maps to `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`). Every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"`).

## When NOT to use this skill

- OpenAI / Azure OpenAI / OpenRouter / local OpenAI-compatible gateways — use `@warlock.js/ai-openai`.
- Anthropic — `@warlock.js/ai-anthropic`. Gemini — `@warlock.js/ai-google`. Ollama — `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`.
- Calling the DeepSeek HTTP API or the raw `openai` SDK directly without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.

## See also

- The `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill — the wrapped adapter; all wire-level behavior.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — passing the model into `ai.agent({...})`.
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — adapter comparison.

## Provider body options and token estimates

This adapter delegates Chat Completions to the OpenAI adapter, so
`providerOptions.openai.body` adds native Chat request fields. Other provider
keys are ignored. Plain-object fields merge one level deep with neutral options;
caller-provided keys win, while arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field.
The OpenAI adapter's protected conversation, tool and transport fields remain
protected here too. Send only fields supported by this provider; do not reuse
OpenAI-only bodies across a mixed-provider fallback chain.

Models from this adapter have no native `countTokens` method. Check
`model.countTokens` before using an optional native counting capability;
`sdk.count(text)` is a separate offline estimate.

# `@warlock.js/ai-groq`

Provider adapter for **Groq** — open models (Llama, GPT-OSS, DeepSeek-R1 distill) served fast on Groq's LPU hardware. Groq speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol, so this package is a **thin wrapper over `@warlock.js/ai-openai`**: it owns an internal `OpenAISDK` pointed at Groq's endpoint and delegates the wire work, while injecting Groq's own capability inference and default pricing. Pair with `@warlock.js/ai` for the agent / tool / system-prompt surface.

## Construction

```ts
import { GroqSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-groq";

// Common path — apiKey only. baseURL + provider default to Groq.
const groq = new GroqSDK({ apiKey: process.env.GROQ_API_KEY! });
```

`baseURL` defaults to `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1` (Groq's **OpenAI-compatible endpoint**) — override only to route through a proxy/gateway. `provider` defaults to `"groq"` and flows through to `ModelContract.provider`, `AgentReport.model.provider`, and logs.

`GroqSDK` is a class (not a factory) — it holds a long-lived internal `OpenAISDK` and aligns with the other adapter entry points. Every upstream `openai` `ClientOptions` field (`timeout`, `maxRetries`, `defaultHeaders`, `fetch`, …) is forwarded verbatim to that inner client.

## Producing a model

```ts
groq.model({ name: "llama-3.3-70b-versatile" }); // flagship general-purpose text
groq.model({ name: "llama-3.1-8b-instant" }); // fastest / cheapest small text
groq.model({ name: "openai/gpt-oss-120b" }); // vision + reasoning auto-true
groq.model({ name: "deepseek-r1-distill-llama-70b" }); // reasoning auto-true
```

Returns a `ModelContract` you pass straight into `ai.agent({ model })`. `name` is the Groq-hosted **open-weight** id (the upstream name, e.g. `openai/gpt-oss-120b`), NOT an OpenAI id. Any current Groq model id works — the list above is curated, not an allow-list.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

The whole reason this wrapper exists: Groq's ids aren't OpenAI's, so the OpenAI adapter's prefix inference would never fire. `GroqSDK` carries its **own** name lists.

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vision`           | Inferred from the Groq model id. `true` for `gpt-oss`, `llama-4`, `llama-3.2-*-vision`; `false` otherwise (e.g. `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `llama-3.1-8b-instant`).              |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from the Groq model id. `true` for `gpt-oss`, `deepseek-r1` / `deepseek-r1-distill`, `qwq`, `qwen3`; `false` otherwise. Drives whether `reasoning_effort` is forwarded. |
| `structuredOutput` | `true` — Groq accepts OpenAI-style `response_format`.                                                                                                                            |
| `promptCaching`    | Inherited from the inner OpenAI adapter (`true`; read-side `cachedTokens` accounting).                                                                                           |

**Override `vision`, `reasoning`, or `structuredOutput` explicitly** via `.model({ name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput? })` — an explicit value always wins over inference.

```ts
groq.model({ name: "some-custom-llama", vision: true }); // force on for an unlisted multimodal id
groq.model({ name: "openai/gpt-oss-120b", reasoning: false }); // pin off
```

## Reasoning (gpt-oss / deepseek-r1 distill)

Reasoning models accept a discrete effort knob, forwarded by the inner adapter as OpenAI's `reasoning_effort`:

```ts
const model = groq.model({ name: "deepseek-r1-distill-llama-70b" }); // reasoning auto-true
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } }); // → reasoning_effort: "high"
```

- `reasoning.effort` (`"low" | "medium" | "high"`) maps verbatim.
- `reasoning.maxTokens` has no Chat Completions equivalent and is ignored (same as the OpenAI adapter).
- When `capabilities.reasoning` is `false` (e.g. `llama-3.3-70b-versatile`), the option is dropped — never sent as an unsupported param.

## Structured output & streaming

Inherited unchanged from `@warlock.js/ai-openai`: a `responseSchema` maps to `response_format: json_schema` (strict) when the schema is a proper root object, else loose `json_object`; `model.stream()` drains the streaming Chat Completions response and yields `delta` / `tool-call` / `done` chunks with `include_usage` on. See the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill for the full wire behavior.

## Embeddings — not available on Groq

As of mid-2026 Groq exposes **no** OpenAI-compatible embeddings endpoint. `groq.embedder({ name })` constructs (delegated to the inner adapter) but a live `.embed()` call fails at the provider. Use `@warlock.js/ai-openai` or `@warlock.js/ai-google` for retrieval embeddings.

There is also no image-generation API on Groq, so `GroqSDK` intentionally does **not** define `image()` — `ai.groq.image(...)` is a compile-time error (structural capability guard, like Anthropic / Bedrock / Ollama).

## Pricing — per-model registry + built-in defaults

`pricing` is a registry keyed by model name, rates in **USD per 1,000,000 tokens** (`ModelPricing`: `input`, `output`, optional `cachedInput`). The adapter ships **built-in default rates** (`GROQ_DEFAULT_PRICING`) as the final fallback.

```ts
import { totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { GROQ_DEFAULT_PRICING, GroqSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-groq";

const groq = new GroqSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.GROQ_API_KEY ?? "",
  pricing: {
    // No public price for Llama on Groq — use your contract rate.
    "llama-3.3-70b-versatile": { input: 0.59, output: 0.79 },
  },
});

GROQ_DEFAULT_PRICING["openai/gpt-oss-120b"]; // { input: 0.15, output: 0.6, cachedInput: 0.075 }

const { usage } = await groq
  .model({ name: "openai/gpt-oss-120b" })
  .complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }]);
console.log(totalCost(usage.cost));
```

Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` (`groq.model({ name, pricing })`) > SDK `pricing[name]` > `GROQ_DEFAULT_PRICING` > `undefined` (no cost computed).

- **Source.** https://console.groq.com/docs/models (groq.com/pricing now redirects to the home page), fetched 2026-10-17: `openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`, `openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b`, `qwen/qwen3.8-27b`. Cached input is 50% of the input rate for the gpt-oss models, the only ones Groq caches — automatically, with no write charge and no request hint (https://console.groq.com/docs/prompt-caching).
- **Unpriced:** the Llama models (listed as "Enterprise – Contact Sales", no public price) and anything else not listed — supply your own rate.

## Token counting

```ts
await groq.count("some text"); // approximate heuristic (delegated), not a real tokenizer
```

Good for budgeting; not for billing.

## Errors

Raw errors are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy by the inner OpenAI adapter's error wrapper (dispatch keys on `status + code`). See the `handle-ai-errors` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill. HTTP 503 maps to `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`); every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"`). Note Groq's documented OpenAI-compat gaps — `n` must be `1`, and `logprobs` / `logit_bias` / `top_logprobs` / `messages[].name` are unsupported.

## When NOT to use this skill

- Embeddings or image generation — Groq has neither; use `@warlock.js/ai-openai` / `@warlock.js/ai-google`.
- OpenAI / Azure / OpenRouter — use `@warlock.js/ai-openai` (`setup-openai`); this wraps it but for Groq specifically.
- Anthropic — `@warlock.js/ai-anthropic`. Bedrock — `@warlock.js/ai-bedrock`. Gemini — `@warlock.js/ai-google`. Local Ollama — `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`.

## See also

- The `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill — the wrapped adapter; full wire / streaming / structured-output detail
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — passing the model into `ai.agent({...})`
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — adapter comparison

## Provider body options and token estimates

This adapter delegates Chat Completions to the OpenAI adapter, so
`providerOptions.openai.body` adds native Chat request fields. Other provider
keys are ignored. Plain-object fields merge one level deep with neutral options;
caller-provided keys win, while arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field.
The OpenAI adapter's protected conversation, tool and transport fields remain
protected here too. Send only fields supported by this provider; do not reuse
OpenAI-only bodies across a mixed-provider fallback chain.

Models from this adapter have no native `countTokens` method. Check
`model.countTokens` before using an optional native counting capability;
`sdk.count(text)` is a separate offline estimate.

name: setup-mistral
description: 'Wire @warlock.js/ai-mistral — new MistralSDK({apiKey, baseURL?, provider?, pricing?}) for Mistral AI, a thin wrapper over the OpenAI adapter that uses Mistral''s OpenAI-compatible endpoint (https://api.mistral.ai/v1). .model({name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput?, responseFormat?, pdf?, audio?}) for a ModelContract with Mistral-aware capabilities (vision auto-inferred for the pixtral family, reasoning for the magistral family + hybrid mistral-small), .embedder({name, dimensions?}) for mistral-embed via /v1/embeddings. # `@warlock.js/ai-mistral`

Provider adapter for Mistral AI. Mistral exposes an **OpenAI-compatible** API, so `MistralSDK` is a **thin wrapper** over `@warlock.js/ai-openai` (the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill) — it does not re-implement the wire protocol, streaming, tool calls, structured output, error wrapping, or token accounting. It builds one internal `OpenAISDK` pointed at Mistral's `baseURL` with `provider: "mistral"`, then layers on this provider's own capability inference + default pricing. Pair with `@warlock.js/ai` for the agent / tool / system-prompt surface.

## Construction

```ts
import { MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({ apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY! });
```

`baseURL` defaults to `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` (the OpenAI-compatible endpoint serving `/chat/completions` and `/embeddings`). `provider` defaults to `"mistral"` and flows through to `ModelContract.provider`, `AgentReport.model.provider`, and logs. Override `baseURL` only to reach a Mistral-compatible gateway/proxy. Every other upstream OpenAI `ClientOptions` value (`timeout`, `maxRetries`, `defaultHeaders`, `fetch`, …) is forwarded verbatim.

## Producing a model

```ts
mistral.model({ name: "mistral-large-latest" }); // multimodal flagship
mistral.model({ name: "magistral-medium-latest" }); // reasoning
mistral.model({ name: "pixtral-large-latest" }); // vision
mistral.model({ name: "some-fine-tune", vision: true }); // explicit capability override
```

Returns a `ModelContract` you pass straight into `ai.agent({ model })`.

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

The wrapper injects **Mistral-aware** inference before delegating to the OpenAI adapter (the OpenAI prefix lists never match Mistral names):

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vision`           | Inferred from the model name. `true` for the `pixtral` family and the recent multimodal generations (`mistral-large`, `mistral-medium`, `ministral-3`); `false` otherwise.    |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from the model name. `true` for the `magistral` family and the hybrid `mistral-small` generation; `false` otherwise. Drives whether `reasoning_effort` is forwarded. |
| `structuredOutput` | `true`, unless `responseFormat` is forced to `"json_object"` / `"text"` (loose modes).                                                                                        |
| `promptCaching`    | `true` (inherited from the OpenAI adapter — read-side `cachedTokens` accounting).                                                                                             |
| `pdf` / `audio`    | `false` by default (opt-in `.model({ pdf: true })` / `{ audio: true }`).                                                                                                      |

**Override any flag explicitly** via `.model({ name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput?, responseFormat?, pdf?, audio? })` — an explicit value always wins over inference. The known-family fragments live in `known-models.ts` (`inferVisionCapability`, `inferReasoningCapability`).

The headline `-latest` aliases are exported as `MISTRAL_MODELS` ({ chat, vision, reasoning, embedding }) for convenience — `mistral.model()` also accepts any version-pinned id (`mistral-large-2512`, `magistral-medium-2509`).

## Uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint

Because Mistral speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions + Embeddings protocol, everything the OpenAI adapter does applies unchanged: streaming deltas + consolidated tool calls, `response_format: json_schema` structured output (override per model with `responseFormat`), `reasoning_effort` for reasoning models, multipart image input, and the neutral `Usage` breakdown (`input` / `output` / `cachedTokens` / `reasoningTokens`). See `@warlock.js/ai-openai` (the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill) for the wire-level detail — it is identical here.

**No image generation.** Mistral has no OpenAI-compatible image endpoint, so `MistralSDK` intentionally does **not** expose `image()` — the structural absence is the capability guard (`ai.mistral.image(...)` is a compile-time error).

## Embeddings

```ts
const embedder = mistral.embedder({ name: "mistral-embed" });

const { vector, dimensions, usage } = await embedder.embed("Hello world");
const { vectors } = await embedder.embedMany(["doc 1", "doc 2"]);
```

`mistral-embed` is reachable through the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings`; the embedder delegates to the wrapped OpenAI embedder.

## Pricing — per-model registry

The adapter ships a default registry (`MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING`, USD per 1,000,000 tokens, with the 10%-of-input cache rate as `cachedInput`) so cost truth works out of the box, on agent reports and on each `model.complete()` / streaming `done` usage. Pass your own `pricing` to win per model id:

```ts
import { totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING, MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY ?? "",
  pricing: {
    // USD per 1M tokens — contract rates win over the defaults.
    "mistral-large-latest": { input: 0.45, output: 1.35, cachedInput: 0.045 },
  },
});

MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING["mistral-small-latest"]; // { input: 0.15, output: 0.6, cachedInput: 0.015 }

const { usage } = await mistral
  .model({ name: "mistral-medium-latest" })
  .complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }]);
console.log(totalCost(usage.cost));
```

Resolution at `model()` time: per-model `pricing` (`mistral.model({ name, pricing })`) > SDK-level `pricing` > `MISTRAL_DEFAULT_PRICING` > `undefined`.

- **Source.** https://docs.mistral.ai/inference/pricing plus the model pages under https://docs.mistral.ai/models (API ids and aliases), fetched 2026-10-17. Covered: `mistral-large-latest` / `mistral-large-2512`, `mistral-medium-latest` / `mistral-medium-3-5`, `mistral-small-latest` / `mistral-small-2603`, `ministral-14b-latest` / `ministral-14b-2512`, `codestral-latest` / `codestral-2508`, `mistral-embed` / `mistral-embed-2312`.
- **Not included:** Mistral Large 4 (public preview at a temporary sale price) and the retired Pixtral / Magistral models (no longer on the price list) — pass `pricing` if you still call them.

## Prompt caching

Mistral's Chat Completions accepts `prompt_cache_key` (https://docs.mistral.ai/studio/conversations/advanced/prompt-caching). Set `promptCacheKey` on the model to route related requests to the same cache; it is sent while the SDK keeps its default `"mistral"` provider label. Cached tokens come back as `usage.cachedTokens` (inside `prompt_tokens`, so `inputIncludesCache: true`) and bill at `cachedInput`.

```ts
import { MistralSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-mistral";

const mistral = new MistralSDK({ apiKey: process.env.MISTRAL_API_KEY ?? "" });
const model = mistral.model({ name: "mistral-large-latest", promptCacheKey: "conversation:42" });
```

## Errors

Raw errors are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy by the wrapped OpenAI adapter (dispatch keys on `APIError.status + code`) — see the `handle-ai-errors` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill. HTTP 503 (and OpenAI's `server_is_overloaded` code) maps to `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`); every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"`).

## When NOT to use this skill

- Image generation — Mistral has no OpenAI-compatible image endpoint; `mistral.image()` does not exist.
- Other providers — OpenAI `@warlock.js/ai-openai`, Gemini `@warlock.js/ai-google`, Anthropic `@warlock.js/ai-anthropic`, Bedrock `@warlock.js/ai-bedrock`, Ollama `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`.
- Raw `@mistralai/mistralai` SDK or Vercel `@ai-sdk/mistral` without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.

## See also

- The `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill — the wrapped adapter; identical wire behavior.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — passing the model into `ai.agent({...})`.
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — adapter comparison.

## Provider body options and token estimates

This adapter delegates Chat Completions to the OpenAI adapter, so
`providerOptions.openai.body` adds native Chat request fields. Other provider
keys are ignored. Plain-object fields merge one level deep with neutral options;
caller-provided keys win, while arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field.
The OpenAI adapter's protected conversation, tool and transport fields remain
protected here too. Send only fields supported by this provider; do not reuse
OpenAI-only bodies across a mixed-provider fallback chain.

Models from this adapter have no native `countTokens` method. Check
`model.countTokens` before using an optional native counting capability;
`sdk.count(text)` is a separate offline estimate.

# Warlock AI Xai — full skills

## setup-xai  `@warlock.js/ai-xai/setup-xai/SKILL.md`

name: setup-xai
description: 'Wire @warlock.js/ai-xai — new XaiSDK({apiKey, baseURL?, provider?, pricing?}) for xAI Grok, .model({name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput?}) for a ModelContract, .embedder({name, dimensions?}) and .image({name, pricing?}) delegated to the OpenAI-compatible adapter. Thin wrapper over OpenAISDK: uses the xAI OpenAI-compatible endpoint (https://api.x.ai/v1) and injects xAI''s own vision/reasoning inference so Grok names resolve to the right capabilities. # `@warlock.js/ai-xai`

Provider adapter for xAI's **Grok** models. xAI speaks the OpenAI Chat Completions protocol, so `XaiSDK` is a **thin wrapper** over `OpenAISDK` (the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill) — it does not reimplement the wire layer. It constructs one internal `OpenAISDK` pointed at xAI's `baseURL` and labeled `provider: "xai"`, then delegates `model()` / `embedder()` / `image()` / `count()`, injecting xAI's own capability inference so Grok model names resolve correctly. Pair with `@warlock.js/ai` for the agent / tool / system-prompt surface.

## Construction

```ts
import { XaiSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-xai";

const xai = new XaiSDK({ apiKey: process.env.XAI_API_KEY! });
```

- `baseURL` defaults to `https://api.x.ai/v1` (the xAI OpenAI-compatible endpoint). Override only to target a proxy/gateway.
- `provider` defaults to `"xai"` — flows through to `ModelContract.provider`, `AgentReport.model.provider`, and logs. Set it to relabel a gateway upstream.
- Every other upstream `ClientOptions` value (`timeout`, `maxRetries`, `defaultHeaders`, `fetch`, …) is forwarded verbatim to the wrapped client.

`XaiSDK` is a class (not a factory) — it holds a long-lived wrapped `OpenAISDK` (which holds a long-lived `OpenAI` client). Construct one per account and reuse it.

## Producing a model

```ts
xai.model({ name: "grok-4" }); // vision + reasoning auto-true
xai.model({ name: "grok-3-mini" }); // reasoning auto-true, vision false
xai.model({ name: "grok-2-vision" }); // vision auto-true
xai.model({ name: "grok-4", temperature: 0.2 }); // sampling controls
xai.model({ name: "grok-3", vision: true }); // explicit capability override
```

Returns a `ModelContract` you pass straight into `ai.agent({ model })`.

## Models & capabilities — what's auto-set

This adapter ships xAI's OWN name lists (Grok ids don't match OpenAI's `gpt-*` / `o*` prefixes). Capabilities are injected per model before delegating; an explicit value always wins over inference.

| Model           | `vision` | `reasoning`                |
| --------------- | -------- | -------------------------- |
| `grok-4`        | true     | true (reasoning-first)     |
| `grok-3`        | false    | false                      |
| `grok-3-mini`   | false    | true (the "think" variant) |
| `grok-2-vision` | true     | false                      |
| `grok-2`        | false    | false                      |

- `vision` — inferred `true` for the `grok-4` and `grok-2-vision` prefixes; `false` otherwise.
- `reasoning` — inferred `true` for `grok-4` and `grok-3-mini`; drives whether `reasoning.effort` is forwarded as `reasoning_effort` on the wire.
- `structuredOutput` / `promptCaching` and the image/PDF/audio wire mapping all come from the wrapped OpenAI adapter unchanged — see the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill.

**Override `vision`, `reasoning`, or `structuredOutput` explicitly** via `.model({ name, vision?, reasoning?, structuredOutput? })`.

> Model availability changes over time — pass any current Grok id through `.model({ name })`; the prefix inference covers dated / `-latest` / `-fast` / `-beta` variants. Don't assume a model exists; check xAI's docs.

## Reasoning (grok-4 / grok-3-mini)

```ts
const model = xai.model({ name: "grok-4" }); // reasoning auto-true
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } }); // → reasoning_effort: "high"
```

`reasoning.effort` (`"low" | "medium" | "high"`) maps verbatim to the OpenAI-compatible `reasoning_effort` param. When `capabilities.reasoning` is `false` (e.g. `grok-3`), the option is dropped — the adapter never forwards it. Pin `reasoning: true` to force it for a custom/gateway id.

## Multipart messages (image input)

Image attachments reach the wire only on a vision-capable model (`grok-4`, `grok-2-vision`); the agent's modality gate throws otherwise. Mapping to OpenAI `image_url` parts is identical to the OpenAI adapter — see the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill.

## Uses the OpenAI-compatible endpoint

All wire work — request/response mapping, streaming, tool-call accumulation, structured output, usage extraction — is the wrapped `OpenAISDK`'s, unchanged. The wrapper only: (1) sets the xAI `baseURL` + `provider` defaults, and (2) injects xAI's vision/reasoning inference per model. For streaming, structured output, and the full multipart surface, read the `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill.

## Embeddings — not available on xAI

```ts
xai.embedder({ name: "text-embedding-3-small" }); // delegates, but xAI has no embeddings API yet
```

xAI does **not** currently expose a public embeddings endpoint. `embedder()` is wired for protocol parity, but a call to `embed()` / `embedMany()` fails upstream. Point an embedder at a dedicated provider (e.g. `@warlock.js/ai-openai`) for vectors.

## Image generation — delegated guard

`image()` delegates to the wrapped OpenAI Images adapter, which only recognizes `gpt-image-*` / `dall-e-*` ids and rejects anything else at construction. xAI's image generation ("Grok Imagine") is a separate, non-OpenAI-Images-compatible surface, so use `@warlock.js/ai-openai`'s `image()` for OpenAI-Images generation.

## Pricing — per-model registry

xAI ships **no built-in price table**: every Grok model on https://docs.x.ai/developers/pricing (checked 2026-10-17) bills all tokens at a higher long-context rate once the prompt reaches 200k tokens, which a flat `ModelPricing` cannot express. Pass the rates you use (USD per 1,000,000 tokens; `ModelPricing`: `input`, `output`, optional `cachedInput`). xAI has no cache-write charge. Resolution: per-model `pricing` > SDK registry > `undefined` (no cost computed).

```ts
import { ai, totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { XaiSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-xai";

const xai = new XaiSDK({
  apiKey: process.env.XAI_API_KEY ?? "",
  pricing: {
    // Below-200k rates from xAI's pricing page; long prompts cost more.
    "grok-4.3": { input: 1.25, output: 2.5, cachedInput: 0.2 },
  },
});

const { usage } = await ai.agent({ model: xai.model({ name: "grok-4.3" }) }).execute("hi");
console.log(totalCost(usage.cost)); // undefined when unpriced
```

`usage` follows OpenAI semantics (`prompt_tokens` includes the cached tokens, `inputIncludesCache: true`), and `usage.cost` is attached to every `model.complete()` / streaming `done` once the model is priced.

## Prompt caching

xAI's Chat Completions accepts `prompt_cache_key`, routed as the `x-grok-conv-id` cache key (https://docs.x.ai/developers/advanced-api-usage/prompt-caching/maximizing-cache-hits). Set `promptCacheKey` on the model — sent while the SDK keeps its default `"xai"` provider label — to keep a conversation's requests on the same cache:

```ts
import { XaiSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-xai";

const xai = new XaiSDK({ apiKey: process.env.XAI_API_KEY ?? "" });
const model = xai.model({ name: "grok-4.3", promptCacheKey: "conversation:42" });
```

OpenAI's `prompt_cache_retention` and explicit breakpoints are never sent to xAI.

## Errors

Raw xAI / OpenAI-SDK errors are wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy by the wrapped adapter's error wrapper (dispatch keys on `APIError.status + code`). See the `handle-ai-errors` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill. HTTP 503 (and OpenAI's `server_is_overloaded` code) maps to `ProviderOverloadedError` (`code: "PROVIDER_OVERLOADED"`, `retryable: true`); every wrapped error carries `status`, `retryable` and `billed` (`false` for 401 / 402 / 403, otherwise `"unknown"`).

## When NOT to use this skill

- Direct calls to the `openai` SDK pointed at `api.x.ai` by hand — without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.
- Non-Grok models — OpenAI: `@warlock.js/ai-openai`. Anthropic: `@warlock.js/ai-anthropic`. Gemini: `@warlock.js/ai-google`. Ollama: `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`.

## See also

- The `setup-openai` topic of the `warlock-js-ai-openai` skill — the wrapped adapter; full wire / streaming / structured-output / multipart surface
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — passing the model into `ai.agent({...})`
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — adapter comparison

## Provider body options and token estimates

This adapter delegates Chat Completions to the OpenAI adapter, so
`providerOptions.openai.body` adds native Chat request fields. Other provider
keys are ignored. Plain-object fields merge one level deep with neutral options;
caller-provided keys win, while arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field.
The OpenAI adapter's protected conversation, tool and transport fields remain
protected here too. Send only fields supported by this provider; do not reuse
OpenAI-only bodies across a mixed-provider fallback chain.

Models from this adapter have no native `countTokens` method. Check
`model.countTokens` before using an optional native counting capability;
`sdk.count(text)` is a separate offline estimate.

## Native web search requires Responses

[xAI's official web-search guide](https://docs.x.ai/developers/tools/web-search)
(verified 2026-10-18) sends `{ type: "web_search" }` to `POST /v1/responses`.
`XaiSDK` currently wraps Chat Completions, so native `web_search` and `x_search`
provider tools are explicitly unsupported and throw `InvalidRequestError`
before transport, explaining that the vendor's Responses API is required.
Use xAI's own Responses SDK for native search. The framework's
`api: "responses"` adapter remains direct-OpenAI-only; passing a tool definition
does not change this transport. No xAI hosted-search request count or list fee
is guessed. See [compatible native search](https://warlock.js.org/v/latest/ai/providers/openai-compatible/#xai).

## setup-ollama  `@warlock.js/ai-ollama/setup-ollama/SKILL.md`

---
name: setup-ollama
description: 'Wire @warlock.js/ai-ollama — new OllamaSDK({host?, headers?}) for local / self-hosted Ollama via the official ollama client (not OpenAI-compat). chat + embed, daemon-down error handling. .model({name, vision?, reasoning?}) with cost-truth capabilities — reasoning inferred from thinking-model tags (deepseek-r1/qwq/qwen3/gpt-oss…), promptCaching/audio/pdf honestly false; options.reasoning → Ollama native `think` flag; usage reasoningTokens/cachedTokens stay undefined (none reported). # `@warlock.js/ai-ollama`

Provider adapter that turns a local (or self-hosted) Ollama server into a vendor-neutral `ModelContract`, plus an Ollama embedder. Uses the **official `ollama` npm package** (not OpenAI-compat). Mirrors the openai / anthropic / bedrock / google adapters.

## Construction

```ts
import { OllamaSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-ollama";

const ollama = new OllamaSDK(); // local default host
const remote = new OllamaSDK({ host: "http://gpu-box.internal:11434" });
const gated = new OllamaSDK({
  host: "https://ollama.internal",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.OLLAMA_TOKEN}` },
});
```

`OllamaSDK` is a class with a long-lived `Ollama` client. Config is `Partial<Config>` (host defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:11434`) + `provider` (default `"ollama"`) + optional `pricing` (local is free; kept for parity/chargeback).

## Producing a model

```ts
ollama.model({ name: "llama3.1" });
ollama.model({ name: "qwen2.5:14b", temperature: 0.2 });
ollama.model({ name: "llama3.2-vision", maxTokens: 1024 });
```

## Capabilities — what's auto-set

| Flag               | Default                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `structuredOutput` | `true` (via Ollama's native `format` JSON-schema field)                                                                                                                                                   |
| `vision`           | Inferred from model tag substring. `true` for `llava`, `bakllava`, `*-vision`, `moondream`, `minicpm-v`, `qwen2-vl`, `qwen2.5-vl`, `llama4`, `gemma3`; `false` otherwise.                                 |
| `reasoning`        | Inferred from model tag substring. `true` for `deepseek-r1`, `qwq`, `qwen3`, `magistral`, `phi4-reasoning`, `phi4-mini-reasoning`, `cogito`, `smallthinker`, `exaone-deep`, `gpt-oss`; `false` otherwise. |
| `promptCaching`    | `false` — Ollama has no provider-side prompt cache.                                                                                                                                                       |
| `audio` / `pdf`    | `false` — the Ollama chat API takes no audio / PDF content parts.                                                                                                                                         |

Explicit config always wins (`vision`, `structuredOutput`, `reasoning` overrides on `ollama.model({ … })`).

## Reasoning / thinking

For thinking-capable families the adapter maps `ModelCallOptions.reasoning` onto Ollama's `think` request flag (`boolean | 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'`):

```ts
ollama.model({ name: "deepseek-r1:7b" });
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" } }); // → chat({ think: "high" })
await model.complete(messages, { reasoning: { maxTokens: 2048 } }); // → chat({ think: true })
```

- `reasoning.effort` (`low` / `medium` / `high`) passes straight through to `think`.
- `reasoning.maxTokens` (the thinking-budget hint) has **no Ollama equivalent** — the daemon takes no thinking-token cap, so it only acts as the on/off signal (`think: true`) and is otherwise ignored.
- The `think` flag is sent **only** to a `reasoning`-capable model; on a plain instruct model `reasoning` options are a no-op (no `think` is sent).
- Set `ollama.model({ name, reasoning: false })` to force it off, or `reasoning: true` to force it on for a tag the substring list doesn't recognize.

`ModelCallOptions.cacheControl` is a **no-op** — Ollama has no prompt cache, so there is no breakpoint to place.

## System prompt & roles

Unlike Anthropic/Gemini/Bedrock, **Ollama keeps a first-class `system` role inside `messages`** — no hoisting. Neutral roles (`system`/`user`/`assistant`/`tool`) pass straight through.

## Tool calls

- Outgoing: neutral tools → `{ type: "function", function: { name, description, parameters } }`.
- Assistant tool calls → `tool_calls: [{ function: { name, arguments } }]` (Ollama has **no tool-call id**).
- Tool results (`role: "tool"`) → a `tool` message with `tool_name` set from `toolCallId` (Ollama matches a result to its call by name).

**Synthesized ids.** Because Ollama tool calls carry no id, the adapter sets neutral `id` = tool name. **Parallel calls to the same tool in one turn share an id** — a documented v1 limitation. Ollama reports `done_reason: "stop"` even when it called a tool; the adapter derives `finishReason: "tool_calls"` from tool-call presence.

## Structured output

Object-root `responseSchema` + `structuredOutput`-capable → `chat({ format: <schema> })` (Ollama's `format` accepts a JSON Schema object).

## Multipart messages (vision)

A multipart user message collapses to a single `content` string + an `images` array of **base64 strings**. `{ type: "image", source: { url } }` → **throws `InvalidRequestError`** (Ollama cannot fetch remote URLs). Resolve images to base64 first.

## Streaming

`model.stream()` drains `chat({ stream: true })` (an `AbortableAsyncIterator`). Each chunk's `message.content` → `{ type: "delta" }`; `message.tool_calls` are emitted as `{ type: "tool-call" }` **fully formed**. Terminal `{ type: "done", finishReason, usage }` — usage from the final (`done: true`) chunk's `prompt_eval_count` / `eval_count`.

Opt-in (`options.streamChunks`, set by `agent.stream()`): `{ type: "reasoning", delta }` per `message.thinking` piece when `think` is on:

```ts
for await (const chunk of model.stream(messages, { reasoning: { effort: "high" }, streamChunks: { reasoning: true } })) {
  if (chunk.type === "reasoning") process.stderr.write(chunk.delta);
}
```

Ollama's chat API has no built-in tools: an `ai.providerTool()` for another provider is left out with a warning.

**`options.signal` is honored** on `stream()` and `complete()`: a pre-aborted signal rejects without sending, and aborting mid-call cancels the HTTP request. The `ollama` client has no per-request signal, so `OllamaSDK` wraps its `fetch` (yours, when you pass `fetch`) to apply each call's signal from async context; the stream iterator's `abort()` is called too.

## Finish-reason mapping

`stop` → `stop` · `length` → `length` · `load` / unknown / null → `error`. `tool_calls` derived from tool-call presence.

## Embeddings

```ts
const embedder = ollama.embedder({ name: "nomic-embed-text" });
const { vector } = await embedder.embed("Hello world");
const { vectors } = await embedder.embedMany(["a", "b"]); // single batched call
const truncated = ollama.embedder({ name: "mxbai-embed-large", dimensions: 512 });
```

`client.embed` accepts a string array natively, so `embedMany` is **one request** (like the Gemini adapter). Usage comes from `prompt_eval_count` (reported as both `promptTokens` and `totalTokens`). Local Ollama runs without a prompt cache, so model usage has no `cachedTokens`.

`dimensions` is optional. When set it's forwarded as Ollama's `dimensions` truncation field (newer embedding models) and seeds `embedder.dimensions`; when omitted, `embedder.dimensions` starts at `0` and is resolved lazily from the first response's vector length, then cached.

## Errors

Wrapped into the typed `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` hierarchy. The `ollama` client throws an internal `ResponseError` (`status_code` + message); transport failures surface as `fetch` `TypeError` with `ECONNREFUSED` cause:

- **Daemon-down (`ECONNREFUSED` / "fetch failed") → `ProviderError`** (operational "is Ollama running?", not a request defect)
- Timeouts → `ProviderTimeoutError`
- 401/403 → `ProviderAuthError`
- 429 → `ProviderRateLimitError`
- 4xx with context phrasing → `ContextLengthExceededError`, else `InvalidRequestError`
- 5xx → `ProviderError`

## Token counting & usage (cost-truth)

```ts
await ollama.count("some text"); // approximate heuristic, offline
```

Per-call `Usage` comes from the chat response's `prompt_eval_count` (→ `input`) and `eval_count` (→ `output`); `total` is their sum. The adapter reports usage **truthfully** — it never fabricates a field Ollama doesn't return:

- `cachedTokens` / `cacheWriteTokens` — **always undefined**. Ollama has no provider prompt cache, so there is no cache-hit or cache-write accounting (honest absence, not a false `0`).
- `reasoningTokens` — **always undefined**. Reasoning models emit their thinking as the `message.thinking` _string_, but the wire format carries **no separate reasoning-token count** — those tokens are already folded into `eval_count`. The adapter does not estimate a count from the thinking text.
- `cost` — attached to each `complete()` / streaming `done` usage only when a `ModelPricing` is configured. The adapter ships no price table (a local model costs nothing per token), so it is usually undefined; set `pricing` for chargeback or a hosted Ollama endpoint.
- `inputIncludesCache` — left unset: with no cache counters there is nothing to include or exclude.

```ts
import { totalCost } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { OllamaSDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-ollama";

const ollama = new OllamaSDK({ pricing: { "llama3.2": { input: 0.05, output: 0.1 } } }); // internal chargeback rate
const { usage } = await ollama
  .model({ name: "llama3.2" })
  .complete([{ role: "user", content: "hi" }]);
console.log(totalCost(usage.cost));
```

## Provider body options

Native body fields merge after neutral options. When both values are plain
objects, their immediate keys merge and caller-provided keys win; untouched
neutral fields remain. Arrays, scalars and `null` replace the field. This merge
is one level deep: a nested object explicitly supplied by the caller replaces
that nested value.

`providerOptions.ollama.body` adds native chat request fields after neutral
options, for completion and streaming:

```ts
await model.complete(messages, {
  providerOptions: { ollama: { body: { keep_alive: "10m", options: { top_k: 4 } } } },
});
```

The key stays `ollama` for custom provider labels. Other provider keys are
ignored. `OllamaCallOptions` is exported. `model`, `messages`, `tools` and `stream`
are protected; replacing them throws `InvalidRequestError`. Fields merge
shallowly: a provider `options` object replaces the generated inference options,
so include any neutral sampling settings you want to retain in that object.

Ollama's chat transport has no native preflight token-count endpoint, so its
model has no `countTokens` method. `sdk.count(text)` remains an offline estimate.

## When NOT to use this skill

- Direct `ollama` client calls without going through `@warlock.js/ai` agents.
- OpenAI / Anthropic / Bedrock / Google models — those have their own adapter packages.
- An OpenAI-compatible Ollama gateway you specifically want to drive through the OpenAI protocol — use `@warlock.js/ai-openai` with `baseURL` instead.

## See also

- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill
- The `pick-ai-provider` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill
- The `embed-text` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill

## use-ai-live  `@warlock.js/ai-live/use-ai-live/SKILL.md`

---
name: use-ai-live
description: 'Live & generative rich-media add-on for @warlock.js/ai. A side-effect import `import "@warlock.js/ai-live"` mounts two heavy modalities onto the shared `ai.*` facade: `ai.video({ model, prompt })` — text-to-video (Sora / Veo / Kling-class), the async submit→poll job hidden behind the same uniform never-throws `{ data, error, usage, report }` envelope as `ai.image`, with per-second cost-truth folded into `Usage.cost`; and `ai.realtime({ transport, model })` — a stateful duplex VOICE SESSION over a pluggable `RealtimeTransport` (sendAudio / sendText / events() / close()→RealtimeReport).
