Skip: still-image OUTPUT — [[generate-images]]; text-to-speech / transcription (one-shot audio, not a session) — [[generate-speech]]; chat agents / tools / workflows — the `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill.'
---

# Live rich-media — `ai.video` + `ai.realtime` (`@warlock.js/ai-live`)

`@warlock.js/ai` ships the synchronous modality verbs (`ai.agent`, `ai.image`, `ai.speech`, `ai.transcribe`). `ai-live` adds the two that need heavyweight, demand-gated machinery — a **long-running job** (video) and a **persistent network session** (realtime voice) — kept in their own package so the core stays dependency-light.

Both mount onto the same `ai.*` facade by a **side-effect import**:

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-live"; // lights up ai.video + ai.realtime on the shared Ai facade
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
```

The mount mirrors how `@warlock.js/ai-tools` mounts `ai.mcp` and `@warlock.js/ai-workspace` mounts `ai.workspace`: a `declare module "@warlock.js/ai"` interface-merge plus `ai.video = video; ai.realtime = realtime` at load. Forget the side-effect import and `ai.video` is a compile-time `undefined` — not a silent runtime miss.

## `ai.video` — text-to-video, uniform envelope

Prompt in / one video out. The adapter hides the provider's async **submit→poll** lifecycle and resolves only when the clip is ready, so the verb returns the framework's uniform **never-throws** `{ data, error, usage, report }` — the exact shape `ai.image` returns, so video spend and traces fold into the same dashboards.

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const { data, error, usage, report } = await ai.video({
  model: sora.video({ name: "sora-2", pricing: { perSecond: 0.1 } }), // VideoModelContract
  prompt: "a timelapse of a city skyline at dusk, cinematic",
  durationSeconds: 8,
  aspectRatio: "16:9",
});

if (error) {
  console.warn(error.code); // typed AIError — NEVER thrown
} else {
  const clip = data.video; // GeneratedVideo (discriminated)
  if (clip.type === "url") download(clip.url);
  else save(Buffer.from(clip.base64, "base64"), clip.mediaType);
}
```

### Shape

```ts
type VideoResult = ExecuteResult<VideoData> & { type: "video"; report: VideoReport };
type VideoData = { video: GeneratedVideo };

type GeneratedVideo =
  | { type: "url"; url: string; mediaType?: string }
  | { type: "base64"; base64: string; mediaType: string };

// VideoParams (provider-neutral) — the model is the only required field beyond prompt:
await ai.video({
  model, // VideoModelContract from an adapter's video({ name })
  prompt: "...",
  durationSeconds: 8, // requested clip length
  aspectRatio: "9:16",
  resolution: "1080p", // hint
  negativePrompt: "blurry, watermark",
  signal, // AbortSignal → status "cancelled"
  observe: collector, // route the report to an Observer (panoptic), like agents
  sessionId: "campaign-42",
  name: "hero-clip", // report node name (defaults to "video")
  options: { seed: 7 }, // provider-specific escape hatch, forwarded verbatim
});
```

`VideoModelContract` is the moving-image sibling of `ImageModelContract` — `{ name, provider, pricing?, generate(prompt, options) }` — produced by an adapter's `video()` factory. An adapter with no video API simply doesn't define `video()`.

## Video cost-truth — per-second first

`VideoModelPricing` carries `{ perSecond?, input?, output? }`. Per-second wins when set (video is metered by clip length): `usage.cost = { input: 0, output: durationSeconds × perSecond }`, attributed to `cost.output`. A token-metered model falls back to the standard `computeCost` against reported tokens. No usable pricing → `usage.cost` stays `undefined` (honest "cost unknown", never a false zero). A pre-priced adapter response is honored, not overwritten. The final `durationSeconds` from the provider (not just the requested one) drives the math and lands on `report.durationSeconds`.

## `ai.realtime` — a duplex voice SESSION (not a one-shot)

Unlike every other `ai.*` verb, `ai.realtime()` returns a **stateful, long-lived session** — its closest sibling is `ai.orchestrator`. You open it over a pluggable **`RealtimeTransport`** (the low-level connection to the provider's realtime endpoint), push microphone audio / text turns in, consume an async **event stream** out, and `close()` to end it and receive a `RealtimeReport` for the cost/observability surfaces.

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const session = await ai.realtime({
  transport: openAiRealtime({ apiKey }), // RealtimeTransport (own adapter)
  model: "gpt-realtime",
  voice: "alloy",
  instructions: "You are a friendly phone receptionist.",
  sessionId: "call-8891",
});

session.sendAudio(micChunkBase64, "audio/pcm"); // push mic audio upstream
session.sendText("Please hold for one moment."); // or a text turn

for await (const event of session.events()) {
  // duplex output
  switch (event.type) {
    case "audio":
      speaker.write(event.base64);
      break;
    case "transcript":
      if (event.final) log(event.role, event.text);
      break;
    case "tool-call":
      await handleTool(event.name, event.input);
      break;
    case "error":
      console.warn(event.error.code);
      break;
    case "done":
      break;
  }
}

const report = await session.close(); // RealtimeReport — idempotent
```

### Session contract & event union

```ts
interface RealtimeSession {
  sendAudio(base64: string, mediaType: string): void;
  sendText(text: string): void;
  events(): AsyncIterable<RealtimeEvent>;
  close(): Promise<RealtimeReport>; // idempotent — second close() returns the first report
}

type RealtimeEvent =
  | { type: "audio"; base64: string; mediaType: string }
  | { type: "transcript"; role: "user" | "assistant"; text: string; final: boolean }
  | { type: "tool-call"; id: string; name: string; input: unknown }
  | { type: "error"; error: AIError } // typed, non-fatal
  | { type: "done" }; // server ended the session

type RealtimeReport = {
  runId: string;
  rootRunId: string;
  type: "realtime";
  name: string;
  status: "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled";
  startedAt: string;
  endedAt: string;
  duration: number;
  sessionId?: string;
};
```

The transport seam is what lets `ai-live` ship the session surface without hard-wiring `ws` (it's an optional peer). A concrete transport implements just two interfaces: `RealtimeTransport.connect(config) → RealtimeConnection` (with `sendAudio` / `sendText` / `events()` / `close()`).

## Pattern — a live phone receptionist over a channel

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-live";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

async function handleCall(caller: PhoneChannel, transport: RealtimeTransport) {
  const session = await ai.realtime({
    transport,
    model: "gpt-realtime",
    voice: "alloy",
    instructions: "Greet the caller and route them to the right department.",
    sessionId: caller.id,
  });

  // Pump caller audio → session (fire-and-forget).
  caller.onAudio((chunk) => session.sendAudio(chunk, "audio/pcm"));

  // Pump session output → caller, until the model signals done.
  for await (const event of session.events()) {
    if (event.type === "audio") caller.playAudio(event.base64);
    if (event.type === "done") break;
  }

  const report = await session.close();
  metrics.record({ runId: report.runId, seconds: report.duration / 1000 });
}
```

## Testing — mocks, no HTTP, no sockets

`@warlock.js/ai-live` exports deterministic doubles so both verbs test offline.

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { MockVideoModel, MockRealtimeTransport } from "@warlock.js/ai-live";

// Video — script the returned clip / usage / duration; assert cost math + recorded calls.
const model = new MockVideoModel("mock-video", [{ durationSeconds: 8 }], { perSecond: 0.1 });
const { data, usage } = await ai.video({ model, prompt: "x", durationSeconds: 8 });
// data.video → { type: "url", url: "https://mock/video.mp4", ... }
// usage.cost.output === 0.8   (8 × 0.1)
// model.calls[0] → { prompt: "x", options: { durationSeconds: 8, ... } }

// Realtime — script the outbound event stream; assert what the session sent.
const transport = new MockRealtimeTransport([
  { type: "transcript", role: "assistant", text: "Hi!", final: true },
  { type: "done" },
]);
const session = await ai.realtime({ transport, model: "mock-realtime" });
session.sendText("hello");
for await (const e of session.events()) {
  /* ... */
}
const report = await session.close();
// transport.lastConnection.sentText → ["hello"]
// transport.connectConfigs[0] → { model: "mock-realtime", ... }
// report.status === "completed"
```

Feed `MockVideoModel` an `{ error }` response and `ai.video` lands it on `result.error` (never throws), setting `report.status` to `"failed"` (or `"cancelled"` when the signal aborted).

## Status — contracts now, transports next

`4.6.0` introduces the package: the `VideoModelContract` / `RealtimeSession` contracts, the `ai.video()` verb (uniform envelope + per-second cost-truth, tested against `MockVideoModel`), and the `ai.realtime()` session primitive over a pluggable transport (tested against `MockRealtimeTransport`). The first **concrete provider transports** — an OpenAI Realtime **WebSocket** for `ai.realtime`, and **Sora / Veo** video adapters for `ai.video` — are the next implementation step; the seams are defined so they drop in without changing the verb surface.

## See also

- [[generate-images]] — still-image OUTPUT (`ai.image`), the synchronous sibling `ai.video` mirrors.
- [[generate-speech]] — one-shot text-to-speech / transcription (`ai.speech` / `ai.transcribe`); use `ai.realtime` instead when you need a live duplex conversation, not a single audio render.
- The `observe-ai-flows` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — the `observe` seam both verbs route their reports through.
- The `run-orchestrator` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — the other session-shaped primitive `ai.realtime` resembles.

# Connect to an external MCP server (Direction A)

`ai.mcp(server, options?)` opens a connection to any Model Context Protocol server, lists its tools, and adapts each one into a native `ToolContract` — so a remote MCP tool is indistinguishable from a local one and drops straight into `ai.agent({ tools: [...] })`.

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const github = ai.mcp(
  { type: "stdio", command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"] },
  { namePrefix: "github." },
);

const dev = ai.agent({
  model,
  systemPrompt: "Use the GitHub tools to triage issues.",
  tools: [...(await github.tools())], // handshake + tools/list, run once and cached
  maxTrips: 20,
});

await dev.execute("Find the oldest open 'bug' issue and propose a fix.");

await github.close(); // on teardown — kills the child / ends the HTTP session
```

## The transport — `stdio` or `http`

The `server` argument is discriminated by `type`:

```ts
// Spawn a child process and speak JSON-RPC over its stdin/stdout.
// Uses node:child_process + node:readline — NO dependency.
{ type: "stdio", command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"], env: { GITHUB_TOKEN: "…" } }

// Streamable HTTP against an endpoint.
{ type: "http", url: "https://mcp.example.com/rpc", headers: { authorization: "Bearer …" } }
```

> **stdio env is not inherited.** When you pass `env`, only those keys reach the child — pass what the server needs (e.g. its API token) explicitly.

## Client options

```ts
ai.mcp(server, {
  namePrefix: "github.", // prepended to every remote tool name
  filter: (name) => name.startsWith("issues_"), // only adapt tools whose name passes
  timeoutMs: 30_000, // per tools/call deadline (default 30s)
  signal: controller.signal, // optional: close the client when this aborts
});
```

- **`signal`** binds the client's lifetime to a run: on abort the client closes its transport (kills the stdio child / ends the HTTP session), in-flight requests reject, and later `tools()` / tool calls fail with `McpTransportError` type `"closed"` without sending anything. Each `tools/call` honors it together with the per-call `ctx.signal` — whichever aborts first. `close()` stays idempotent.

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai, type ModelContract } from "@warlock.js/ai";

export async function triage(model: ModelContract): Promise<void> {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const github = ai.mcp(
    { type: "stdio", command: "npx", args: ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-github"] },
    { namePrefix: "github.", signal: controller.signal },
  );

  const agent = ai.agent({ model, tools: [...(await github.tools())] });
  await agent.execute("Triage the open issues", { signal: controller.signal });

  controller.abort(); // ends the run AND shuts the MCP server down
}
```

- **`namePrefix`** is the collision mitigation — there is **no runtime tool-name collision guard** (the agent resolves a tool by first name match), so the author owns uniqueness. Prefix remote tools to keep them distinct from local ones.
- **`filter`** receives each tool's _unprefixed_ name; return `false` to drop it.

## What `tools()` does

`client.tools()` is lazy and cached: the **first** call runs the `initialize` handshake, sends `notifications/initialized`, then `tools/list`, and maps each descriptor into a `ToolContract`. Repeat calls return the cached array without re-handshaking.

For each remote tool:

1. its JSON-Schema `inputSchema` is wrapped as a Standard Schema via `jsonSchemaToStandard` (Ajv-backed — `ajv` is an optional peer needed only for the client);
2. `execute` issues `tools/call` honoring `ctx.signal` (cooperative abort) and the configured `timeoutMs`, then unwraps the result content (a single JSON text block is parsed back into an object);
3. an MCP `isError` result is thrown so the surrounding `tool()` wraps it as a `ToolExecutionError` — the agent reads it as `{ error }` data and self-corrects.

### Selecting one discovered tool

When selecting one discovered tool, guard the array result before invoking it.
A server may advertise no tools, and `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` reflects that:

```ts
import type { McpClient } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";

export async function invokeFirst(client: McpClient, input: unknown) {
  const [contract] = await client.tools();
  if (!contract) throw new Error("The MCP server advertised no tools");
  return contract.invoke(input);
}
```

## `type`, never `kind`

MCP's wire vocabulary uses `kind` in some content/capability descriptors. The client translates any inbound `kind` to `type` when normalizing content blocks, so a value a tool returns never carries MCP's `kind` — every discriminator the agent sees is `type`.

## Errors

Connection / handshake failures surface **at agent-construction time** because the example `await`s `github.tools()` — you see them then, not mid-run. A `tools/call` failure raised mid-run is wrapped by `tool()` and reaches the model as data. Branch on `McpTransportError.type`:

```ts
import { McpTransportError } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";

try {
  await github.tools();
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof McpTransportError && error.type === "connect") {
    // the child failed to spawn, the endpoint was unreachable, or the handshake failed
  }
}
```

`McpTransportError.type`: `"connect"` | `"protocol"` | `"timeout"` | `"closed"` (plus an optional `.method` naming the in-flight JSON-RPC method).

## Optional peers

The MCP client does not use `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`: it speaks MCP's JSON-RPC itself, over a spawned child process (`node:child_process`) for `{ type: "stdio" }` and the global `fetch` for `{ type: "http" }`, so neither transport needs a dependency. Its only optional peer is `ajv`, which validates tool-call input against each MCP tool's `inputSchema`. It is imported lazily the first time a schema is checked; when it is missing, the call fails validation with a curated `npm install ajv` message instead of crashing at import time. A tool with no `inputSchema` needs no validator.

- The `expose-as-mcp-server` topic — the reverse direction: publish a local primitive AS an MCP server.
- The `use-web-and-http-tools` topic — the built-in web / HTTP / calculator / date-time belt.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — running the agent that consumes the adapted tools.

# Expose tools AS an MCP server (Direction B)

`ai.mcp.serve(source, options)` turns a local set of `ToolContract`s into a Model Context Protocol server — so Cursor, Claude Desktop, a coding CLI, or any MCP client can call your warlock tools / agent. Transports: **stdio** (default) and MCP **Streamable HTTP**.

## Serve over HTTP with a per-session token

```ts
import { randomBytes } from "node:crypto";
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const token = randomBytes(32).toString("hex");

const server = ai.mcp.serve([ai.tools.calculator(), ai.tools.dateTime()], {
  name: "session-tools",
  transport: { type: "http", auth: { bearer: token } },
});

const { url, close } = await server.start();
// url → "http://127.0.0.1:<free port>/mcp" — hand url + token to the MCP client

await close(); // drains in-flight calls, then frees the port
```

Defaults: `host: "127.0.0.1"`, `port: 0` (free ephemeral port), `path: "/mcp"`. `start()` resolves `{ url, close }` once bound.

## Serve over stdio

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const server = ai.mcp.serve([ai.tools.calculator()], {
  name: "warlock-utils",
  transport: { type: "stdio" },
});

await server.start(); // reads JSON-RPC lines from stdin, answers on stdout
// on teardown:
await server.stop();
```

## HTTP options and security rules

```ts
transport: {
  type: "http",
  host: "127.0.0.1",           // non-loopback (e.g. "0.0.0.0") REQUIRES auth — start() throws otherwise
  port: 0,
  path: "/mcp",
  auth: {
    bearer: ["current-token", "previous-token"], // constant-time compare; several = rotation
    authorize: async (request) => sessions.has(request.headers["x-session-id"] ?? ""), // optional hook
  },
  allowedOrigins: ["https://app.example.com"], // besides loopback origins
  allowedHosts: ["mcp.internal"],              // extra Host names while on loopback
  maxBodyBytes: 1_048_576,                     // larger → 413
  drainTimeoutMs: 5_000,                       // close() then aborts ctx.signal
}
```

- Checks run in order: `bearer`, `authorize`, `authenticate`; every configured check must pass. A failed check skips later hooks. `authenticate` alone satisfies the non-loopback auth requirement. Host/Origin checks run first. A throwing authentication hook denies. Failures → `401`; bearer or authenticate failures include a Bearer `WWW-Authenticate` challenge.
- A foreign or `null` `Origin` → `403` (DNS-rebinding guard from the MCP spec). Requests without `Origin` pass.
- On loopback, a `Host` other than `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` / `[::1]` (or `allowedHosts`) → `403`.
- Stateless: no session id; `GET` / `DELETE` → `405`; batches → `400`; unsupported `MCP-Protocol-Version` → `400`.
- Plain HTTP: put TLS in front before exposing beyond the machine.

## Tools read request headers from `ctx.request`

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai, type ToolContract } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const whoami: ToolContract = ai.tool({
  name: "whoami",
  description: "Report the calling tenant",
  execute: async (_input: unknown, ctx) => ({
    tenant: ctx?.request?.headers["x-tenant-id"] ?? "unknown",
  }),
});

const { url, close } = await ai.mcp
  .serve([whoami], { name: "tenant-tools", transport: { type: "http" } })
  .start();
```

Header names are lower-cased; every client header is present (including `authorization`). Over stdio `ctx.request` is absent. Nothing on `ctx.request` reaches the model.

## Authenticated context, policy and cancellation

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import type { McpHttpRequestInfo, McpCallRefusal } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";

declare function findMember(
  request: McpHttpRequestInfo,
): Promise<{ id: string; canCall: boolean } | undefined>;
const denied: McpCallRefusal = {
  isError: true,
  content: [{ type: "text", text: "Member cannot call tools" }],
  _meta: { policy: "membership" },
};
const identity = ai.tool({
  name: "identity",
  description: "Report the authenticated caller and request id",
  execute: async (_input: unknown, ctx) => {
    ctx?.signal?.throwIfAborted();
    return { requestId: ctx?.requestId, principal: ctx?.principal };
  },
});

const server = ai.mcp.serve([identity], {
  name: "member-tools",
  transport: { type: "http", auth: { authenticate: findMember } },
  beforeCall: async (context, tool, input) => {
    const member = context.principal; // unknown — narrow before use
    if (
      typeof member !== "object" ||
      member === null ||
      !("canCall" in member) ||
      member.canCall !== true
    ) {
      return denied;
    }
    // context.requestId: JSON-RPC id; tool: original ToolContract;
    // input: validated data, treated as read-only.
  },
});
```

- `authenticate(request)` may be synchronous or async. `undefined` or a thrown error → `401` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer realm="mcp"`; every other value becomes `context.principal` and `ctx.principal`. Secrets in thrown auth errors are not exposed.
- `beforeCall(context, tool, input)` runs after schema validation. Return nothing to allow; return `McpCallRefusal` (`isError: true`) to send native content/metadata unchanged, independent of result mode. Throw → JSON-RPC `-32602`. Invalid refusals → `-32603`. Invalid input skips policy. The boundary validates before policy and `invoke` keeps its own validation, so schemas must be deterministic and policy input read-only.
- Stdio identity: `transport: { type: "stdio", principal: { id: "local" } }` or `transport: { type: "stdio", principalProvider: async (context) => ({ id: "local", requestId: context.requestId }) }`. The provider runs per request, takes precedence over static principal, and receives the request id and abort signal. A provider throw → JSON-RPC internal error. No HTTP request metadata exists over stdio.
- Public types: `McpBeforeCall`, `McpCallRefusal`, `McpServeToolContext`, `McpStdioServeTransport`; `ToolContext` in `@warlock.js/ai` adds optional `requestId` and `principal`.

[Cancellation (MCP 2025-11-25)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/utilities/cancellation): send `{ jsonrpc: "2.0", method: "notifications/cancelled", params: { requestId: 42, reason: "Caller cancelled" } }`. The matching signal aborts; no JSON-RPC response is sent even if the tool later returns or throws. Unknown/completed/malformed ids are ignored; `initialize` cannot be cancelled. String and numeric ids are distinct; calls sharing an in-flight id still execute, but ambiguous cancellation in one scope is ignored.

HTTP cancellation POSTs must repeat caller credentials and application headers (`Authorization`, `Cookie`, tenant/custom auth headers), from the same remote address. Transport headers such as content length, accept, protocol version and connection may differ. Different credentials can reuse ids safely. Clients sharing credential/application headers must use unique in-flight ids for cancellation to identify a call. Notifications get `202`; a cancelled HTTP call ends with `202`, no JSON-RPC body, when its handler settles. Stdio scopes cancellation to the connection. HTTP disconnect, stdio EOF/close/stop, or HTTP shutdown after the drain timeout also abort tools. Pass `ctx.signal` into cancellable work.

## Return native MCP results

Default results become one text block, even when an object resembles an MCP result. Return the exported `mcpResult(...)` helper to preserve native content blocks, `isError`, `structuredContent` and `_meta` over stdio or HTTP:

```ts
import { mcpResult } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const count = ai.tool({
  name: "count",
  description: "Return a structured count",
  meta: {
    outputSchema: {
      type: "object",
      properties: { count: { type: "number" } },
      required: ["count"],
    },
  },
  execute: async (_input: unknown, ctx) =>
    mcpResult({
      content: [{ type: "text", text: '{"count":2}' }],
      structuredContent: { count: 2 },
      _meta: { tenant: ctx?.request?.headers["x-tenant-id"] ?? "unknown" },
    }),
});

ai.mcp.serve([count], { name: "counts" });
```

The helper returns a branded `McpNativeResult` wrapper. The serving boundary validates and unwraps it without altering its payload. `isError: true` is sent as-is; thrown tool errors retain the existing mapping.

For tools that already return native objects, opt in at the server or tool level:

```ts
const nativeTool = ai.tool({
  name: "native-result",
  description: "Return a native result",
  meta: { mcpResults: "native" }, // this tool opts in even on a default server
  execute: async () => ({ content: [{ type: "text", text: "fixture" }], isError: true }),
});

ai.mcp.serve([nativeTool], { name: "native-tools", results: "native" });
// On a native-mode server, meta: { mcpResults: "text" } disables detection for a tool.
// Explicit mcpResult(...) returns always opt in, regardless of the detection setting.
```

Native mode detects objects containing any of `content`, `isError`, `structuredContent` or `_meta`; other values keep text serialization. `content` must be an array of valid MCP text/image/audio/resource-link/embedded-resource blocks. Optional `isError` must be boolean; `structuredContent` and `_meta` must be JSON objects. Invalid or non-JSON native payloads answer a JSON-RPC internal error (`-32603`), including malformed helper payloads.

`meta.outputSchema` is emitted as `outputSchema` in `tools/list`; `structuredContent` passes through unchanged. Tool authors own schema conformity. Follow the [MCP 2025-11-25 tools specification](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/server/tools#structured-content): also include serialized structured output in a text block for compatibility.

Request identity is unchanged: native tools receive each HTTP call's headers and remote address on `ctx.request`, plus `ctx.signal`. Over stdio, `ctx.request` is absent. Returning a native result does not automatically expose request metadata; the tool controls its response.

## Sources and tool-name collisions

```ts
ai.mcp.serve([calc, dt], { name: "utils" }); // literal array
ai.mcp.serve({ tools: () => ws.tools.all() }, { name: "workspace" }); // anything with tools()
ai.mcp.serve(
  { groups: { prod: [search], staging: [search] } },
  {
    name: "search",
    prefixToolNames: true, // → prod_search, staging_search; or (group, name) => `${group}.${name}`
  },
);
```

Duplicate exposed names throw `McpServeError` (`type: "collision"`) **when `serve()` is called**. `prefixToolNames` on an ungrouped source throws `type: "config"`.

## Resources and prompts (optional)

```ts
ai.mcp.serve(tools, {
  name: "handbook",
  resources: [
    {
      uri: "docs://handbook",
      name: "handbook",
      mimeType: "text/markdown",
      read: () => "# Handbook",
    },
  ],
  prompts: [
    {
      name: "review",
      arguments: [{ name: "diff", required: true }],
      get: (args) => `Review this diff:\n${args.diff ?? ""}`, // string → one user message
    },
  ],
});
```

`read()` returns a string (text) or `Uint8Array` (base64 blob). `get()` returns a string or `McpPromptMessage[]`. Unknown resource → `-32002`; unknown prompt / missing required argument → `-32602`.

## How the protocol maps

- **`initialize`** → `{ name, version }`, capabilities `tools` (+ `resources` / `prompts` when configured); protocol version negotiated from `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSIONS` (`2025-11-25`, `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26`).
- **`tools/list`** → `inputSchema` via `extractJsonSchema(contract.input, { target: schemaTarget })` (default `"draft-2020-12"`).
- **`tools/call`** → `invoke()`; default `data` → text block (JSON-stringified unless a string), opted-in native results → validated passthrough, `error` → `isError: true`. Unknown tool → JSON-RPC error.
- **`ping`** → `{}`.

## Drive the protocol yourself (tests, custom servers)

```ts
import { createServeHandler } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const handler = createServeHandler([ai.tools.calculator()], { name: "utils" });

const response = await handler.handle(
  { jsonrpc: "2.0", id: 1, method: "tools/list" },
  { request: { method: "POST", path: "/mcp", headers: { "x-tenant-id": "acme" } } },
);
```

Mounting it in your own server means you own Origin validation, auth and body limits.

## Errors

`McpServeError.type`: `"collision"` (from `serve()`), `"config"` (unsafe/invalid options, from `start()`), `"listen"` (bind failed). Bad requests never throw — they get an HTTP status or JSON-RPC error; failing tools return `isError: true`.

# Use the web + HTTP tool belt

`@warlock.js/ai-tools` ships five ready-made tools. Import the package once for its side effect and they register on the shared `ai` object under `ai.tools.*` — each is a factory returning a `ToolContract` you spread into `ai.agent({ tools: [...] })`.

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { OpenAISDK } from "@warlock.js/ai-openai";

const openai = new OpenAISDK({ apiKey: process.env.OPENAI_API_KEY! });

const agent = ai.agent({
  model: openai.model({ name: "gpt-4o" }),
  systemPrompt: "Research, then call the API. Read tool errors and adjust.",
  tools: [
    ai.tools.webSearch({ provider: "tavily" }),
    ai.tools.fetchUrl({ extract: "text", allowHosts: ["docs.stripe.com"] }),
    ai.tools.http({ baseUrl: "https://api.stripe.com", allowHosts: ["api.stripe.com"] }),
    ai.tools.calculator(),
    ai.tools.dateTime({ defaultTimeZone: "UTC" }),
  ],
  maxTrips: 15,
});
```

The construction `options` are the **rails** — they bound what the model may do; the model supplies the per-call inputs _within_ those rails. Least-privilege is just array composition: hand an agent only the tools (and only the methods/hosts) it needs.

## The five tools

| Factory                         | Name           | Model input                                                    | Returns                                          |
| ------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `ai.tools.webSearch(options)`   | `web_search`   | `{ query, maxResults? }`                                       | `{ results: { title, url, snippet, score? }[] }` |
| `ai.tools.fetchUrl(options?)`   | `fetch_url`    | `{ url }`                                                      | `{ url, status, content, truncated }`            |
| `ai.tools.http(options?)`       | `http_request` | `{ method?, url, headers?, body? }`                            | `{ status, headers, body, truncated }`           |
| `ai.tools.calculator(options?)` | `calculator`   | `{ expression }`                                               | `{ result }`                                     |
| `ai.tools.dateTime(options?)`   | `date_time`    | `{ op, iso?, from?, to?, amount?, unit?, timeZone?, format? }` | `{ value }`                                      |

## `web_search` — pick a provider, supply a key

```ts
ai.tools.webSearch({ provider: "tavily", apiKey: process.env.TAVILY_API_KEY, maxResults: 8 });
```

- `provider`: `"tavily"` (LLM-ready snippets + a relevance `score`), `"brave"`, or `"serpapi"`. Each is called over the global `fetch` — **no provider SDK is required**.
- `apiKey` falls back to a per-provider env var: `TAVILY_API_KEY` / `BRAVE_API_KEY` / `SERPAPI_API_KEY`. A missing key is a `WebToolError` of type `"missing-key"`.
- The model's `maxResults` is clamped into `[1, options.maxResults]` (default `5`).

## `fetch_url` — read a page you have the URL for

```ts
ai.tools.fetchUrl({
  extract: "text",
  allowHosts: ["docs.stripe.com"],
  maxBytes: 500_000,
  timeoutMs: 10_000,
});
```

- `extract`: `"text"` (default — readability-extracted main text), `"html"` (raw body), or `"markdown"`. **`"text"`/`"markdown"` lazily import the `@mozilla/readability` + `jsdom` optional peers** — a missing peer is a `WebToolError` of type `"missing-peer"` carrying the `npm install @mozilla/readability jsdom` string. `"html"` needs nothing.
- `allowHosts` (when set) rejects any other host **before the fetch** (an SSRF guardrail) → `"denied-host"`, and redirect targets are held to the same allowlist.
- **Private-network deny by default.** Every request — and every redirect hop — now routes through `@warlock.js/ai`'s hardened `guardedFetch` outbound policy instead of a local host check. It refuses private / loopback / link-local / CGNAT / cloud-metadata addresses (`169.254.169.254`, RFC1918, `localhost`, …) by resolving the hostname via DNS and checking every returned address, failing closed on resolution failure — and re-validates every redirect `Location` (scheme, allowlist, private-IP deny) before following it. This applies even with no `allowHosts` set, so a bare `ai.tools.fetchUrl()` is no longer an SSRF primitive; blocks surface as `WebToolError` `type: "denied-host"`.
- `allowPrivateNetwork` (default `false`) — set `true` to deliberately permit a private/internal target, e.g. a tool that must call a local dev server. Pair with `allowHosts` to scope it rather than opening the whole private range.
- `maxBytes` caps the body and flags `truncated`; `timeoutMs` aborts via `AbortSignal.timeout`.

## `http_request` — a guarded REST client

```ts
ai.tools.http({
  baseUrl: "https://api.stripe.com",
  allowHosts: ["api.stripe.com"],
  allowMethods: ["GET", "POST"], // default ["GET"] — mutating methods are opt-in
  headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.STRIPE_KEY}` },
  timeoutMs: 15_000,
  maxBytes: 1_000_000,
  // allowPrivateNetwork: true,             // only for a deliberate internal/dev target
});
```

All guardrails are enforced **before the network call** and surface as a typed `HttpPolicyError`:

- a method outside `allowMethods` → `"method-not-allowed"`;
- a host outside `allowHosts` → `"host-not-allowed"` (SSRF guardrail);
- an unresolvable URL → `"invalid-url"`.
- **Private-network deny by default** — like `fetch_url`, every request and redirect hop routes through `guardedFetch`, refusing private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/cloud-metadata addresses (DNS-resolved and re-checked per redirect hop) even when `allowHosts` isn't set → `"host-not-allowed"`. Set `allowPrivateNetwork: true` (default `false`) to permit a deliberate internal target.

When `baseUrl` is set the model passes a **path** joined against it; otherwise it must pass an absolute `http(s)` URL. Static `headers` merge **under** the per-call headers (per-call wins). An object `body` is JSON-serialized (with a default `content-type: application/json`); a string `body` is sent verbatim; `body` is dropped for `GET`. The response body is JSON-parsed when the `content-type` is JSON, else returned as text.

## `calculator` — SAFE arithmetic (never `eval`)

```ts
const { data } = await ai.tools.calculator().invoke({ expression: "(3 + 4) * 2 ^ 3" });
data?.result; // 56
```

Supports `+ - * / % ^`, unary signs, parentheses, and decimal/scientific literals, with the usual precedence (`^` highest and right-associative). The expression is tokenized and evaluated with a shunting-yard pass — there is no path to an identifier, function call, or property access, so nothing code-like can be smuggled in. Failures are a `CalculatorError`: `"syntax"`, `"divide-by-zero"`, or `"overflow"`.

## `date_time` — clock + calendar

```ts
await ai.tools.dateTime().invoke({ op: "now", format: "iso" });
await ai.tools
  .dateTime()
  .invoke({ op: "add", iso: "2026-06-22T00:00:00Z", amount: 3, unit: "days" });
await ai.tools
  .dateTime()
  .invoke({ op: "diff", iso: "2026-06-22T00:00:00Z", to: "2026-06-25T00:00:00Z", unit: "days" }); // "3"
await ai.tools
  .dateTime({ defaultTimeZone: "Africa/Cairo" })
  .invoke({ op: "format", iso: "2026-06-22T12:00:00Z", format: "datetime" });
```

- `op`: `"now"` / `"add"` / `"diff"` / `"format"`. `format`: `"iso"` (default), `"date"`, `"time"`, `"datetime"`.
- For `diff`, pass the start instant as `iso` **or** `from` (an alias models reach for naturally with `from`/`to`); `iso` wins when both are set. The end instant is always `to`.
- Units are millisecond-based: `milliseconds`, `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `weeks` (plus singular/short aliases like `day`/`d`). Calendar-relative `month`/`year` are intentionally **unsupported** — they have no fixed length. An unknown unit → `DateTimeError` `"invalid-unit"`; an unknown IANA zone → `"invalid-time-zone"`.
- For deterministic tests, inject a clock by calling the factory directly: `import { dateTimeTool } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools"; dateTimeTool({}, { clock: () => Date.parse("2026-06-22T00:00:00Z") })`.

## `ai.tools.measure` — what the belt costs per model call

`ai.tools.measure(tools, options?)` is `measureTools` from `@warlock.js/ai`: the input tokens a tool list adds to every call, per tool and in total. Native and exact when the model has `countTokens` (`source: "native"`, `tools.length + 2` count calls, `overhead` = the provider's once-per-request tool preamble); estimated from the schema JSON otherwise (`source: "estimate"`).

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-tools";
import { ai, type ModelContract } from "@warlock.js/ai";

export async function reportBeltCost(model: ModelContract): Promise<void> {
  const belt = [ai.tools.calculator(), ai.tools.dateTime()];

  const full = await ai.tools.measure(belt, { model });
  const compact = await ai.tools.measure(belt, { model, mode: "compact" });

  console.log(full.source, full.tokens, "→", compact.tokens, full.perTool);
}
```

If compact saves enough, run the agent with `toolSchemas: "compact"` (the `define-ai-tool` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill).

## Errors flow as data, not throws

Every failure above is thrown inside the tool handler, caught by the framework's `tool()` wrapper, and surfaced in the returned `{ error }` field — `invoke()` never throws, so the agent reads the failure as a `role: "tool"` message and self-corrects on the next trip. Each error class extends the `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` base; branch on `.type`:

```ts
import { WebToolError } from "@warlock.js/ai-tools";

const { error } = await ai.tools
  .fetchUrl({ allowHosts: ["docs.stripe.com"] })
  .invoke({ url: "http://evil.test" });
if (error instanceof WebToolError && error.type === "denied-host") {
  // rejected before any network call
}
```

# Build a build-loop agent — read → edit → run tests, until green

The point of a workspace is to hand its tools to an agent and let it close the loop itself: read the failing spec, edit the source, run the tests, read the failure, fix again. The failure comes back as tool **data** (a non-zero `exitCode`, the captured `stderr`), not a thrown error — so the model can see what broke and self-correct.

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const ws = ai.workspace({
  cwd: "/srv/acme-api",
  denyPaths: [".git/**", ".env*"],
  shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], timeoutMs: 120_000 },
});

const dev = ai.agent({
  model,
  tools: ws.tools.all(), // read/edit/multi_edit/write, list_dir, run_shell, run_tests, grep, glob, todo_write/todo_read
  maxTrips: 25, // give the loop room to iterate
});

await dev.execute("`npm test` fails on the cart-total suite. Make it green.");
```

## Why the loop works: errors as data

A failing test isn't a tool error — it's a normal result with `exitCode !== 0`. `run_tests` (and `run_shell`) return `{ exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, truncated }` as the tool's `data`, so the model reads the failure on the next trip and tries again. The same is true of the policy/edit guards: a jail escape, a denied command, a non-unique edit, or a stale hash all come back as tool-error data the agent can react to, never a thrown run-killer. Give `maxTrips` enough headroom for the read → edit → test cycle to converge.

## Give the test command a path

`run_tests` defaults to `npm test`. It runs through the **same shell policy** as `run_shell`, so the agent can't run it unless:

- the executable basename is allowed — `shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"] }`, and
- the env can find it — `inheritEnv: ["PATH"]` (the workspace never inherits `process.env` wholesale).

Override the base command per agent: `ws.tools.runTests({ command: "vitest run" })`. A `pattern` the model supplies is appended as a filter (e.g. `vitest run cart-total`).

## Least-privilege variants

### A read-only reviewer

A reviewer should never write or run a shell. Pick exactly the read tools, or hand it a `readonly()` projection (which omits the mutating tools _and_ rejects the mutating direct methods):

```ts
const reviewer = ai.agent({
  model,
  tools: ws.tools.pick("readFile", "grep", "glob"),
});
await reviewer.execute("Review src/cart for off-by-one bugs and summarize.");

// Equivalent projection of the same jail:
ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.readonly().tools.all() }); // read_file, list_dir, grep, glob, todo tools
```

### Scope an agent to one package

`scope(subdir)` narrows the jail so a per-package agent can't reach outside it — one sub-agent per package, isolated blast radius:

```ts
const apiDev = ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.scope("packages/api").tools.all() });
const webDev = ai.agent({ model, tools: ws.scope("packages/web").tools.all() });
```

## Scaffold from code, then hand off

You don't have to let the agent do everything. Seed structure (and install deps) with the direct methods, then hand the tools to the agent for the creative part:

```ts
await ws.writeFile("src/routes.ts", ROUTES_BOILERPLATE);
await ws.exec("npm install zod");
await dev.execute("Implement the handlers declared in src/routes.ts.");
```

For a purely mechanical change, skip the LLM entirely: `ws.glob(...)` + a loop of `ws.editFile(...)` under the stale-hash guard.

## Share one workspace across a team

One workspace is one jail and one tree. Pass it to several members of a supervisor, varying only the tool slice each gets — they all read/write the **same** files:

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd, shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] } });

ai.supervisor({
  members: [
    ai.agent({ /* executor */ model, tools: ws.tools.all() }),
    ai.agent({ /* reviewer */ model, tools: ws.readonly().tools.all() }),
    ai.agent({ /* tester   */ model, tools: ws.tools.pick("readFile", "runTests") }),
  ],
});
```

# Use a workspace — a policy jail for an agent's filesystem + shell

`ai.workspace(policy)` returns a **workspace**: a bounded place an agent reads, writes, and runs commands. One policy, one shared rule set, two ways to touch it — the agent uses `ws.tools.*`; you use the direct methods. Import the package once for its side effect so the verb is registered on the shared `ai`:

```ts
import "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";

const ws = ai.workspace({
  cwd: "/srv/acme-api",
  denyPaths: [".git/**", ".env*"],
  shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], timeoutMs: 60_000 },
  read: { defaultLines: 2_000 },
  backend: "local", // default; use "mock" for hermetic tests
});
```

## A policy jail, NOT OS isolation

This is least-privilege guardrails for a **trusted** agent — not a sandbox around hostile code. It enforces a `realpath`-resolved `cwd` jail, path allow/deny, a fail-closed shell allow/deny list, timeouts, output caps, and a non-inherited environment. It does **not** contain what an _allowed_ process does once it runs.

Paths are resolved against `cwd` with symlinks collapsed and accepted inside `cwd` or an `allowPaths` root, off `denyPaths`; absolute paths inside the jail, links that stay inside and not-yet-existing paths (for writes) are accepted. To read a folder you do not trust from app code (no links at all, size and entry caps), use `fs.confined(root)` from `@warlock.js/fs` (the `read-a-folder-confined` topic) instead of a workspace.

**Shell mode (`interpreter: "sh"`) is a policy layer (defence in depth), not an OS sandbox.** It parses the line before `/bin/sh` runs it and refuses what it cannot read, but `/bin/sh` differs between systems (bash, dash, busybox ash), an allowed program (`node`, `npm`, `make`, a git hook) can still start anything the OS user can, and a symlink can change between the jail re-check and the write. For an untrusted agent (one that reads untrusted repos, issues, web pages or tool output), run the workspace in a container or microVM with only the project mounted, or at least as a separate unprivileged user, and keep the policy as a second layer. Prefer argv mode (the default) when the agent does not need pipes or redirections.

## The policy surface

| Field                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cwd`                                               | **Absolute** jail root. Every path resolves against it and must stay inside.                                                                                                                                             |
| `allowPaths`                                        | Extra readable roots outside `cwd`.                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `denyPaths`                                         | Globs (`*`, `**`, `?`) blocked **even inside `cwd`** — e.g. `[".git/**", ".env*"]`. A bare dir name (`"node_modules"`) also blocks its contents.                                                                         |
| `shell.allow` / `shell.deny`                        | Executable **basenames** matched against every command's argv (after tokenizing — see below). **Deny wins**, case-insensitively. An `allow` list is exhaustive (fail-closed); no `shell` block at all ⇒ nothing may run. |
| `shell.denyPatterns` / `shell.allowCommand`         | Argument rules on every command: string prefix patterns (`"git push --force"`) or RegExps, and a predicate `(argv, ctx) => true \| false \| "why"`.                                                                      |
| `shell.interpreter`                                 | `"none"` (default, argv) or `"sh"` (opt-in shell syntax, every command checked).                                                                                                                                         |
| `shell.background`                                  | `{ maxJobs?, timeoutMs? }` — enables background commands. Absent ⇒ refused.                                                                                                                                              |
| `list.ignore` / `list.maxDepth` / `list.maxEntries` | `list_dir` bounds: hidden globs (default `node_modules`, `.git`), depth cap (5), entry cap (500).                                                                                                                        |
| `shell.inheritEnv`                                  | Opt-in `process.env` keys to pass through (e.g. `["PATH"]`). **Nothing leaks in otherwise** — a command can't find `node`/`npm` without `PATH`.                                                                          |
| `shell.env`                                         | Explicit env vars injected into every spawned process (override inherited on collision).                                                                                                                                 |
| `shell.timeoutMs` / `shell.maxOutputBytes`          | Per-command wall-clock cap (process tree SIGKILLed on expiry) and stdout/stderr byte cap (clipped on a character boundary).                                                                                              |
| `read.defaultLines` / `read.maxBytes`               | Default read window + a ceiling on the UTF-8 bytes of the returned `content` (line numbers included). See [Read windows and the byte ceiling](#read-windows-and-the-byte-ceiling).                                       |
| `backend`                                           | `"local"` (default — real disk) or `"mock"` (in-memory, for tests).                                                                                                                                                      |

> **The most common gotcha:** `run_shell` fails to find `node`/`npm` because the env is empty. Add `shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] }`.

## `run_shell`/`exec` run argv, NOT a shell

Commands are tokenized (via `tokenizeCommand`) into an argv and spawned with **no shell semantics** — no pipes, redirection, chaining, backticks, or variable expansion. `npm test && rm -rf /` or `` `curl evil` `` doesn't chain or substitute; it's rejected outright rather than executed piecemeal:

```ts
await ws.exec("npm test"); // OK — ["npm", "test"]
await ws.exec('node -e "console.log(1)"'); // OK — quotes respected, one argv element
await ws.exec("npm test; curl http://evil"); // rejected — unquoted `;` is a metacharacter
```

- **Quoting is respected**; **unquoted** shell metacharacters — `;` `&` `|` `<` `>` `` ` `` `$` `(` `)` and newlines — are rejected as a `WorkspacePolicyError` `type: "denied-command"` before anything spawns. The `shell.allow`/`shell.deny` basename check runs against the tokenized argv's first element, not a raw string prefix, so a disguised leading token can't slip past the gate.
- **On Windows**, the argv is run through a `cmd.exe /d /s /c` wrapper with every element individually quoted (needed because batch shims like `npm.cmd` can't be spawned shell-less); arguments containing `"`, `%`, or newlines are refused there rather than risked (guards the BatBadBut-class argument-smuggling bug class).
- **`run_tests`'s `pattern`** (model-controlled test-name filter) is forwarded as a **single double-quoted argv token** to the runner, not concatenated into the command string — a pattern containing double quotes or newlines is rejected at input validation rather than passed through.
- Shell conveniences (pipes, redirection, `&&` chaining, `$(...)` substitution) don't work in argv mode. The refusal (`reason: "metacharacter"`) names the operator and suggests the split — e.g. "`&&` is not supported in argv mode: run `git add -A`, then `git commit -m "wip"`, as separate commands." — so the model retries correctly.
- **Wrappers are followed**: `env`, `time`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `command`, `builtin`, `exec`, `find -exec` — the inner command is checked too. Runners the policy can't see into (`sh -c`, `bash`, `eval`, `source`, `xargs`, `sudo`, `setsid`, …) are refused with `reason: "nested-command"` while deny rules are in force, unless `allow` names them.

## Argument rules and shell mode

```ts
import { workspace, WorkspacePolicyError } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function commitWork(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    shell: {
      interpreter: "sh", // opt in: pipes, &&, redirections — every command still checked
      allow: ["git", "npm", "grep"],
      denyPatterns: ["git push --force", /^git reset --hard\b/],
      allowCommand: (argv) => (argv[0] === "git" && argv[1] === "push" ? "CI pushes." : true),
      inheritEnv: ["PATH"],
      timeoutMs: 120_000,
    },
  });

  try {
    await ws.exec("git add -A && git commit -m 'wip'");
    return await ws.exec("npm test 2>&1 | grep -i fail > logs/failures.txt");
  } catch (error) {
    if (error instanceof WorkspacePolicyError && error.type === "denied-command") {
      console.warn(error.reason, error.message); // e.g. "denied-pattern", "path-escape"
    }

    throw error;
  }
}
```

- Shell mode parses the line and checks every simple command — inside `;`, `&&`, `||`, pipes, `( )`, `$( )`, backticks, here-documents and `NAME=value cmd` prefixes. Redirection targets and `cd` directories must be literal paths inside the jail (`/dev/null` is fine), re-checked with symlinks resolved.
- It refuses what it can't parse with confidence (`reason: "unsupported-syntax"`): compound commands, arithmetic, brace expansion, unusual `${…}` forms, bash-only redirections, a command name decided at run time, `&` in a line (use `background: true`), assignments to `IFS`/`PS4`/`CDPATH`/`BASH_ENV`…; it drops shell start-up variables (`ENV`, `BASH_ENV`, `SHELLOPTS`, `BASH_FUNC_*`, …) from the environment.
- `reason` values: `"metacharacter"`, `"unbalanced-quotes"`, `"denied-executable"`, `"not-allowed"`, `"denied-pattern"`, `"nested-command"`, `"unsupported-syntax"`, `"path-escape"`. `checkShellCommand(policy, line)` returns the verdict without running anything.
- Pair shell mode with an exhaustive `allow`: `deny` alone is a best-effort filter.

## Two callers, one jail

### Agent-facing — `ws.tools.*`

Each tool is a `ToolContract` (with a JSON Schema of its input) ready for `ai.agent({ tools })`. The LLM-visible tool names are `read_file`, `edit_file`, `multi_edit`, `write_file`, `list_dir`, `run_shell`, `shell_output`, `shell_kill`, `run_tests`, `grep`, `glob`, `todo_write`, `todo_read` — `shell_output` / `shell_kill` only in `all()` when `shell.background` is set.

```ts
ws.tools.all(); // every tool, canonical order
ws.tools.pick("readFile", "grep", "glob"); // a least-privilege subset
ws.tools.readFile({ name: "open" }); // one tool, optionally renamed
ws.tools.runTests({ command: "vitest run" }); // override the test base command
```

### Human-facing — direct methods

The same policy seam, callable from code (no LLM):

```ts
const { content, hash, totalLines, endLine, truncated, bytesCapped } = await ws.readFile(
  "src/index.ts",
  { offset: 1, limit: 200 },
);
await ws.writeFile("src/new.ts", "export const x = 1;\n");
await ws.editFile({ path: "src/index.ts", oldString: "old", newString: "new", expectHash: hash });
const { exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, cancelled, truncated } = await ws.exec("npm test");
const { matches } = await ws.grep("TODO", { glob: "src/**/*.ts", ignoreCase: true });
const paths = await ws.glob("src/models/**/*.ts");
await ws.exists("package.json");
await ws.mkdir("src/generated");
await ws.remove("dist");
```

## The coding-agent tool belt

```ts
import { workspace } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function devLoop(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    list: { maxEntries: 300 },
    shell: { allow: ["npm", "node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"], background: { maxJobs: 2 } },
  });

  try {
    const { entries } = await ws.listDir("src", { depth: 2 }); // bounded, jailed, node_modules/.git hidden
    console.info(entries.map((entry) => `${entry.type} ${entry.path}`));

    const { hash } = await ws.readFile("src/cart.ts");
    await ws.multiEdit({
      path: "src/cart.ts",
      expectHash: hash,
      edits: [
        { oldString: "let total = 0;", newString: "let total = 0n;" },
        { oldString: "total += price;", newString: "total += BigInt(price);" },
      ], // all apply, or none (WorkspaceEditError.editIndex names the failing one)
    });

    const server = await ws.startShell("npm run dev"); // run_shell({ command, background: true })
    const { stdout, cursor } = await ws.shellOutput(server.id, { waitMs: 5_000 });
    console.info(stdout, cursor); // pass `since: cursor` to read only what comes next
    await ws.shellKill(server.id); // kills the whole process tree

    ws.writeTodos([{ content: "Fix the rounding bug", status: "completed" }]); // todo_write
    return ws.readTodos().counts; // todo_read
  } finally {
    await ws.dispose(); // kills every background command; the workspace refuses new commands
  }
}
```

- `list_dir({ path?, depth?, ignore? })` → `{ path, entries: [{ path, type, size?, depth }], truncated }`; `denyPaths` always hidden, `list.ignore` (default `node_modules`, `.git`) hidden from listings, symlinks reported but never followed.
- `multi_edit({ path, edits, expectHash? })` → `{ path, edits, replacements, hash }`; same uniqueness rules as `edit_file`, at most 100 edits.
- Background: `shell_output({ id, since?, waitMs? })` → `{ stdout, stderr, cursor, droppedBytes, truncated, status, exitCode }`; only the newest `shell.maxOutputBytes` per command are kept. States `"running"`, `"exited"`, `"killed"`, `"timed-out"`. Unknown id → `WorkspaceJobError`. Background commands outlive the agent run; `dispose()` (or process exit) kills them. Only processes the workspace spawned are ever signalled.
- Todos: one in-memory list per workspace, shared with `readonly()` / `scope()`; `todo_write` replaces the whole list (≤ 100 items, status `pending` / `in_progress` / `completed`).
- `run_shell`'s model-supplied `timeoutMs` can only lower `shell.timeoutMs`.

## `grep` is ReDoS-bounded

The model supplies `pattern` freely, so `grep` treats it as untrusted input before compiling it into a `RegExp`: patterns over 200 characters and patterns matching a nested-quantifier shape (`(x+)+`, `(x*)*`, `(x+)*`, `(x*)+`-style groups — the classic catastrophic-backtracking shape) are rejected up front as a `WorkspacePolicyError` `type: "unsafe-pattern"`, before any regex is compiled. Any scanned line longer than 2000 characters is skipped (not tested), bounding the worst-case backtracking cost of any single call regardless of pattern shape.

## Read windows and the byte ceiling

`readFile()` and the `read_file` tool return the same result for the same arguments: a `cat -n` numbered window plus `{ startLine, endLine, totalLines, totalBytes, truncated, bytesCapped, hash }`.

- The window starts at `offset` (`startLine` on the tool) and holds at most `limit` lines (default `read.defaultLines`, else 2000).
- `read.maxBytes` caps the UTF-8 bytes of the returned `content` itself — line-number prefixes and newlines count. Whole lines are kept while they fit; the first line that doesn't is cut on a **character boundary** (never mid-character), so a single very long line still comes back bounded. `bytesCapped` is `true` whenever the cap cut anything, and `endLine` is the last line included, possibly partially.
- `truncated` is `true` when anything after `content` was withheld — later lines (by `limit`, the default window or the cap) or the tail of `endLine`.
- `hash` is always the SHA-256 of the **whole file**, not the window, so it is a valid `expectHash` whatever was returned. `totalBytes` is the whole file's size.
- No `maxBytes` ⇒ no byte cap (only the line window applies).

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd, read: { maxBytes: 64_000, defaultLines: 400 } });
const page = await ws.readFile("dist/bundle.js");
if (page.bytesCapped) console.warn(`Only part of line ${page.endLine} fit in the read budget.`);
```

## Cancelling a command

`exec()` accepts a per-call `signal`; `run_shell` and `run_tests` pass the agent run's signal (the dispatch `ctx.signal`) automatically, so cancelling the agent run stops the command it is waiting on.

- Already aborted ⇒ the command is **not started** (`exitCode: 130`).
- Aborted mid-run ⇒ the whole process tree is SIGKILLed, as on a timeout.
- Either way the result says `cancelled: true` — it resolves, it doesn't throw — and `cancelled` and `timedOut` are never both `true`. Branch on those flags, not on the exit code.
- The signal belongs to that one call; the workspace never stores it, so one workspace can serve many runs. The abort listener is removed once the command settles.

```ts
const controller = new AbortController();
const pending = ws.exec("npm test", { signal: controller.signal, timeoutMs: 120_000 });
controller.abort();
const { cancelled } = await pending; // true
```

A custom `WorkspaceBackend` receives the signal as `exec(command, { signal })` and should follow the same rules, reporting `cancelled: true` in its result.

## Read-before-edit (the stale-hash guard)

`readFile` returns a SHA-256 `hash` of the full file. Pass it to `editFile`'s `expectHash`; if the file changed since you read it, the edit is rejected as stale so you re-read before clobbering. `editFile` also requires the `oldString` to be **exact and unique** — pass `replaceAll: true` to replace every occurrence, or include more surrounding context to disambiguate.

Writes, edits and removes of the same path run one after another, even when the agent dispatches tool calls concurrently: of two edits pinned to the same `expectHash`, the second is rejected as stale instead of silently overwriting the first. `read.maxBytes` bounds what a read returns, not memory — the whole file is still read and hashed.

## Errors flow as data, not throws

Policy and edit failures are typed errors extending the `@warlock.js/ai` `AIError` base. Inside a tool the `tool()` wrapper catches them and surfaces them in `{ error }`, so the agent reads the failure and self-corrects. Branch on `.type`:

```ts
import { WorkspacePolicyError, WorkspaceEditError } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

try {
  await ws.exec("rm -rf /");
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof WorkspacePolicyError && error.type === "denied-command") {
    console.warn(`Blocked: ${error.command}`);
  }
}
```

- `WorkspacePolicyError.type`: `"path-escape"` (jail escape / deny glob) | `"denied-command"` (the shell policy refused the line — `reason` says why) | `"unsafe-pattern"` (`grep` pattern too long or nested-quantifier ReDoS shape).
- `WorkspaceEditError.type`: `"not-found"` | `"not-unique"` | `"stale-hash"` (+ `editIndex` for `multiEdit`).
- `WorkspaceJobError.type`: `"not-found"` (unknown background command id).

## Composition — `readonly()` and `scope()`

```ts
const ro = ws.readonly(); // vends only read/grep/glob; mutating direct methods reject
const api = ws.scope("packages/api"); // a sub-jailed workspace rooted at the subdir
```

`readonly()` is the least-privilege reviewer projection — `tools.all()` on it returns `read_file`, `list_dir`, `grep`, `glob` and the todo tools only, and `writeFile` / `editFile` / `multiEdit` / `exec` / `startShell` / `shellKill` / `mkdir` / `remove` throw a `WorkspacePolicyError`. Projections share the workspace's background commands and todo list. `scope(subdir)` narrows `cwd` to `join(cwd, subdir)` (same sub-policies, same backend), so a per-package agent gets a tighter blast radius.

## Hermetic tests with the mock backend

`backend: "mock"` swaps the local disk for an in-memory `Map` + scripted `exec` — same policy, same tool/method surface, no filesystem:

```ts
const ws = ai.workspace({ cwd: "/srv/app", backend: "mock", shell: { allow: ["npm"] } });
// (Seed files / scripted commands via createMockBackend when constructing a backend directly.)
```

## See also

- The `build-loop-agent` topic — wiring these tools into a read → edit → test agent loop.
- The `run-ai-agent` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — running the agent that consumes `ws.tools.all()`.
- The `define-ai-tool` topic of the `warlock-js-ai` skill — the `tool()` / `ToolContract` seam every workspace tool is built on.

## Complete bounded-read and cancellation example

```ts
import { workspace } from "@warlock.js/ai-workspace";

export async function inspectWorkspace(cwd: string) {
  const ws = workspace({
    cwd,
    read: { maxBytes: 64_000, defaultLines: 400 },
    shell: { allow: ["node"], inheritEnv: ["PATH"] },
  });
  const page = await ws.readFile("package.json");
  console.info(page.bytesCapped, page.endLine, page.hash);

  const controller = new AbortController();
  controller.abort();
  const result = await ws.exec('node -e "console.log(1)"', { signal: controller.signal });
  if (result.cancelled) console.info("Command cancelled before it started");
  return page;
}
```

The caller supplies an absolute existing workspace root. The already-aborted
signal demonstrates the no-spawn path; a later abort also kills a running
command's process tree. The byte ceiling limits returned content, while the
hash still describes the whole file.

# Run coding CLIs as agents

`@warlock.js/ai-cli` drives vendor coding CLIs headless. One run is one session. The vendor's stream is reduced to one event model, and `done()` resolves the final text, the usage and a session reference you can resume. It ships fourteen adapters: Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity, Qwen Code, Kimi Code, Cursor, Copilot, Grok Build, OpenCode, Amp, Factory Droid, Mistral Vibe, Aider and Reasonix. The CLIs themselves are not installed by the package.

## Run a prompt and read the events

```ts
import { cli } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

const claude = cli.claudeCode({ model: "sonnet", apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY });
const session = await claude.run("Fix the failing test in src/math.spec.ts", {
  cwd: "/srv/acme-api",
});

for await (const event of session.events) {
  switch (event.type) {
    case "session.started":
      console.log("session", event.sessionRef);
      break;
    case "message":
      if (event.delta) process.stdout.write(event.text);
      break;
    case "tool.call":
      console.log("\ntool", event.name, event.input);
      break;
    case "tool.result":
      console.log(event.isError ? "failed:" : "ok:", event.output.slice(0, 200));
      break;
    case "usage":
      console.log("tokens", event.usage.total);
      break;
    case "error":
      console.error(event.fatal ? "fatal:" : "warning:", event.message);
      break;
    case "session.ended":
      console.log("ended", event.status, event.exitCode);
      break;
  }
}

const result = await session.done();

if (result.status === "completed") {
  console.log(result.text, result.usage, result.sessionRef);
} else {
  console.error(result.status, result.error, result.stderr);
}
```

- **`session.events`** replays from the first event on every iteration, and ends after `session.ended`.
- **`done()` never rejects.** Branch on `status`: `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `timeout`.
- **`text`** is the vendor's final record, or else the last assistant message. `messages` holds every complete message.
- **`run()` rejects only for setup problems,** with a `CliError` whose `type` is one of:
  - `not-found` — the executable is not on `PATH`;
  - `capability` — `--help` lacks a needed flag; the error carries `flag` and `version`;
  - `probe-failed` — the CLI's help could not be read;
  - `unsupported-option` — the adapter cannot honour an option;
  - `prompt-transport` — the prompt fits neither argv nor stdin.

`ai.cli` is the same namespace once `import "@warlock.js/ai-cli"` has run.

## Resume, cancel, time out

```ts
import { cli } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

const codex = cli.codex({ cwd: "/srv/acme-api" });
const plan = await (await codex.run("Plan the billing refactor; do not edit files")).done();

const controller = new AbortController();
const step = await codex.run("Implement step 1 of the plan", {
  resume: plan.sessionRef,
  signal: controller.signal,
  timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000,
});

setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 60_000); // or step.cancel()

const outcome = await step.done();

console.log(outcome.status); // "cancelled" after the abort
```

Abort and timeout kill the whole process tree. On POSIX that is the CLI's process group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after `killGraceMs`, default 2000); on Windows it is `taskkill /T /F` on its PID. A run whose signal is already aborted never spawns.

## Permissions — bypass is opt-in

```ts
import { cli } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

// Default "standard": the CLI's own non-interactive rules; anything needing approval is refused.
const reviewer = cli.copilot({ cwd: "/srv/acme-api" });

// "bypass": every tool call approved without asking. Only for a sandboxed run.
const fixer = cli.grok({ cwd: "/sandbox/acme-api", permission: "bypass" });

const review = await (await reviewer.run("Review src/billing for bugs")).done();
const fix = await (
  await fixer.run("Apply the fixes from the review", { permission: "bypass" })
).done();

console.log(review.text, fix.status);
```

What `"standard"` allows depends on the vendor:

- **Read-only:** Codex and Droid. Allow edits with `args: ["-c", "sandbox_mode=workspace-write"]` (Codex) or `args: ["--auto", "medium"]` (Droid).
- **Permissive:** OpenCode and Amp.
- **Refused:** Kimi Code always approves in print mode, so its adapter rejects `"standard"` and needs `"bypass"`.

## MCP servers, secrets and homes

```ts
import { cli } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

const claude = cli.claudeCode({
  apiKey: process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, // exported as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, never argv
  inheritEnv: ["GITHUB_TOKEN"], // minimal system env + these names only
});

const session = await claude.run("Triage the open issues", {
  mcp: {
    tracker: {
      type: "stdio",
      command: "npx",
      args: ["-y", "@acme/tracker-mcp"],
      env: { TRACKER_TOKEN: process.env.TRACKER_TOKEN ?? "" },
    },
    docs: {
      type: "http",
      url: "https://mcp.acme.dev/mcp",
      headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.DOCS_TOKEN ?? ""}` },
    },
  },
});

console.log((await session.done()).text);
```

**MCP servers.** They are written as a mode-0600 file inside a private per-run directory (mode 0700), never into argv, and the file is removed after the run. CLIs that read MCP only from their config home (Kimi, Grok, Cursor, Droid, Antigravity, Mistral Vibe, Reasonix) need the default private home. Aider has no MCP support.

**Homes.** The `home` option takes one of:

- `"private"` (default) — a fresh config home per run;
- an absolute path — a home you own, for example one you logged in to;
- `"inherit"` — your normal config.

The adapter's home variable (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, `CODEX_HOME`, `COPILOT_HOME`, `GROK_HOME`, …) is pointed at it.

## Use a CLI as an `ai.agent` model

```ts
import { ai, budget } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import { cli } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

const coder = cli.codex({ cwd: "/srv/acme-api" });

const reviewer = ai.agent({
  model: coder.model({ name: "codex-reviewer" }),
  middleware: [budget({ maxTokens: 200_000 })],
});

const review = await reviewer.execute("Review the last commit for bugs.");

console.log(review.text, review.usage.total);
```

How the model behaves:

- **One fresh CLI session per call.** System messages lead the prompt, and a history is rendered as a transcript.
- **The CLI uses its own tools.** A call with agent `tools` is refused; give the CLI `mcp` servers instead.
- **Streaming yields the final answer once the session ends.**
- **A failed run throws `CliError` with `type: "run-failed"`,** so `fallbackModel` works.
- **Pass `pricing`** for USD cost.

## Pitfalls

- Install and log in to the vendor CLI yourself. With the default private home, authenticate with `apiKey`/`env`.
- `effort` is refused by CLIs without an effort control (Qwen Code, Kimi, Cursor, Mistral Vibe), and `model` is refused by Amp. Nothing is silently ignored.
- `args` is passed verbatim; never put a token there.
- The vendor table in the docs ("Vendor adapters") lists each CLI's flags, stream format, and the version it was verified against.


## write-a-cli-adapter  `@warlock.js/ai-cli/write-a-cli-adapter/SKILL.md`

---
name: write-a-cli-adapter
description: 'Write a CliAdapter for a coding CLI that @warlock.js/ai-cli does not ship. Triggers: `CliAdapter`, `CliLaunchContext`, `CliLaunchPlan`, `CliStreamParser`, `cli.custom`, `createCliAgent`, `jsonLinesParser`, `stringField`, `numberField`, `usageOf`, `mcpServersJson`, `jsonFile`, `toToml`, `mapEffort`, `argvPrompt`, `promptFile`, `requirePrivateHome`, `unsupportedOption`, `createClaudeStreamParser`, `helpLists`, `missingFlags`, `requires`, `verification`; ''add a new coding CLI'', ''support another agent CLI'', ''parse a vendor JSONL stream'', ''adapter for a new CLI version''; typical import `import { cli, jsonLinesParser, type CliAdapter } from "@warlock.js/ai-cli"`. Skip: using the built-in adapters — the `run-cli-agents` topic.'

# Write a CLI adapter

An adapter is a plain object with two jobs: `plan(context)` builds argv, stdin, environment and files for one run, and `parser(context)` turns stdout lines into the unified events. The runner does the rest: executable lookup, the Windows `.cmd` rules, the capability probe, homes, secrets, cancellation and the result.

```ts
import path from "node:path";
import {
  cli,
  jsonFile,
  jsonLinesParser,
  mcpServersJson,
  numberField,
  stringField,
  usageOf,
  type CliAdapter,
  type CliLaunchFile,
} from "@warlock.js/ai-cli";

export const acmeAdapter: CliAdapter = {
  name: "acme",
  title: "Acme Agent",
  command: "acme",
  apiKeyEnv: ["ACME_API_KEY"],
  homeEnv: ["ACME_HOME"],
  transports: ["argv", "stdin"],
  effort: false,
  mcp: true,
  probe: { help: [["run", "--help"]], version: ["--version"] },
  verification: {
    version: "3.2.0",
    verifiedBy: "help",
    sources: ["https://acme.dev/docs/cli"],
    checkedAt: "2026-10-17",
  },
  plan(context) {
    const args = ["run", "--json"];
    const requires = ["--json"];
    const files: CliLaunchFile[] = [];

    if (context.model !== undefined) {
      args.push("--model", context.model);
      requires.push("--model");
    }

    if (context.resume !== undefined) {
      args.push("--resume", context.resume);
      requires.push("--resume");
    }

    if (context.permission === "bypass") {
      args.push("--yes-to-all");
      requires.push("--yes-to-all");
    }

    if (context.mcp !== undefined) {
      const file = path.join(context.runDir, "mcp.json");

      files.push({ path: file, content: jsonFile({ mcpServers: mcpServersJson(context.mcp) }) });
      args.push("--mcp-config", file);
      requires.push("--mcp-config");
    }

    return {
      args,
      tail: context.transport === "argv" ? [context.prompt] : [],
      stdin: context.transport === "stdin" ? context.prompt : undefined,
      env: context.home !== undefined ? { ACME_HOME: context.home } : undefined,
      files,
      requires,
    };
  },
  parser: () =>
    jsonLinesParser((record) => {
      switch (record.type) {
        case "start":
          return [{ type: "session.started", sessionRef: stringField(record, "id") }];
        case "text":
          return [{ type: "message", text: stringField(record, "text") ?? "", delta: true }];
        case "tool":
          return [
            {
              type: "tool.call",
              id: String(record.id),
              name: String(record.name),
              input: record.input,
            },
          ];
        case "tool_done":
          return [
            {
              type: "tool.result",
              id: String(record.id),
              output: String(record.output),
              isError: record.ok !== true,
            },
          ];
        case "usage":
          return [
            {
              type: "usage",
              cumulative: true,
              usage: usageOf({
                input: numberField(record, "in"),
                output: numberField(record, "out"),
              }),
            },
          ];
        case "error":
          return [{ type: "error", message: String(record.message), fatal: true }];
        default:
          return [];
      }
    }),
};

const acme = cli.custom(acmeAdapter);
const result = await (await acme.run("Add a health check endpoint", { cwd: "/srv/api" })).done();

console.log(result.status, result.text);
```

## Rules

- **`requires`:** list every flag and subcommand the plan uses, spelled as `--help` prints it. The probe then fails the run up front, naming the flag and the installed version, if a release drops or renames one. Leave out only a flag the CLI accepts but no longer documents, and say so in a comment.
- **Secrets:** never put one in `args` or `tail`. Use `env`, or a file under `context.runDir` (written 0600, removed after the run). A home-level config file may be written only when `context.homeIsPrivate`; `requirePrivateHome(context, adapter, "MCP servers")` fails closed otherwise.
- **Prompt placement:** `tail` goes after the caller's `args`. Wrap a positional prompt in `argvPrompt(prompt)`, so a prompt starting with `-` is not read as a flag. For a `"file"` transport, `promptFile(context)` writes the prompt into the run directory.
- **Effort:** `mapEffort(effort, { low: "low", high: "high" })` follows the framework clamping rule. Set `effort: true` only when you map it. The runner refuses `effort` for adapters that do not.
- **Unsupported options:** `throw unsupportedOption(adapter, "why")` for an option the CLI cannot honour; never drop it silently.
- **Failures:** report a vendor failure as `{ type: "error", fatal: true }`, so a CLI that exits 0 still ends `failed`.
- **Late session ids:** if the id arrives only at the end, return it from the parser's `sessionRef()`. If the CLI writes its result to a file, point it at `context.runDir` and read the file in the parser's `end()`.
- **Claude-style streams:** for a CLI that reproduces Claude Code's `stream-json`, reuse `createClaudeStreamParser({ usage: "anthropic" | "inclusive" })`.
- **Verification:** record `verification` — the version, the sources, and `"help"` or `"docs"`.

## Test without the real CLI

```ts
// acme-adapter.spec.ts — `acmeAdapter` from above; `readFileSync` from "node:fs",
// `missingFlags` from "@warlock.js/ai-cli", `expect`/`it` from "vitest".
it("normalizes a recorded stream and needs only listed flags", () => {
  const parser = acmeAdapter.parser({
    prompt: "x",
    transport: "argv",
    cwd: "/work",
    permission: "standard",
    homeIsPrivate: true,
    runDir: "/tmp/run",
    platform: "linux",
  });
  const events = readFileSync("fixtures/acme/stream.jsonl", "utf8")
    .split("\n")
    .flatMap((line) => parser.line(line));

  expect(events[0]).toMatchObject({ type: "session.started" });

  const plan = acmeAdapter.plan({
    prompt: "x",
    transport: "argv",
    cwd: "/work",
    model: "fast",
    permission: "bypass",
    homeIsPrivate: true,
    runDir: "/tmp/run",
    platform: "linux",
  });

  expect(missingFlags(readFileSync("fixtures/acme/help.txt", "utf8"), plan.requires)).toEqual([]);
});
```
