## create-a-warlock-project  `create-warlock/create-a-warlock-project/SKILL.md`

---
name: create-a-warlock-project
description: "Create a Warlock project with the canonical scaffold, package selection, and project conventions."
---

# create-warlock — scaffold a new project

`create-warlock` builds a fresh Warlock.js project: it copies the `warlock` template, substitutes the project name, wires the chosen database driver into `.env` (or, when you opt out with `--db=none`, removes `src/config/database.ts`), derives `agent-kit` targets into the generated project, then delegates every optional package install to the project's own `warlock add` so dependency versions are never duplicated by the scaffolder.

## The shape

```bash
# Default: choose API-only or full-stack web, then a database unless a DB flag already answered it
npx create-warlock my-app

# Fully headless — one command scaffolds the whole app, no prompts at all
npx create-warlock my-app --yes --db=postgres --features=test,redis --ai=ai-openai

# The one structural fork
npx create-warlock my-web-app --yes --stack=web

# No database at all
npx create-warlock my-api --yes --no-db --features=test

# The full long-form wizard, one prompt at a time
npx create-warlock --interactive
```

The first positional argument is the project name; it also becomes the directory created under the current working directory. If that directory already exists, the command aborts — it never overwrites.

## Three modes

1. **Default (a TTY, no `--yes`, no `--interactive`)** — asks the project name (if not already given), API-only or full-stack web (`--stack`), then a database unless `--db` or `--no-db` already supplied it. The stack is the only choice that changes the generated app's shape.
2. **`--yes` (or no TTY at all — CI, a script, an agent harness)** — fully headless. Every answer comes from a flag or its default; nothing is ever prompted, and stdin is never read.
3. **`--interactive` (alias `--customize`)** — the full long-form wizard: project name, package manager, database driver, features, AI providers, lint/format toolchain, git, JWT — one prompt after another, exactly like earlier `create-warlock` releases.

**Without a terminal, `--yes` is not required.** When stdin is not a TTY — CI, a
script, a container, an agent harness — the scaffolder does not try to prompt,
regardless of which of the three modes was requested. If the flags already
answer everything it needs, it simply scaffolds. Prompting is the fallback,
not the precondition.

Only a question that genuinely cannot be answered stops the run, and in practice
that is just the project name, the one required answer with no default:

```
A project name is required and no terminal is available to ask for one. Pass it as
the first argument or --name=<name>. Non-interactive flags: --yes, --pm=<npm|yarn|pnpm>,
--db=<driver>|--no-db, --features=<list>, --ai=<list>, --lint=<oxc|eslint>, --git|--no-git, --jwt|--no-jwt.
```

## After scaffolding: the decisions summary

Because almost every choice defaults silently, `create-warlock` prints what it
decided right after scaffolding, e.g.:

```
Using npm · database: none · lint: oxc · agent-kit targets: claude
Features: none
  change these — package manager: --pm, database: --db/--no-db, agents: --agents,
  features: --features, ai: --ai, lint: --lint, git: --git/--no-git, jwt: --jwt/--no-jwt — or
  re-run with --interactive for the full wizard.
```

## Flags

| Flag                           | Takes value | Default                                                             | Purpose                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `<positional>` / `--name`      | yes         | — (required)                                                        | Project name + target directory.                                                                                       |
| `--stack`                      | yes         | `api`                                                               | `api` or `web` — the structural choice; `web` seeds the `web` feature by default.                                      |
| `--db`                         | yes         | `mongodb`                                                           | Database driver key (`mongodb`, `postgres`, or `none`).                                                                |
| `--no-db`                      | no          | —                                                                   | Opt out of a database — shorthand for `--db=none`.                                                                     |
| `--pm`                         | yes         | inferred (`npm_config_user_agent` / system)                         | Package manager — must be one of `npm` / `yarn` / `pnpm` / `bun`; anything else is rejected before scaffolding starts. |
| `--features`                   | yes (CSV)   | none, or `["web"]` when `--stack=web` and `--features` is not given | Comma-separated optional feature keys. An explicit `--features` always wins over the `--stack` default.                |
| `--lint`                       | yes         | `oxc`                                                               | `oxc` (Oxlint/Oxfmt) or `eslint` (ESLint/Prettier, deprecated); unknown or missing values fail before writes.          |
| `--ai`                         | yes (CSV)   | none                                                                | Comma-separated AI provider keys (auto-pulls `@warlock.js/ai`).                                                        |
| `--agents`                     | yes (CSV)   | `claude`                                                            | Comma-separated `agent-kit` targets — see below.                                                                       |
| `--git` / `--no-git`           | no          | off                                                                 | Initialize a Git repo (`git init` + `main` branch + initial commit).                                                   |
| `--jwt` / `--no-jwt`           | no          | off                                                                 | Generate JWT secrets via the project's `jwt` script.                                                                   |
| `--yes` / `-y`                 | no          | off                                                                 | Fully headless mode.                                                                                                   |
| `--interactive`, `--customize` | no          | off                                                                 | Restore the full long-form wizard.                                                                                     |

With `--pm=pnpm`, the scaffold reads `pnpm --version` and records install-script
approvals (esbuild, and Sharp when the `image` feature is selected) where that
version reads them: `allowBuilds` in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` on pnpm 10.26+, 11
and 12; that file plus `onlyBuiltDependencies` on 10.5–10.25; and, before 10.5,
no workspace file (those versions reject one without `packages:`) but
`pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` in `package.json`. An explicit existing denial is
retained. If selected feature dependencies do
not install, JWT generation is skipped and reported rather than retried through
the package manager.

Value flags accept either `--db=postgres` or `--db postgres`. Unknown `--pm` / `--db` / `--features` / `--ai` / `--agents` / `--lint` values fail fast before any write or install.

`--help`/`-h` and `--version`/`-v` short-circuit before anything else — no prompt, filesystem write, or network call, and `--help` wins even over a positional project name. `--version` prints the installed `create-warlock` version. `--help` lists every flag above together with its default.

## `--agents` and agent-kit targets

`--agents` picks which `agent-kit` targets the generated project derives
docs/skills for (written into the scaffolded `package.json`'s `agentKit.targets`
when it differs from the default). The default, `claude`, is a tiny built-in
fallback that always works — even fully offline. Any other target
(`cursor`, `codex`, `kiro`, `copilot`, `antigravity`, `opencode`, `amp`,
`goose`, …) is validated against the list published at
https://mongez.js.org/agent-kit/llms.txt, fetched once and cached locally. If
that fetch fails for an explicitly requested non-default target, the run fails
visibly and names every target it _could_ determine — it never silently
guesses.

## Valid keys

**Database drivers** (`--db`):

| Key        | Default port | Status                                                                   |
| ---------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `mongodb`  | 27017        | available                                                                |
| `postgres` | 5432         | available                                                                |
| `mysql`    | 3306         | coming soon (disabled in the wizard)                                     |
| `none`     | —            | opt out — no driver, no driver package, `src/config/database.ts` removed |

**Features** (`--features`): `react`, `react-email`, `mail`, `ses`, `image`, `s3`, `redis`, `scheduler`, `herald`, `socket`, `test`, `access`, `web`, `tailwind`, `shadcn`, `notifications`.

**AI providers / packages** (`--ai`): `ai-openai`, `ai-google`, `ai-anthropic`, `ai-bedrock`, `ai-ollama`, plus the capability packages `ai-tools`, `ai-panoptic`, `ai-workspace`. Any pick auto-pulls the core `@warlock.js/ai` package.

## Interactive selectors

The default flow and Customize both use the same database selector: MongoDB
and PostgreSQL, with MySQL shown as disabled, then **None**. **None** is
`--db=none` / `--no-db`: no driver
feature is added and `src/config/database.ts` is removed. A supplied database
flag skips the default-flow selector.

In Customize's AI multiselect, pressing Enter with no selection skips AI.
**None** is the last option and also skips AI when it is the sole choice.
Selecting **None** alongside a provider or capability is invalid: the wizard
shows a warning and returns to that selector with the non-**None** choices
retained for correction. Noninteractive `--ai` flag semantics are unchanged.

> The scaffolder holds **no dependency versions** for these — the keys map to `warlock add <key>`, whose feature map in `@warlock.js/core` is the single source of truth. A feature that resolves there will install; one that does not is rejected.

## What gets generated

```
my-app/
├─ .env                         # copied from .env.example, name + DB driver/port substituted
├─ .env.example
├─ .gitignore                   # renamed from the template's _.gitignore
├─ package.json                 # "name" set to the project name
├─ tsconfig.json
├─ warlock.config.ts
└─ src/
   ├─ config/                   # app, auth, cache, database, http, log, mail, repository, storage, tests, validation
   └─ app/
      ├─ auth/                  # controllers, schema, services, requests, utils, OTP model + migration
      ├─ users/                 # model, migration, resource, repository, create + list controllers, schema, events, seeds, commands
      ├─ posts/                 # sample module — model, migration, resource, schema, create + update controllers
      ├─ uploads/               # routes.ts mounts core's uploadedFileController; named image variants go in src/config/uploads.ts
      └─ shared/                # router/locale utils, home page, scheduler
```

The template ships a working auth module (login / logout / logout-all / refresh / me / forgot + reset password via OTP), a `users` module, and a sample `posts` module — all using the current framework surface: schemas via `v` from `@warlock.js/seal`, controllers typed with `GuardedRequestHandler` carrying a `.validation = { schema }`, models on `@warlock.js/cascade`, and declarative migrations via `Migration.create`.

## Setup steps the scaffolder runs

1. Copy template → substitute name → wire `DB_DRIVER` / `DB_PORT` into `.env` (or, for `--db=none`, remove `src/config/database.ts`) → record non-default `--agents` targets into `package.json`'s `agentKit.targets`.
2. Install base dependencies (so the `warlock` binary exists).
3. `warlock add <driver> <features...> <ai...> --no-install`, then one batched install. The `<driver>` is omitted for `--db=none`.
4. `git init` (if `--git`).
5. `jwt` script (if `--jwt`) — otherwise `warlock --warm-cache`.
6. Print the decisions summary.

Failures surface the error and halt; there is no rollback. After it finishes, `cd my-app` and run the dev server.

## Gotchas

- **The target directory must not already exist** — the command exits rather than merge into it.
- **`--db=none` / `--no-db` scaffolds without a database** — no driver, no driver package, and `src/config/database.ts` is deleted. The framework's database connector is gated on that file, so the app boots with no database. The `DB_*` lines stay in `.env` (harmless) as a template for adding one back later.
- **`--ai` never takes `ai` itself.** Pick a provider (`ai-openai`, …); the core `@warlock.js/ai` package is pulled in transitively.
- **`mysql` is disabled** in the wizard; passing `--db=mysql` resolves the driver record but the driver is marked coming-soon.
- **Versions are not the scaffolder's job.** If a feature installs the wrong version, the fix is in core's `warlock add` feature map, not here.

## See also

- The `run-app` topic of the `warlock-js-core` skill — `warlock dev` / `build` / `start` once the project exists.
- The `create-module` topic of the `warlock-js-core` skill — generate a new module inside the project.
- The `add-connector` topic of the `warlock-js-core` skill — what `warlock add` wires when a feature pulls a connector.

The project-ready summary wraps the complete feature list to your terminal width.
Terminals narrower than 50 columns get a plain list; piped output uses 80 columns.

## Custom feature groups

`--customize` opens a section menu for optional features. Open a section to edit
its checklist; **Select all** includes the remaining features while preserving
items you explicitly unticked. The category cursor stays on the last edited
section. Section
counts update when returning to the menu, and **Continue** keeps the selection.
Flags preselect their existing feature keys. Both menus and checklists retain
terminal paging. The decisions overview previews up to six feature/AI keys with
a total count; the success screen shows the complete list.

## Choose the linter and formatter

`--lint=oxc` is the default. It also accepts `--lint oxc` and installs exact
`oxlint@1.88.0` and `oxfmt@0.73.0` versions, emits `.oxlintrc.json` and
`.oxfmtrc.json`, and removes the template's ESLint/Prettier configs and dependencies.
Pass `--lint=eslint` to opt in to ESLint/Prettier. The custom wizard prompts for
the same choice; a flag preselects it.

```bash
# Default: Oxlint + Oxfmt, TypeScript 7.0.2
npm create warlock@latest my-app -- --yes

# Explicit opt-in: ESLint + Prettier, TypeScript 6.0.3
npm create warlock@latest my-eslint-app -- --lint=eslint --yes
```

Both choices provide `lint`/`format` and non-mutating `lint:check`/`format:check`
scripts. Oxc projects also configure VS Code format-on-save with the official
`oxc.oxc-vscode` formatter, use `source.fixAll.oxc` for lint fixes and recommend
that extension. The ESLint toolchain retains its Prettier/ESLint editor settings.
Oxc config enables `devServer.healthCheckers: { eslint: false, oxlint: true }` and
leaves TypeScript health checks enabled. Style matches the template's 100-column,
double-quote, semicolon and trailing-comma settings. Import sorting is on in
`.oxfmtrc.json`, kept to one block like the ESLint toolchain's
`@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports`:

```json
{ "sortImports": { "newlinesBetween": false, "internalPattern": ["app/", "web/", "@shared/"] } }
```

`format` (`npm run format`) orders built-ins, packages, internal aliases,
then relative imports. Neither formatter deletes unused imports. ESLint reports
them through `unused-imports/no-unused-imports`; Oxlint uses `no-unused-vars`.
Scripts in both toolchains call local binaries
(`eslint --fix ./src --max-warnings=0`, `tsc --noEmit`), never `npx`.

## TypeScript 7 in 5.32

Default Oxlint/Oxfmt projects pin `typescript` to `7.0.2`; `tsc` is the native Go compiler.
The template uses `module: "ESNext"`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, explicit
Node types, and `paths` relative to its tsconfig, without `baseUrl`.
Existing apps must remove `baseUrl`, rebase alias targets, and replace
`moduleResolution: "node"` / `"node10"` before typechecking.

Explicit `--lint=eslint` projects pin `typescript` to **6.0.3**, the newest version
supported by typescript-eslint. Its parser requires the JavaScript compiler API
removed in TypeScript 7, and its declared peer range is `>=4.8.4 <6.1.0`
([parser package metadata](https://registry.npmjs.org/@typescript-eslint/parser/8.71.2)).
Both modes use the same tsconfig settings above, which are valid in TypeScript 6.
ESLint mode prints a deprecation warning naming removal in 5.34.0 and the Oxc migration command. Both modes install with every supported package manager.

### Prettier import order in ESLint mode

The ESLint scaffold’s `@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports` uses Babel instead of
the compiler API. Keep these options in `.prettierrc.json`:

```json
{
  "plugins": ["@ianvs/prettier-plugin-sort-imports"],
  "importOrder": ["<BUILTIN_MODULES>", "<THIRD_PARTY_MODULES>", "^(app|web|@shared)/", "^[.]"],
  "importOrderParserPlugins": ["typescript", "jsx", "decorators"]
}
```

Leave `importOrderTypeScriptVersion` at its default to keep type and value imports
separate. Run `npm run format`, then `npm run lint:check`; formatting preserves
unused imports, and `npm run lint` can apply ESLint’s unused-import fixes.

## Migrate to Oxlint and Oxfmt in 5.33

ESLint + Prettier are deprecated in 5.33.0 and will be removed in **5.34.0**.
New apps should use `--lint=oxc`. To migrate an existing app, install the new
core release and `ts-morph`, then run:

```bash
npx warlock upgrade --from 5.32 --to 5.33.0 --dry-run
npx warlock upgrade --from 5.32 --to 5.33.0
npm install
npm run format
npm run lint:check
npx warlock check
```

Review every reported `file:line`: customized configs are preserved and need
manual translation before removal. The codemod installs the template's Oxlint
and Oxfmt versions and pins TypeScript to 7.0.2. It replaces standard lint/format
scripts, removes legacy dependencies, and deletes only recognized generated
configs. A generated `.prettierignore` becomes `.oxfmtignore`. Existing Oxc
configs are preserved. `--dry-run --json` reports the same planned changes
without writing files.

Explicit deprecated ESLint scaffolds set `devServer.healthCheckers.eslint: true`;
existing apps must set this themselves to retain background ESLint checking.

Oxc formatting scripts explicitly read `.gitignore` and `.oxfmtignore`. Oxfmt
0.73 otherwise defaults to `.prettierignore` (`oxfmt --help`); the explicit
paths make migrated ignore rules effective. The package template format gate
also defaults to Oxfmt; `--lint=eslint` is its deprecated compatibility mode.

# Warlock Devtools — full skills

> Package: `@warlock.js/devtools`

> Generated artifact. Concatenates every SKILL.md and reference file under `@warlock.js/devtools/skills/`. Re-run `node scripts/generate-llms.mjs` after any change.

## devtools-overview  `@warlock.js/devtools/devtools-overview/SKILL.md`

---
name: devtools-overview
description: 'Development-only dashboard for Warlock.js apps at `/__warlock`: request timeline (router + page middleware, loaders, render, deferred values), every SQL/Mongo query with EXPLAIN, N+1 warnings naming the file and line, a dev mailbox, logs, cache operations, AI traces per HTTP request (model, tokens, cost, cache hits, tools, retries, truncation, compaction), the route map and an API docs page (`/__warlock/docs`, the OpenAPI 3.1 document of the app rendered with Scalar or Swagger UI at `/__warlock/docs/swagger`, with OpenAPI and Postman downloads). Use for: "why is this page slow", "which queries does this request run", "find N+1 queries", "see the email my app just sent in dev", "open the dashboard", "browse my API docs in dev", "see the OpenAPI for my routes", "open Swagger UI for my API", "export my routes to Postman". Install with `warlock add devtools`; never registered in warlock.config.ts. Not this package: production monitoring/APM or OpenTelemetry export — use `http.tracing` hooks in @warlock.js/core; slow-query logging in production — subscribe to cascade `dataSourceRegistry.on("query")` yourself.'
---

# `@warlock.js/devtools` — overview

A dashboard for **development only**, served by your own app at `/__warlock`.
It shows what each request did: its timing waterfall, the queries it ran, the
cache operations, the logs, and any mail it sent.

## Install: one command, no config

```bash
warlock add devtools   # adds @warlock.js/devtools as a DEV dependency
warlock dev            # open http://localhost:<port>/__warlock
```

There's nothing to register. `warlock dev` loads devtools automatically when
the package is installed.

**Do not** add `devtoolsConnector()` to `warlock.config.ts`. Devtools is a
dev dependency, so a production install doesn't have it, and a config import
of it would fail to resolve there.

## Why it can't leak into production

1. **It isn't installed there.** Production installs omit dev dependencies.
2. **It refuses to run outside development.** If it's present anyway, it logs
   one warning (`@warlock.js/devtools only runs in development; it is not mounted`)
   and mounts nothing.
3. **It only answers loopback clients.** Every dashboard and API route answers
   404 unless the connection comes from `127.0.0.1` / `::1`. It checks the
   socket address, not `X-Forwarded-For`, so a forwarded-for header can't
   unlock it.

## What each panel shows

| Panel        | What you see                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Where it comes from                       |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| **Requests** | Each request with its status, duration and query count. Click one for a waterfall: router middleware, `page.middleware`, loaders, `page.cache` hit/miss, `render.shell`, `defer.settle`, with queries and cache ops placed on the same time axis. | core `registerTracingHooks()`             |
| **Queries**  | SQL + bindings or the Mongo command, duration, rows, and an **Explain** button (Postgres `SELECT` only; runs `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`, never `ANALYZE`)                                                                                            | cascade `dataSourceRegistry.on("query")`  |
| **N+1**      | `⚠ N+1: 12× "select … where post_id = $1" — src/app/posts/services/list-posts.service.ts:18`, shown on the request and printed in the terminal                                                                                                    | same query shape ≥ 5 times in one request |
| **Mail**     | Every mail sent in development: headers, HTML (sandboxed) and text, attachment names                                                                                                                                                              | core `mailEvents.onCaptured()`            |
| **Logs**     | Log entries per request, filterable by level and module                                                                                                                                                                                           | a logger channel                          |
| **Cache**    | hit / miss / set / removed / `invalidated` (tags, keys removed)                                                                                                                                                                                   | cache `cache.on(...)`                     |
| **Routes**   | Every HTTP route with its method, path, name and middleware                                                                                                                                                                                       | core router                               |
| **API**      | The app's API reference: every route with its parameters, request body, responses and auth                                                                                                                                                        | core `getDevelopmentOpenApiDocument()`    |

Work outside a request (boot, scheduler ticks, queue jobs) goes to a separate
background list, so it never clutters a request's timeline.

## AI runs alongside HTTP requests

The **AI** tab and each request's **AI runs** section display completed traces
from optional `@warlock.js/ai-panoptic`. If it cannot be imported, the tab shows
install/restart guidance and the other panels keep working.

```bash
warlock add devtools
pnpm add @warlock.js/ai @warlock.js/ai-panoptic
```

At app boot, enable observation, then restart `warlock dev`:

```ts
import { ai } from "@warlock.js/ai";
import "@warlock.js/ai-panoptic";
ai.config({ panoptic: { observeAll: true } });
```

No `dashboard: true` or extra listener port is needed. Existing `attach`,
middleware and explicit collection through Panoptic's built-in collector also
feed the panel. An installed but unobserved flow produces no trace.

- `DevtoolsAiRun` and `DevtoolsAiEvent` are public types from
  `@warlock.js/devtools`; `DevtoolsStreamEvent` includes the `ai` event.
- Read all runs with `GET /__warlock/api/ai`, or filter by an exact HTTP id with
  `GET /__warlock/api/ai?requestId=<encoded-id>`. Responses include `available`,
  `runs` and a root-usage `aggregate`; unavailable responses contain `message`.
- Inspect tools/timings, retry attempts and compaction records with
  `GET /__warlock/api/ai/runs/<encoded-trace-id>` (404 when evicted). The existing
  stream emits `ai` events with `{ traceId, requestId? }`.
- Model, input/output/cache-read/cache-write tokens and historical USD cost come
  from the trace, never a guessed price table. Unknown cost is unpriced. Root
  usage includes children already; do not sum all spans for a run total.
- Cache hits count trips reporting positive provider `cachedTokens`.
  Semantic-cache hits have no explicit report flag and remain unreported; zero
  tokens alone do not prove a hit. `—` means unreported rather than zero.
- `incomplete` status or normalized `AGENT_INCOMPLETE` / `AgentIncompleteError`
  marks truncation. Recovered truncated trips still contribute to their count.
- Compaction metadata includes applied/skipped agent decisions and provider
  compaction-block counts; summary content is omitted. Orchestrator result-only
  compaction cannot be reconstructed from a report-only trace.

A same-origin browser tool can consume the public types directly:

```ts
import type { DevtoolsAiEvent, DevtoolsAiRun, DevtoolsStreamEvent } from "@warlock.js/devtools";

const response = await fetch("/__warlock/api/ai?requestId=request-42");
const { runs }: { runs: DevtoolsAiRun[] } = await response.json();
console.log(runs.map((run) => [run.traceId, run.usage, run.cost]));

function handleStream(event: DevtoolsStreamEvent): void {
  if (event.type === "ai") {
    const update: DevtoolsAiEvent = event.data;
    console.log(update.traceId, update.requestId);
  }
}
handleStream({ type: "ai", data: { traceId: "run-42", requestId: "request-42" } });
```

Request correlation reads core's current request id at collection time, before
exporters. Concurrent/late runs can retain their async context. No id means
background; `sessionId` is never substituted. Replayed reports outside the
request cannot recover its context automatically.

Devtools retains its own content-free in-memory store, at most `maxRequests`
traces (200 by default), independently of HTTP request retention. Clear/shutdown
empties this view, leaving application exporter/cache stores alone. Boot-time
and persisted traces are not replayed. The source only attaches in development;
AI routes keep the same socket-loopback guard as every other panel.

## API docs

`/__warlock/docs` renders the app's OpenAPI 3.1 document with [Scalar](https://github.com/scalar/scalar); the dashboard's **API** tab shows the same page and has a **Scalar | Swagger UI** switch (remembered in the browser). `/__warlock/docs/swagger` renders the same document with [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). The document comes from `GET /__warlock/api/openapi.json`, built in-process by core's `getDevelopmentOpenApiDocument()` from the routes already registered, so it is the same generator as `warlock generate.openapi` and follows your edits with no CLI run. It covers API routes (not pages): paths, parameters, request bodies from Seal validation, responses from each handler's `responseSchema`, `401`/`422` and bearer/cookie security from `authMiddleware()`. See core's `generate-openapi` topic for what is documented and how to declare it.

- It answers `503` from `/__warlock/api/openapi.json` when the host provides no generator.
- Same guard as the rest of devtools: dev-only and loopback-only.
- Scalar's prebuilt bundle is vendored and served as `assets/scalar.js`, so apps install nothing extra. The page fetches nothing from a CDN, and Scalar's web fonts, telemetry, AI agent and MCP are turned off.
- Swagger UI's prebuilt bundle (swagger-ui-dist, Apache-2.0) is vendored too, served as `assets/swagger-ui-bundle.js` and `assets/swagger-ui.css`; its schema validator badge is off, so it fetches nothing from outside either.
- The API tab links `OpenAPI JSON` (`/__warlock/api/openapi.json`) and `Postman collection` (`/__warlock/api/postman.json`, built by core's `getDevelopmentPostmanCollection()`; `503` when core cannot build one) for importing the routes into Postman or Insomnia.
- To write a file instead, run `warlock generate.openapi` (default `storage/openapi/openapi.json`).

## Options

`warlock dev` uses the defaults: path `/__warlock`, the last 200 requests
kept, and an N+1 threshold of 5. Everything lives in memory and is gone on
restart.

## From the terminal (agents)

`npx warlock trace POST /posts --body '{"title":"Hi"}' --json` sends one
request to the running dev server and prints this dashboard's record of it as
JSON — middleware, validation result, queries with N+1 flags, logs, response
and timings. See the `warlock-trace` skill of `@warlock.js/core`.

`npx warlock mcp` (or `npx warlock dev --mcp`) gives a coding agent the same
records through its `requests_recent` tool: the newest requests with their
phases, queries flagged `nPlusOne`, warnings, logs and timings. See the
`warlock-mcp` skill of `@warlock.js/core`.

## Secrets

Query bindings and log context go through the logger's redaction rules
before they're stored. The data is still real request data, which is exactly
why the dashboard is development-only and loopback-only.

## Related

- Building your own tooling on the same hooks: core `registerTracingHooks()`,
  cascade `dataSourceRegistry.on("query")`, core `mailEvents.onCaptured()` and
  the cache `invalidated` event are public APIs that also work without devtools.

## Process supervision panel

Run `npx warlock add process` to create an app-owned supervisor and
`src/app/processes/devtools.ts`, exporting `processPanel = { list: () =>
processes.list() }`. Devtools discovers this registration only in development.
The **Processes** tab refreshes `GET /__warlock/api/processes`: PIDs, workload
categories, labels, display commands, limits, enforcement, and peak memory.
It excludes ownership tokens. Without registration the list is empty. The
endpoint retains development/loopback guards and provides no stop action.
Use the `supervise-processes` skill of `@warlock.js/process` for launch,
recovery and stop APIs; configure one owner/registry per application instance.

# Warlock Sitemap — full skills

> Package: `@warlock.js/sitemap`

> Generated artifact. Concatenates every SKILL.md and reference file under `@warlock.js/sitemap/skills/`. Re-run `node scripts/generate-llms.mjs` after any change.

## sitemap-overview  `@warlock.js/sitemap/sitemap-overview/SKILL.md`

---
name: sitemap-overview
description: "Front-door orientation for `@warlock.js/sitemap`: framework-blind `Sitemap` and streaming `SitemapIndex` builders, URL metadata, hreflang, Google image entries, sharding, diagnostics, and atomic publication. Use when adding or debugging sitemap output; Warlock page discovery and `/sitemap.xml` routing belong to `@warlock.js/web`."
---

# `@warlock.js/sitemap` — overview

A sitemap builder that knows nothing about any framework. Entries in, a valid
sitemaps.org document out. **Zero runtime dependencies.** Generation only; no
remote sitemap parser.

## It does not import Warlock

There is no connector, no config module, no lifecycle and no page registry in
this package. It owns the sitemap PROTOCOL and every byte it emits, and
nothing else. `@warlock.js/web` is a CALLER of it, exactly like an Express app
or a cron script is — which is what makes the same three lines work everywhere.

If you are looking for page discovery, `sitemap: false` exclusion, locale
expansion, the `/sitemap.xml` route or `robots.txt`, those belong to
`@warlock.js/web`, not here.

## The whole common case

```ts
import { Sitemap } from "@warlock.js/sitemap";

const sitemap = new Sitemap({
  baseUrl: "https://example.com",
  changefreq: "weekly",
  priority: 0.5,
});

sitemap.add({ path: "/" });

declare const posts: { slug: string; updatedAt: Date }[];

for (const post of posts) {
  sitemap.add({
    name: "post-details",
    route: "/posts/:id",
    path: `/posts/${post.slug}`,
    lastmod: post.updatedAt,
    priority: 0.8,
  });
}

const xml = sitemap.toXML();

await sitemap.saveTo("public/sitemap.xml");
```

## `baseUrl` is validated in the CONSTRUCTOR

A `Sitemap` that cannot produce a valid URL should not exist. Anything that is
not an absolute `http(s)` URL throws `InvalidBaseUrlError` at construction, so
a typo surfaces at the line that wrote it rather than at the first request.
`new URL()` accepts `mailto:` and `file:` happily, so the protocol is checked
explicitly.

This replaces the 5.15.0 config key, its `PUBLIC_APP_URL` env fallback and its
boot refusal entirely: the origin is an argument now, so it cannot be missing.

## The entry

Only `path` is required, and it must be a **concrete path** — `/posts/123`,
never `/posts/:id`. A pattern is not a URL.

| Field        | Meaning                                                                       |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `path`       | Required. Resolved against `baseUrl`; an absolute URL is used as given.       |
| `name`       | Optional route label, for your own diagnostics. Never serialised.             |
| `route`      | Optional pattern this URL came from. Feeds `routes()` and `duplicates()`.     |
| `lastmod`    | `Date` → W3C datetime. A string is passed through UNTOUCHED, never re-parsed. |
| `changefreq` | One of the seven protocol values; anything else throws.                       |
| `priority`   | `0.0`–`1.0`; anything else throws.                                            |
| `alternates` | `{ hreflang, path }[]` — language versions of this page.                      |
| `images`     | `{ loc }[]` — absolute HTTP(S) image URLs, including verified external CDNs.  |

Invalid entries throw `InvalidSitemapEntryError` from `add()`. Paths are
normalised to carry a leading slash, so `a` and `/a` are ONE entry.

## Duplicates: silent, but not hidden

Entries are stored keyed by `path`. Adding the same path twice keeps the later
one, silently — a duplicate `<loc>` makes the document invalid, and two loops
legitimately covering an overlapping set is the normal cause.

`duplicates()` reports every collision with its count and the `route` of each
contributing add, so a caller who cares can fail their own build:

```ts
sitemap.duplicates();
// [ { path: "/posts/1", count: 2, routes: ["/posts/:id", "/:slug"] } ]
```

## `routes()` and why `declareRoute()` exists

```ts
sitemap.declareRoute("/products/:slug");

sitemap.routes();
// [ { route: "/posts/:id", count: 400 }, { route: "/products/:slug", count: 0 } ]
```

**The zero is the interesting row.** It means a route you expected to
contribute URLs contributed none, and a whole section of the site is missing
from a document that otherwise looks perfect.

Without `declareRoute()` a route only becomes known by appearing on an entry,
so every route has at least one URL, `count: 0` can never occur and the
diagnostic is decorative. Declaring the pattern is what turns a silent loss
into a visible one.

**This package reports; it never prints.** Whether a zero is a warning or a
build failure is the caller's decision.

## Alternates

`alternates` emits `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` inside each
`<url>`. Two rules:

1. **Every language version is also its own `<url>`, carrying the complete
   alternate set including itself.** Listing alternates on only one of them is
   the usual way this ships broken.
2. **The package does not know what a locale is.** `hreflang` is any string —
   `en`, `en-GB`, `x-default` — and it never derives `/{locale}/…` for you.
   Each path is supplied explicitly, which is the only thing that works when
   slugs diverge between languages.

The `xhtml` namespace is declared only when something uses it. `SitemapIndex`
applies the same rule PER SHARD — a shard declares `xmlns:xhtml` only when its
own entries carry alternates — and an alternate's `<xhtml:link>` bytes count
toward that shard's byte ceiling exactly like the rest of its `<url>` block.

## Images

Use `images` when a page has image assets to expose:

```ts
sitemap.add({
  path: "/products/widget",
  images: [{ loc: "https://cdn.example.com/widget.jpg" }],
});
```

Each image `loc` must be an absolute HTTP(S) URL. The builder emits Google's
`<image:image><image:loc>…</image:loc></image:image>` extension and declares
`xmlns:image="http://www.google.com/schemas/sitemap-image/1.1"` only in
documents that need it. An external CDN URL is valid when that host is verified
for the site.

Google permits at most 1,000 images for one `<url>`. Extra images are dropped.
Pass `onImageLimitExceeded({ route, dropped })` in `SitemapOptions` to receive
the one diagnostic for that route; without it, the builder issues one
`console.warn` per route. Image XML and its namespace count toward the shard byte
ceiling.

## `toXML()` is pure, repeatable and synchronous

Calling it twice returns the same string; it mutates nothing and drains
nothing. It has no I/O and stays synchronous.

## The ceiling

The protocol caps one file at **50,000 URLs or 50MB uncompressed**. `Sitemap`
retains every entry — that is what makes `entries()` and a repeatable
`toXML()` possible — so it is right up to that ceiling and wrong above it. A
site past it needs the streaming writer, which retains nothing and emits shards
plus an index.

`maxBytesPerFile` is enforced at shard boundaries, not within an entry: a
single entry too large for the ceiling is written alone in its own shard
rather than split — an entry can't be split.

For `SitemapIndex`, `shardPathPrefix` changes the URL directory used for shard
links in the index without changing where `saveTo(outDir)` writes those files.
Use it when a proxy serves generated shards from a different public path.

## `SitemapIndex.saveTo(outDir)` owns the whole directory

It publishes atomically by swapping `outDir` for a freshly written temp
directory in one `rename` — which means `outDir` must be a directory
dedicated to this sitemap set, never an app's `public/` or anything else
something else writes to. Every publish marks `outDir` with
`.sitemap-set.json`; a later call only swaps a directory that is absent,
empty, or already carries that marker. A non-empty, unmarked `outDir` gets
`UnownedOutputDirectoryError` instead, and is left completely untouched.

## Errors

| Error                         | When                                                                                                                                  |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `InvalidBaseUrlError`         | `baseUrl` missing, relative, or not `http(s)`. From the constructor.                                                                  |
| `InvalidSitemapEntryError`    | No path, priority outside `0.0`–`1.0`, unknown `changefreq`, invalid `Date`, alternate with no `hreflang`. From `add()`.              |
| `UnownedOutputDirectoryError` | `SitemapIndex.saveTo(outDir)`: `outDir` is non-empty with no `.sitemap-set.json` marker. From `saveTo()`, before anything is written. |

## Also exported

`buildSitemapXml(entries, baseUrl)`, `escapeXml(value)`, `joinOrigin(origin,
path)`, `SitemapImage`, and `SitemapImageLimitExceeded` — the pieces the class
is built from, for a caller who wants the serialiser or image diagnostics
without the builder.
